Implemented Model","sectionText":"## 3. Implemented Model

Current canonical authoring sources:

```txt
core/skills/
domains/<domain>/skills/
```

Current generated or assembled distribution targets:

```txt
.agents/skills/ (assembled portable projection)
.claude/skills/ (generated thin wrappers for canonical skills; hand-authored skills preserved)
plugins/fgOS/skills/ (mirrored fgos-* dev skills and _shared/; hand-authored plugin skills preserved)
.gemini/extensions/fgos/ (prototype extension package generator; partial/planned)
```

Current build/proof surfaces:

| Surface | Status | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Assemble canonical skills from `core/skills` and `domains/*/skills` into `.agents/skills` | implemented | `src/setup/skill-wrappers.mjs`, `scripts/build-skill-wrappers.mjs`, `test/setup/skill-wrappers.test.mjs` |
| Generate Claude wrapper skills from `.agents/skills` | implemented | `src/setup/skill-wrappers.mjs`, `test/setup/skill-wrappers.test.mjs` |
| Mirror `fgos-*` dev skills into the fgOS plugin for plugin-only consumers | implemented | `plugins/fgOS/skills/`, `test/skills/fgos-mirror.test.mjs` |
| Detect missing/stale plugin skill packaging through doctor/fix registry | implemented | `src/setup/registrations.mjs`, `test/skills/fgos-mirror.test.mjs`  **Status note (2026-10-14):** The retained implementation claim overstates doctor/fix coverage: `plugin-dev-skills-packaged` detects missing files only (`src/setup/registrations.mjs:3251-3276`); byte drift is checked by `test/skills/fgos-mirror.test.mjs:137`, and this check has no registered repair. |
| Generate Gemini CLI extension package layout and commands | partial | `src/setup/skill-wrappers.mjs` (`generateGeminiSkillPackage`), `test/setup/skill-wrappers.test.mjs` |

Generated targets are not the source of truth. They may be committed for host compatibility, but edits should flow from the canonical source through the generator. Note that host trees may be mixed: `plugins/fgOS/skills/` contains hand-authored user commands (`pick`, `submit`, `cook`, `list`, etc.) alongside mirrored `fgos-*` dev skills, and `.claude/skills/` preserves hand-authored skills (`ui-spec`, `gitnexus`) without treating them as generated wrappers.

Run `npm run build:skills` in the fgOS source repo after editing canonical skill sources. Every Markdown file written by assembly carries a one-line HTML generated-from header naming its repo-relative `core/skills/...` or `domains/<domain>/skills/...` source and that rebuild command. The header follows byte-identical YAML frontmatter, or is the first line when none exists. Host Adapter Targets","sectionText":"## 5. Host Adapter Targets

The target model is:

```txt
canonical skill source
  -> portable skill projection
  -> host adapter projections
```

| Host / consumer | Adapter target | Trigger shape | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Codex / OpenAI skills | `.agents/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` | `$fgos-...` or implicit selection by skill description | implemented for current canonical skills |
| Claude | `.claude/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` plus fgOS plugin wrappers/commands where needed | existing `/fgOS:<verb>` compatibility, target lowercase alias `/fgos:<verb>` where host allows | partial |
| Claude plugin-only consumer | `plugins/fgOS/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` | plugin-exposed command/skill surface | implemented for current `fgos-*` dev skills |
| Gemini CLI | extension package with `gemini-extension.json`, `GEMINI.md`, and `commands/fgos/<verb>.toml` | `/fgos:<verb>` via command directory namespace | partial (prototype generator only; release/doctor wiring planned) |

Claude, Gemini, and Codex are adapters. None of them should own the fgOS skill semantics.

Self-containment rule for the Gemini package (and any future installable extension): the package must run with the fgOS source repo absent. Every `commands/fgos/<verb>.toml` names only its packaged copy (`packaged_source = "skills/<skill>/SKILL.md"`) as the thing the host reads; the canonical directory it was rendered from is recorded in `provenance` as ledger metadata only, never as a runnable reference. Shared fragments ship inside the package under `skills/_shared/`. Generated adapter classification for `plugins/fgOS/skills/` follows the mirror's own write rule plus provenance (`_shared/` or `fgos-*` **and** a canonical/assembled source), so a hand-authored `plugins/fgOS/skills/fgos-custom/` with no source stays unmanaged."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-18","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-18","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-18","title":"Unheaded block 18","startLine":98,"endLine":104,"textDigest":"dbe2274ea5ac62da2b00557308d940f5b4f70538bcc1dddc0c5a7132b7ed4884","sample":"The target model is:

Trigger Vocabulary","sectionText":"## 6. Trigger Vocabulary

fgOS should keep a host-neutral intent id and map it to each host's native affordance.

Canonical intent id shape:

```txt
fgos:<verb>
fgos:<compound-verb>
```

Examples:

```txt
fgos:submit
fgos:pick
fgos:code-panel
fgos:architecture-panel
```

Adapter mapping:

| Intent id | Codex/OpenAI skill | Claude | Gemini | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fgos:code-panel` | `$fgos-code-panel` | `/fgos:code-panel` and compatibility `/fgOS:code-panel` if already shipped | `/fgos:code-panel` | deprecated (stubbed by Unit I29; superseded by `fgos:code-change`) |
| `fgos:code-change` | `$fgos-code-change` | `/fgos:code-change` | `/fgos:code-change` | deprecated (superseded by `fgos-run`, routing via canonical capability) |
| `fgos:architecture-panel` | `$fgos-architecture-panel` | `/fgos:architecture-panel` | `/fgos:architecture-panel` | implemented |
| `fgos:routing` | `$fgos-routing` | `/fgos:routing` | `/fgos:routing` | implemented |
| `fgos:pick` | `$fgos-routing` (alias) | `/fgos:pick` (compat `/fgOS:pick`) | `/fgos:pick` | partial (hand-authored plugin command; canonical public-intent mapping planned) |
| `fgos:submit` | `$fgos-clarifying` (target) | `/fgos:submit` (compat `/fgOS:submit`) | `/fgos:submit` | partial (hand-authored plugin command; canonical public-intent mapping planned) |

Direct 1:1 intent-to-trigger mapping is implemented for canonical skills whose intent matches their canonical name or frontmatter `intent:` / `public-intent:`. Compatibility mapping for legacy `/fgOS:*` commands where discovery does not yet produce explicit intent aliases (e.g. `fgos:pick` vs `fgos-routing`) is partial and tracked for subsequent instruction/routing phases.

The lowercase `fgos:*` vocabulary is the desired cross-host user surface where the host supports slash commands and auto-suggest. Projection Ledger Fit","sectionText":"## 10. Projection Ledger Fit

Skill distribution targets are host-visible projections. The long-term ledger should be able to answer:

- which runtime generated the projection;
- which canonical skill source produced it;

`docs/specs/distribution.md` currently describes the shipped baseline:

- Install is a GitHub-backed npm package install, commonly
  `npm install -g github:vantt/forgent#v0.1.0`.
- The package exposes two public binaries: `fgos` and `fgos-runner`.
- `package.json` defines the installable surface with `bin` and `files`.
- Install runs no lifecycle script; contributor hooks are manual.
- `setup` and `doctor` exist in the old public model. `setup` writes/fixes,
  plain `doctor` reports, and `doctor --fix` runs registered fixes.
- Doctor checks, doctor fixes, and config defaults are extensible registries,
  not a hardcoded closed list.
- Global config and project config coexist; project config wins.
- A dev checkout shell helper can resolve three tiers from one sourced shell
  function: dev checkout, project-local `node_modules/.bin`, then global
  install.
- The Claude Code plugin distribution is separate from the npm CLI package and
  must ship wrapper skills plus copied coding-domain dev-skills.

This baseline works as a Node/npm distribution story. It does not solve the
new project-local runtime identity problem, worktree runtime sharing, tracked
pin, activation, or Rust CLI release path."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-21","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-21","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-21","title":"Unheaded block 21","startLine":128,"endLine":128,"textDigest":"31211360c2d65c73cb9a4eb7ecc7beb88e965a78f3af11793f543bac65e60d84","sample":"`docs/specs/distribution.md` currently describes the shipped baseline:","identityFingerprint":"37ec69eba0487525f02575161cccd8ceaf3f020e44b03dd8c615caa2241dd185","ancestry":["History: Distribution Baseline","Retained Distribution Baseline Source Detail","Distribution Baseline And Scattered Spec Fragments","1. Old Design Pressure From `tsk-1fp`","sectionText":"#### 3. Old Design Pressure From `tsk-1fp`

The `tsk-1fp` family captured the earlier pending direction:

- Move away from a shared global npm location toward a git-hosted installer
  that vendors/copies fgOS into each project.
- Installer resolves target version, copies payload, writes a baseline ledger,
  and fails closed when payload is unsafe.
- Project-vendored fgOS owns version-specific init/doctor/config/schema
  knowledge.
- Existing project honors its pinned version unless an explicit upgrade path is
  invoked.
- Downgrade is refused unless forced and both versions are known.
- Drift is reportable from `fgos doctor`; repair should flow through
  installer/re-vendor path, not ad hoc patching release files.
- Parity gate fails closed when payload files/projections disagree on
  version/fingerprint.
- `docs/specs/distribution.md` entry points must be superseded explicitly once
  the generated-spec workflow is updated.

Current interpretation:

- `install.sh`/`install.ps1` as primary mechanism is superseded by `fgctl`.
- `setup --latest` vocabulary is superseded by `fgctl upgrade` plus local
  `fgos init` / `fgos doctor --fix`.
- "fingerprint ledger" is split into `ReleaseManifest`, `ActivationRecord`,
  `Pin`, `ProjectionLedger`, and later `MigrationJournal`."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-25","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-25","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-25","title":"Unheaded block 25","startLine":167,"endLine":167,"textDigest":"de5699f55d95e2c8a777b9f85f02974ae9d9858286e6d8a74a2477a774c7407c","sample":"The `tsk-1fp` family captured the earlier pending direction:","identityFingerprint":"286454c60873a47e3539e8e8f5364e51b8e01894136ed6c0b0ccb47fd6631f97","ancestry":["History: Distribution Baseline","Retained Distribution Baseline Source Detail","Distribution Baseline And Scattered Spec Fragments","3. Bảy trụ cột của tầm nhìn","sectionText":"## 2. Bảy trụ cột của tầm nhìn

1. **Cài đặt không cần clone.** Người dùng lấy được `fgos`/`fgos-runner` mà
   không cần tự tay `git clone` repo nguồn trước.
2. **Hai cấp cài đặt: global hoặc project.** Cả hai cấp đều là cách cài hợp
   lệ, không cấp nào là "chính", cấp nào là "phụ".
3. **`setup`/`doctor` luôn tự sửa được mọi thứ cần để fgOS chạy tốt** —
   upgrade/update bản đã cài, init mới, VÀ fix mọi hạ tầng cần thiết + merge
   cấu hình mới vào cấu hình đã có + điền cấu hình còn thiếu. Không dừng ở
   "báo cáo rồi im" — phải tự sửa được, không chỉ chẩn đoán.
4. **Setup/config phải mở được cho module mới.** Bất kỳ chức năng/module mới
   nào cũng có đường chính thức để đăng ký thêm năng lực cấu hình của nó vào
   `setup`/`doctor` tổng — không phải mỗi module tự vá tay một chỗ riêng.
5. **Mọi thay đổi mới đều phải tự hỏi: có đụng cấu hình/config không? có cần
   hạ tầng đặc biệt nào cần setup hỗ trợ không?** Đây là một câu hỏi bắt buộc
   cho MỌI công việc trong project này, không riêng việc thuộc mảng
   cài đặt — xem §5 (gate áp dụng toàn project).
6. **Global và project không xung đột.** fgOS luôn nhận biết (aware) được cả
   hai cấp đang tồn tại; nếu project có cài fgOS riêng thì bộ ở project được
   ưu tiên vận hành, không có thì rơi về global; **cấu hình của project luôn
   ghi đè (overwrite) cấu hình global** — không phải hợp nhất mù hai bên.
   **Cập nhật 2026-08-01:** còn một CONTEXT THỨ 3 nằm ngoài cặp global/project
   — dev-checkout self-hosting (contributor phát triển CHÍNH fgOS qua
   `scripts/fgos-shell-integration.sh`, không cài đặt gì). Ba context này
   phải cùng "không xung đột" trên một máy, không chỉ hai. Xem §3 cho phát
   hiện thật (đọc code) về va chạm cụ thể giữa context này với global-install.
7. **CI/GitHub CI workflow là một phần của bộ setup.** CI giúp fgOS ổn định +
   sẵn sàng ngay khi cài, giảm bớt việc phải tự dò các ràng buộc môi trường
   ngay tại máy người dùng — kiểm trước ở CI thay vì để người dùng tự đụng."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-6","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-6","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-6","title":"Unheaded block 6","startLine":50,"endLine":76,"textDigest":"6a8d7e629b0c2c751e982db8a8790f1a19a0ab377523ea5c903e72608c9895ac","sample":"1. **Cài đặt không cần clone.** Người dùng lấy được `fgos`/`fgos-runner` mà

- **RUL11 (distribution.md) nói `fgos doctor --fix` chưa tồn tại, là
  "Deferred Idea có chủ đích", không phải gap.** Trụ cột 3 ở trên **đảo
  quyết định này** — chủ sản phẩm giờ muốn `doctor`/`setup` tự fix, không
  còn hoãn. Khi mảng này được thi công thật, RUL11 phải được sửa/supersede
  trong distribution.md (không sửa tại chỗ mà không ghi rõ lý do đảo).
- **Data Dictionary #7 (distribution.md)** liệt kê đúng 3 check cố định
  (`node-and-git`, `shell-integration-sourced`, `config-not-stale`) trong
  `src/setup/checks.mjs`. Trụ cột 4 đòi hỏi danh sách này trở thành
  **mở-rộng-được** (registry mà module khác tự thêm entry), không còn là
  literal 3 dòng cố định.
- **Trụ cột 6 (global vs project, không xung đột, project ghi đè global)**

Rewrite `docs/specs/distribution.md` into `docs/platform/packaging-distribution/spec.md`.

The new spec should be BA/state-oriented:

- user-visible install/setup/doctor behavior;
- supported install channels;
- global/project/dev checkout precedence;
- setup/doctor rules;
- package/plugin distribution facts;
- compatibility guarantees;

The coordinator/user has settled the Node fallback posture: Rust host is the
default runtime path for activated workspace installs; legacy Node fallback is
deprecated immediately and may remain only as an explicit escape hatch with a
warning/log/proof marker during a short compatibility window. The escape hatch
must not silently catch Rust-host failures. The escape hatch is supported for
30 calendar days after the preview release publication date. Public preview tag
`v0.1.0` was published on 2026-09-18, so the earliest removal date for this
preview release is 2026-10-18 unless a later release decision replaces the
support promise.

Public/default release posture means the official stance for users outside the
source checkout: which release channel is published or recommended, which
installed `fgos` entrypoint is documented as the default, and what
compatibility/rollback promise applies to that channel. It is broader than the
P6/P7 local proof that an activated workspace path enters the Rust host.

The installed/default runtime claim is now implemented for preview public
posture: external-installed/default `fgos` enters the Rust host, and fallback
follows the explicit deprecated Node escape-hatch policy. The first published
preview release proof is `v0.1.0`, published by release workflow `35317876419`
with `fgctl`, `fgos`, `SHA256SUMS`, and `install.sh` assets; post-release CI
run `35498322149` passed, including external-consumer proof. The evidence is
recorded in `verification/install-and-release-proof.md`.

The code-panel track still does not decide these product/release questions:

- whether this preview posture graduates to stable/default release;
- whether stable graduation changes the fallback promise before 2026-10-18.

| Entry point | Status | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `install.sh` | Implemented | Installs `fgctl` from release assets into a machine-local install directory. |
| `install.ps1` | Implemented preview | The Windows counterpart of `install.sh` (PowerShell 5.1 or later, no administrator rights, no `PATH` change): installs `fgctl.exe` for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` with the same `FGCTL_VERSION` / `FGCTL_INSTALL_DIR` / `FGCTL_ASSET_BASE_URL` / `FGCTL_TARGET` semantics and a mandatory `SHA256SUMS` check (rule RUL16 (Windows is a native release target: same assets, an installer and launchers that need no POSIX shell) in `docs/specs/distribution.md`). |
| `fgctl init` | Implemented preview | Initializes a project/workspace from a release chosen by `--from` > `FGCTL_FROM` > `FGCTL_VERSION` > the committed pin > the latest GitHub release; a downloaded asset is checksum-verified against `SHA256SUMS` before staging (rule RUL15 (fgctl init downloads a checksum-verified release when no source is given) in `docs/specs/distribution.md`). |
| `fgos` launcher | Implemented preview | One `fgos` (`fgos.cmd` on Windows) written next to `fgctl` by `fgos doctor --fix` (which `fgctl init` runs): it walks up to the nearest `.fgos/installation/bin/fgos` and runs it, so each project runs its own activated release with no absolute path and no rc edit. A different `fgos` found first on `PATH` is reported, never overwritten. See distribution spec RUL17 (one fgos on PATH runs each project's own activated fgos). |
| `fgctl upgrade` | Implemented preview | Moves a workspace activation to a new release chosen by `--from` > `FGCTL_FROM` > `FGCTL_VERSION` > the latest GitHub release (checksum-verified against `SHA256SUMS` when downloaded), records the previous release for rollback, and updates `.fgos/distribution.json` (including `releaseVersion` when downloaded). |
| `fgctl repair` | Implemented preview | Repairs a workspace installation under the selected release model; current preview proof covers repair after activation. |
| `.fgos/installation/bin/fgos` | Implemented preview | Stable workspace command surface after activation; current preview proof reports `host: "rust"` and the activated `artifactDigest`. |
| `.fgos/installation/bin/fgos.cmd`, `fgos-runner.cmd` | Implemented preview | The same stable surface for PowerShell and `cmd.exe`, written by `fgctl init`/`repair` next to the `sh` pair and needing no POSIX shell; `fgctl verify` reports a missing or edited launcher and `fgctl repair` regenerates it. |
| `npm install -g github:vantt/forgent` | Implemented legacy deprecated | Installs the legacy Node `fgos` and `fgos-runner` entry points; explicit deprecated escape hatch during the compatibility window, not the public/default posture. |
| `scripts/fgos-shell-integration.sh` | Implemented | Contributor/dev helper that resolves fgOS command tiers from shell functions. |
| local `fgos init` | Partial target | Adopts/materializes workspace state after `fgctl` publishes a ready activation. |
| `fgos doctor` | Implemented | Reports environment checks without writing by default. |
| `fgos doctor --fix` | Implemented | Runs registered fixes and then reports checks. |
| `fgos setup` | Implemented deprecated legacy compatibility | Wires local development support and runs registered environment repairs in the current Node CLI; command surfaces point workspace onboarding to `fgctl init` plus local `fgos doctor --fix`/`fgos doctor`, while shell/global integration remains compatibility behavior through the 30-day preview fallback window unless a later release decision replaces it. |"},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-4","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-4","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-4","title":"Unheaded block 4","startLine":36,"endLine":51,"textDigest":"fd8f41577cf07e6e6713f2a48792d88071e7fa072e87b32c08ec0be373173c6c","sample":"| Entry point | Status | Purpose |

The README recommends the release install script:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vantt/forgent/main/install.sh | sh
```

This installs `fgctl`, then the user initializes a project with:

```bash
fgctl init
```

With no pin and no explicit source, `fgctl init` downloads the latest release through the system `curl` and refuses unless the asset matches its `SHA256SUMS` entry. `FGCTL_VERSION=<tag>` selects an exact tag (pre-releases are never "latest"); `FGCTL_FROM=<path | URL>` or `--from` installs a non-release build. `install.sh` itself defaults to the latest release and takes `FGCTL_VERSION` the same way."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-6","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-6","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-6","title":"Unheaded block 6","startLine":59,"endLine":59,"textDigest":"975fdac85c2ee1cc78b299368b9e24ae2841c000e44dc16d2034a3d208e5cab3","sample":"The README recommends the release install script:","identityFingerprint":"c874e8bdd5f0b6bd195623da43de0699888e6c5f37b7a514eba4d7ef7c856dbc","ancestry":["Spec: Packaging-Distribution","3.1 Recommended Native Channel"],"text":"The README recommends the release install script:"},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-7","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-7","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-7","title":"Unheaded block 7","startLine":61,"endLine":63,"textDigest":"d71195e5c17af66db9dca719904ffb3ad90e36b8d6818d27a6e5716e5b090b5d","sample":"```bash

On Windows 10 and later, from a plain PowerShell session (no Git Bash, no WSL, no administrator rights):

```powershell
irm https://github.com/vantt/forgent/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex
fgctl init
```

`install.ps1` installs `fgctl.exe` into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\fgos\bin` (or `FGCTL_INSTALL_DIR`) and prints, without running, the commands that put that directory on `PATH`. Like `install.sh` it takes the latest NON-prerelease unless `FGCTL_VERSION` names a tag, so a pre-release such as `v0.2.0-rc.2` needs `FGCTL_VERSION`. `fgctl init` then downloads the `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` asset through the `curl.exe` that ships with Windows, verifies it against `SHA256SUMS`, and writes the workspace launchers: `.fgos/installation/bin/fgos.cmd` and `fgos-runner.cmd` for PowerShell and `cmd.exe`, beside the `sh` pair for Git Bash. A release publishes the same asset set for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` (built on `ubuntu-22.04`, with a CI gate that its binaries need no glibc newer than 2.35) and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`; macOS is not published. The full rule is RUL16 (Windows is a native release target: same assets, an installer and launchers that need no POSIX shell) in `docs/specs/distribution.md`.

The target runtime selection rule is:

```txt
workspace installation > dev checkout > project-local install > global install

Release Tree","sectionText":"## 5. Release Tree

The native release tree contains:

```txt
bin/fgos
bin/fgos-runner
libexec/legacy-node/
manifest.json
```

The release tree builder refuses unsafe payload shapes such as source entries escaping the checkout, symlinks in release payloads, and non-empty arbitrary output directories. In Git checkouts the shared source walker selects tracked and non-ignored untracked files, so ignored setup output never enters the payload; unpacked tarballs retain filesystem selection. This changes a release digest once when the previous builder included ignored output. The manifest carries `artifactDigest`, computed from canonical manifest content rather than archive bytes.

The decision index unions committed rows with local state (state wins by scope and decision ID, otherwise scope and timestamp); generator and doctor share this computation. Until cross-machine event history is complete, explicit removal requires removing a row from both state and the committed index.

Repository, workspace, worker-capsule, release-store, and projection layout boundaries belong to `contracts/repository-runtime-layout.md`. Doctor, Fix, And Legacy Setup","sectionText":"## 6. Doctor, Fix, And Legacy Setup

The target architecture has no separate setup verb for workspace onboarding. One-command workspace onboarding is `fgctl init`; after publishing the ready workspace activation, `fgctl` invokes the active local runtime tail:

```txt
local fgos init
local fgos doctor --fix
local fgos doctor
```

Current legacy `fgos setup` remains implemented and deprecated in the Node CLI and still:

- wires shell/helper and hook support where applicable;
- fills missing config defaults without overwriting customized values;
- applies both project-local and global config default handling;
- runs every registered fix unconditionally, using the same fix registry as `doctor --fix`;
- reports what changed;
- exposes a deprecation path in command help, command manifest JSON, and setup result payloads.

`fgos doctor`:

- runs registered checks;
- does not write by default;
- reports pass/fail and what to do next.

`fgos doctor --fix`:

- runs every registered fix;
- then reports checks;
- uses named fix registrations rather than ad hoc command-specific repair logic.

Exact registry behavior and legacy setup compatibility belong to `contracts/setup-doctor-registry.md`."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-30","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-30","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-30","title":"Unheaded block 30","startLine":142,"endLine":142,"textDigest":"9c4fef3562b68911b09c98076aa84afad927dc0d538424d94fe6c8420dbccc8f","sample":"The target architecture has no separate setup verb for workspace onboarding. Plugin And Skill Packaging","sectionText":"## 8. Plugin And Skill Packaging

Skill packaging is a distribution concern when one canonical fgOS skill must be rendered into host-specific surfaces:

- `.agents/skills` for portable Codex/OpenAI skill projection;
- `.claude/skills` for Claude wrapper projection;
- `plugins/fgOS/skills` for plugin-only consumers;
- future Gemini extension packaging.

The canonical skill body belongs to the owning component or domain. Packaging-distribution owns only the generated/adapted host surfaces, install packaging, and stale/missing-target checks.

Current implementation assembles canonical skills from `core/skills` and `domains/*/skills`, generates `.agents/skills` and `.claude/skills`, and mirrors required `fgos-*` dev skills into the fgOS plugin. Mirror integrity is tested by `test/skills/fgos-mirror.test.mjs`; doctor/fix checks detect missing or stale plugin packaging surfaces.

Exact source-of-truth, host adapter, trigger vocabulary, and doctor/fix obligations belong to `contracts/skill-package-distribution.md`."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-39","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-39","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-39","title":"Unheaded block 39","startLine":188,"endLine":188,"textDigest":"312c9979ff28ff23ff865e42b770f86fb2b9a64c5de89fb36f337f408234836e","sample":"Skill packaging is a distribution concern when one canonical fgOS skill must be rendered into host-specific surfaces:","identityFingerprint":"4c7cafbc920fd18433b40a97a30a90835cd9406105fae0339078de653dacc980","ancestry":["Spec: Packaging-Distribution","8. Instruction Composition And Projection","sectionText":"## 9. Instruction Composition And Projection

Instruction packaging is a distribution concern when rules from platform, component, domain, workspace, command, or skill sources must become host-visible instructions. Composition and registry semantics belong to the Agent Context Engine; packaging-distribution owns discovery, installation, host rendering, projection health and repair (main RUL102 (Agent Context Engine owns instruction composition; distribution delivers it); see the boundary in `contracts/instruction-composition-and-projection.md`).

`AGENTS.md` is the primary portable projection when a host supports it. Host-specific files such as Claude or Gemini context files should be generated only for host syntax, plugin/extension behavior, command surfaces, or compatibility gaps.

The hard contract is merge policy, not Markdown rendering. Composition must resolve rule force, authority, specificity, valid override/refine relationships, and conflicts before rendering any projection.

Exact instruction unit fields, rule force, composition order, conflict rules, effective instruction set, and doctor/fix obligations belong to `contracts/instruction-composition-and-projection.md`."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-44","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-44","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-44","title":"Unheaded block 44","startLine":203,"endLine":203,"textDigest":"74168286346a1889a62eda268fde63f93add50f0f1899ca922a2a6a790bef705","sample":"Instruction packaging is a distribution concern when rules from platform, component, domain, workspace, command, or skill sources must become host-visible instructions. Authority for what YAML means: `docs/platform/yaml-document/spec.md`.

Boundary Rule","sectionText":"#### 3. Boundary Rule

Use this rule to decide whether a detail belongs in packaging/distribution:

```txt
If the detail affects which fgOS payload is selected, trusted, materialized,
started, repaired, upgraded, or allowed to mutate a project, it belongs in
packaging/distribution.
```

Use this rule to decide whether it belongs elsewhere:

```txt
If the detail assumes the correct local payload is already selected, then it
probably belongs in host invocation, runner, work-state, agent coordination,
domainization, or gateway architecture instead.
```

Examples:

- "Where is `.fgos/runtime/bin/fgos` installed?" belongs to distribution.
- "Which provider handles `work.pick` after the local payload is selected?"
  belongs to host invocation/provider routing.
- "Can shared gateway accept a remote chat command for a project?" belongs to
  gateway/host surface later. For now, distribution only records the boundary
  so local payload shape does not make that impossible.
- "How does shared gateway translate that command into this project's semantic
  verb?" belongs to Project Runtime Adapter, currently recorded under
  distribution because it affects package shape.
- "Which event schema version is valid for this project?" belongs to
  work-state semantically, but distribution must record which local payload
  owns that schema.
- "Where do generated `.agents/skills` files come from?" belongs to
  workshop materialization under distribution."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-65","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-65","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-65","title":"Unheaded block 65","startLine":342,"endLine":342,"textDigest":"0a60f4e2b6313ac8efb1e1923ff5e4010b74da93e88909aa00aa045b8e0a498d","sample":"Use this rule to decide whether a detail belongs in packaging/distribution:","identityFingerprint":"f8cff758a3f4e40c3ff43110936a9182a9fff138f8dca791cd87550695b9d56f","ancestry":["Spec: Packaging-Distribution","Retained Scope Map Source Detail","Packaging Distribution Scope Map","3. Activation Boundary","sectionText":"#### 5. Activation Boundary

The activation-boundary shape captured here was:

```txt
acquire artifact
  -> stage immutable release in shared release store
  -> verify release manifest
  -> prepare workspace with candidate runtime
  -> publish ready workspace activation binding atomically
  -> allow project-state mutation
```

No project workflow command should run from a payload that has not crossed the
activation boundary. `fgctl` owns acquisition, staging, verification,
workspace binding publication, repair, upgrade, rollback, and quarantine.
Local `fgos` owns project semantics only after this workspace has a ready
activation binding and the runtime is write-compatible with the selected
work-state root."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-75","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-75","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-75","title":"Unheaded block 75","startLine":415,"endLine":415,"textDigest":"99029fbd090749e3dd3c7abfb6f4767de2d1542b4d04952b908be8c8979841a0","sample":"The activation-boundary shape captured here was:","identityFingerprint":"8cf3b54533b055a947576484c2486408ea7f1909151155327f7ad0aeb9ba3f5a","ancestry":["Spec: Packaging-Distribution","Retained Scope Map Source Detail","Packaging Distribution Scope Map","5. - `npm install -g github:vantt/forgent` (run anywhere) → resolves and installs
  the `fgos` command globally from the forgent GitHub repository.
- After install, `fgos init` (run inside the target project) → on the npm
  channel it refuses (`git-addon-unavailable: addon not shipped on this
  channel: onboard this project with fgctl init`) and changes nothing: this
  channel ships no native Git addon and Git has one door, so a project is
  onboarded with `fgctl init`, whose activated release carries the addon. The
  init/doctrine/marker-detection behavior itself (owned by the coexistence
  area, see `docs/coexistence.md`) runs from that activated release.
- Sourcing the dev checkout's shell helper file from a contributor's own
  shell profile → makes `fgos` and `fgos-runner` available directly from any
  location inside a checkout of the forgent source repository itself
  (including a linked git worktree of it), with no separate install step.
- `fgos setup` (run anywhere) → deprecated legacy compatibility command;
  wires the shell helper's source line into every shell profile the caller
  actually has, and brings the local config file up to date with the current
  defaults. New workspace onboarding should use `fgctl init` (which
  downloads the latest release when `.fgos/distribution.json` is absent, RUL15 (fgctl init downloads a checksum-verified release when no source is given))
  plus local `fgos doctor --fix` and `fgos doctor`; `doctor --fix` runs only registered fixes, so the
  config defaults, hook wiring and Claude Code hook still come from one `fgos
  setup` in the project. Shell/global integration remains legacy setup
  compatibility until the compatibility-window decision retires it.

- **Blocked when:** the installer's machine cannot reach GitHub over the
  network, or does not have Node.js 18+ available.
- **What changes:** the installer's package manager (npm, pnpm, or yarn)
  resolves the forgent GitHub repository, packages it according to the
  distribution file allowlist, and installs both CLI entry points — `fgos`
  and `fgos-runner` — into the caller's chosen install location (global or
  project-local, per the installer's own install flags), both immediately
  executable. The install resolves against whatever ref the installer's own
  command names: a tagged release commit when the command names a tag
  (`README.md`'s recommended path,
  `docs/knowledge/how-to-cut-a-fgos-release-tag/cut-a-fgos-release-tag.md`),
  or the source repository's default branch when it doesn't (the
  bleeding-edge path README also documents) — preparing release metadata is
  scripted by `npm run release:prepare -- <tag>`, but tag-cutting itself stays
  a manual, repo-owner-judgment act (per tsk-jtb). Pushing a `v*` tag then
  triggers the release workflow that builds assets, verifies the external
  consumer path, and publishes the GitHub Release. The
  install runs
  no lifecycle script of its own — there is nothing for a package manager's
  build-script policy (e.g. pnpm's `allowBuilds`) to approve or block, so the
  install succeeds the same way regardless of which of the three package
  managers runs it (per str88-fgos-pnpm-lifecycle).
- **Side effects:** none beyond the local install; no registry account is
  created or touched, and nothing is published to the public npm registry.
- **Afterwards:** the installer has a working `fgos` command. The content
  they received is limited to the distribution file allowlist — the source
  repository's own internal data (its live event log, its own dogfood
  runner configuration, its test suite) is never part of what they receive.
  The installer also receives the end-user documentation subset (how-to
  guides, design-rationale docs, and the read-by-tag index) — every link the
  README's Documentation section points to resolves to a file that is
  actually present in what they installed; contributor/maintainer-only docs
  (decision records, area specs, the product backlog, platform foundations)
  are not part of the install and are not linked from that section — a
  reader who wants those clones the source repository instead."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-91","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-91","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-91","title":"Unheaded block 91","startLine":567,"endLine":601,"textDigest":"ddee3916eeb71a2e1df124e5b3b2737128f48fa21494c2720fd4284db23a9941","sample":"- **Blocked when:** the installer's machine cannot reach GitHub over the

- **RUL1 (distributed package never includes the source repo's own runtime data).** The distributed package never includes the source repository's own
  runtime data directory or its own dogfood runner configuration — install
  content is always limited to the distribution file allowlist.
- **RUL2 (distribution is a GitHub install, not an npm registry publish).** Distribution happens by installing directly from the GitHub
  repository, not by publishing to the public npm registry — no package
  rename and no registry publish credentials are involved.
- **RUL3 (install never changes init/doctrine/marker-detection behavior).** Installing fgos does not change init/doctrine/marker-detection
  behavior in any way — that behavior belongs entirely to the coexistence
  area and is unchanged by installation.
- **RUL4 (every README Documentation link resolves to a shipped file).** Every link in the README's Documentation section resolves to a
  file that is actually present in the distribution file allowlist — a link
  to content that isn't shipped is a defect, not an acceptable pointer to
  "clone the repo for more" (per str77-79-doc-gap-fixes / ea8b9a8d).
  Contributor/maintainer-only documentation (decision records, area specs,
  the product backlog, platform foundations) is intentionally excluded from
  both the allowlist and that section — it is out of scope for an installed
  end user, not an oversight.
- **RUL5 (dev checkout shell helper is never sourced automatically).** The dev checkout shell helper file is never sourced automatically
  by any install step or other mechanism in this repository — a contributor
  adding it to their own shell profile is always their own explicit,
  separate action.
- **RUL6 (install never runs a lifecycle script).** Installing (from any of npm, pnpm, or yarn) never runs a lifecycle
  script of its own — the contributor hooks setup is always a separate,
  manually-invoked command, never an automatic `prepare`/`postinstall` step
  (per str88-fgos-pnpm-lifecycle). This is what lets every package
  manager's own build-script approval policy stay out of the way entirely,
  rather than needing to be satisfied.
- **RUL7 (setup/doctor cover both bash and zsh).** `fgos setup` and `fgos doctor` both cover bash and zsh — neither
  shell is treated as a lesser case.
- **RUL8 (setup's config update never overwrites a customized setting).** `fgos setup`'s config update never overwrites a setting the
  caller already customized, at any nesting depth; array-valued settings
  are never partially merged, only added wholesale when entirely missing.
- **RUL9 (doctor's default path never writes anything).** `fgos doctor`'s default (no `--fix`) path never writes
  anything, under any circumstance, including when a check would
  otherwise need to create a file to check it — a missing config file is
  reported as missing, never created as a side effect of checking.
  `--fix` is the deliberate exception: it runs every registered fix
  (Data Dictionary #7b) before re-reporting checks — reversed from the
  original no-exceptions wording per `tsk-2qz`, which reverses this
  rule and RUL11 (doctor --fix exists and is real, runs every registered fix) together (`docs/history/doctor-fix-gate-bypass/
  CONTEXT.md`).
- **RUL10 (setup never asks for confirmation, acts then reports).** `fgos setup` never asks for confirmation before writing to a
  shell profile or the config file — it acts and then reports exactly what
  it changed. Every other verb, and both of these two without
  `--pretty`, still produce the same enveloped-JSON result shape as before
  this feature — `--pretty` only changes how that same result is displayed,
  never what it contains.
- **RUL11 (doctor --fix exists and is real, runs every registered fix).** `fgos doctor --fix` exists and is real: it runs every fix
  registered via `registerFix` (Data Dictionary #7b) against the current
  cwd before re-reporting checks, then returns the same checks shape as
  the no-flag path plus a `fixed` array. The fix list is a registry, not
  a fixed set — a module can register a new one the same way a check or
  config-default is registered, independent of either (per tsk-2cs). This
  supersedes the original v1 "does not exist yet, Deferred Idea" wording
  — `tsk-2qz` reverses that decision deliberately, per
  `docs/distribution-vision.md` §3's trụ cột 3.
- **RUL12 (setup also runs every registered fix, unconditionally).** Legacy `fgos setup` also runs every registered fix (the same
  `runFixes()` `doctor --fix` calls per RUL11 (doctor --fix exists and is real, runs every registered fix)), unconditionally and with no
  confirmation — consistent with RUL10 (setup never asks for confirmation, acts then reports)'s own act-then-report contract for
  this deprecated compatibility verb, not an exception to it. `setup`'s result gains a `fixed` array,
  the same per-entry `{id, changed, message}` shape RUL11 (doctor --fix exists and is real, runs every registered fix) already describes
  for `doctor --fix`'s own (per `tsk-5hi`,
  `docs/history/setup-runs-registered-fixes/CONTEXT.md`).

- **RUL13 (customer customization lives in one tracked workspace folder; fgOS reads it first and never writes it; specified 2026-10-07; the lookup, the same-tier rule and the doctor check are built (runner decision 0057), the `fgctl init` skeleton and README are not).** A customer project that wants its own agent definitions (persona, role, decision boundary) puts them in `fgos/agents/<name>.yaml` at its project root. It is not `.fgos/`: that folder is runner state, ignored by git (`/.fgos/*`), every merge that stages a change under it is refused (`fgos-write-rejected`), and a fresh worktree has it stripped (ADR0020 (the runner strips .fgos/ from every fresh worktree)). It is not `.agents/` either: that is generated skill output which `fgos setup` and `npm run build:skills` rewrite. The first scope is `agents/` only; `workflows/`, `task-specs/` and `skills/` follow the same layout when a customer needs them, not before.
  - Lookup, by name, first match wins: the workspace folder, then a domain or extension (`domains/<name>/agents/`), then the installed `core/agents`. A higher tier replaces the whole file of a lower one; fields are never merged. Two definitions of one name in the same tier are an error that `fgos doctor` reports, never a silent pick. This replaces the earlier rule that a name is unique across `core/agents` and every domain: a name is unique within a tier and a higher tier shadows a lower one.

A new platform is one row in `src/util/release-targets.mjs`, one in the Rust `host_target` table, one in each installer and one release-workflow matrix entry; macOS is not published.
  - **`install.ps1`.** Same contract as `install.sh`: `FGCTL_VERSION`, `FGCTL_INSTALL_DIR` (default `%LOCALAPPDATA%\fgos\bin`), `FGCTL_ASSET_BASE_URL` (http, https or `file://`), `FGCTL_TARGET`; the tarball's own `SHA256SUMS` entry must match or nothing is installed; a symlinked `fgctl.exe` is refused; every request is bounded by a timeout. It needs no administrator rights (an elevated session is refused unless `FGCTL_ALLOW_ROOT=1`, as `install.sh` refuses root), never changes `PATH`, and prints the commands that do. Like `install.sh`, with no `FGCTL_VERSION` it installs the latest NON-prerelease, so a pre-release needs `FGCTL_VERSION`.
  - **Workspace launchers.** `fgctl init` and `fgctl repair` write four launchers into `.fgos/installation/bin/`: the `sh` pair `fgos`, `fgos-runner` (Linux, macOS, Git Bash) and the batch pair `fgos.cmd`, `fgos-runner.cmd` (PowerShell, `cmd.exe`; no `sh` involved). Each reads `activation.json`, refuses with exit 3 unless `status` is `ready`, and runs the active release's entry. A directory on `PATH` holding them makes `fgos` resolve in PowerShell through `PATHEXT`. The post-activation tail (`init`, `doctor --fix`, `doctor`) runs the `.cmd` form on a Windows host. `fgctl verify` checks that the launchers its host needs (the `sh` pair everywhere, the batch pair too on Windows) exist and equal what this `fgctl` writes; a missing or edited one is reported with `run fgctl repair` and never quarantines the (intact) release.
  - **Proof.** Pushing a release tag builds both targets and runs a consumer proof on each, and only when both pass does the publish job run; publishing exists only in `release.yml`. The Windows proof (`scripts/ci-external-consumer.ps1`, under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7) installs `fgctl` with `install.ps1`, runs `fgctl init` against a local release server, runs the activated `fgos` from PowerShell and from `cmd.exe`, and checks that a tampered download is refused by both the installer and `fgctl init`.
  - **Not covered.** Windows ARM64 and macOS have no asset. The machine release store stays at `%USERPROFILE%\.local\state\fgos` (`FGOS_STATE_HOME` moves it); relocating it to `%LOCALAPPDATA%` is a separate decision.
- **RUL17 (one `fgos` on PATH runs each project's own activated fgos; `doctor --fix` provides it; 2026-10-13).** A release install puts only `fgctl` on PATH and `fgctl init` activates a release per project, so a plain `fgos` used to need an absolute path. `fgos doctor` check `project-fgos-launcher` and its registered fix own the answer, and `fgctl init` already ends by running `doctor --fix`:
  - The fix writes one small launcher named `fgos` (`fgos.cmd` on Windows) into the directory `fgctl` was found in on `PATH`. The launcher walks up from the working directory to the nearest `.fgos/installation/bin/fgos` and runs it with the same arguments, so each project runs the release it activated, from any subdirectory, in any shell, interactive or not; it edits no rc file. Outside a project it exits 127 and says to run `fgctl init`.
  - The launcher carries a marker line. The check reports `ready`, an out-of-date copy (rewritten by the fix), a foreign `fgos` found first on `PATH` (never overwritten; the check names it), no `fgos` with `fgctl` on `PATH` (the fix writes it), or neither on `PATH` (the check says to add the directory `fgctl` was installed into).
  - A source checkout keeps the sourced shell-integration script and needs no launcher; the check passes there.

- **2026-10-23 — Terminal setup loses a row and a fix.** The doctor row `terminal-config` is part of `terminal-control`, and the `terminal-dir` fix is gone: the allocation store creates `<stateRoot>/terminal` and everything under it with mode 0700 itself, so a repair that only recreated what the owner of the directory already creates was a second door. Source: `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md` §15 and the T2 arbitration `plans/reports/council-261023-0402-harden-t2-arbitration.md`.
- **2026-10-23 — Every YAML parse goes through the native door (RUL108 (every YAML parse goes through the native door: one Rust parser behind src/util/yaml.mjs); supersedes RUL101 (fgOS has no npm runtime dependency; every YAML parse goes through one vendored js-yaml 5.4.3 behind src/util/yaml.mjs)).** Before this, a vendored, hash-pinned js-yaml 5.4.3 bundle was the Node parser because a bare checkout had no `npm install`, while the Rust side already read YAML through `fgos-yaml-doc`: two authorities for what YAML means. Decision: the one-door rule of RUL101 (every YAML parse goes through one vendored js-yaml) stays and the implementation behind the door becomes Rust, as the YAML Document spec (section 10) signed on 2026-10-22 says. `src/util/third-party/js-yaml.mjs` and its hash test are deleted in the same change; the upgrade-procedure paragraph of RUL101 (every YAML parse goes through one vendored js-yaml) no longer applies (the parser's own record is `packages/yaml-doc/upgrade-record.md`, RUL107 (a third-party crate under a component contract is pinned exactly with an upgrade record and acceptance tests)). Consequence, stated plainly: a process that cannot load the addon (a bare checkout without a staged addon, a channel that does not ship it) fails every YAML read with the door's named error; scripts that read YAML from a checkout stage the addon first (`ensureAddonForScript`), and a focused `node --test` needs the staged environment `npm test` builds. Evidence: the 136 golden cases of `packages/yaml-doc/contracts/fixtures/parse.v1.json` (every case of the old Node test lives there); a parity run of the old door against the new over 1414 tracked YAML and frontmatter documents found 1396 equal, 18 rejected by both, 0 different; `test/util/yaml.test.mjs` is the one Node wiring proof. Rejected: keeping js-yaml beside the crate (two authorities), a JSON projection plus a spawned process (owner 2026-10-22: 3 to 40 ms per call against 12 microseconds). Reversal condition: if the addon cannot be loaded on a channel the product must support, the fix is to ship the addon there, never a JavaScript parser.

- **2026-10-23 — Third-party crates under a component contract are pinned exactly, with an upgrade record and acceptance tests (RUL107 (a third-party crate that a component's contract rests on is pinned exactly and has an upgrade record and acceptance tests)).** Before this, the YAML parser had a record and the validator crate was about to be the second case; the convention was in neither spec. Decision: the rule above. Evidence: `jsonschema` =0.60.0 reproduced three defects under the product's serde_json feature set that the default-feature evaluation did not show (an `unreachable!` on an out-of-range number, quadratic `pattern` compile time, wrong object comparison under `preserve_order`), each now guarded and covered by a test that fails when upstream fixes it (`packages/config/upgrade-record.md`, `packages/config/rust/tests/validator_acceptance.rs`). Rejected: an unwritten convention (the next crate's author would not know the bar).

- **2026-10-21 — The npm channel's `fgos init` points to `fgctl init`.** Before this, a project onboarded with `npm install -g github:vantt/forgent` plus `fgos init`; that route needs Git through the native addon, which only an activated release ships ("until M10" in the old message). Git keeps one door, so the npm channel gets no addon-less Git read path: in a project no `fgctl init` has activated, `fgos init` refuses with `git-addon-unavailable: addon not shipped on this channel: onboard this project with fgctl init` and writes nothing. `test/setup/doctor-fresh-run.test.mjs` and `test/install-packaging.test.mjs` prove that refusal; the doctor state of an onboarded project is proven by the `fgctl init` tests (real runtime tail).

- **2026-10-18 — Terminal-control enters setup and doctor.** `fgos setup` adds the `terminal` config section and creates `<stateRoot>/terminal` (0700); `fgos doctor` replaces `herdr-available` with `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations`. Reasons: the herdr check now asks the port what the driver can do instead of running `herdr --version` on its own (one door); the new settings must be visible to doctor with their source or they are guesses (L5). Prior art read: the `herdr-available` check and `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` diagnosis are kept inside `terminal-control`; `lock` is the precedent for a top-level section registered by a component. Decisions: (1) a missing herdr is a warning, not a failure, because direct mode does not use a terminal; (2) the doctor floor of 40x8 for `minCols`/`minRows` is the measured one from the measurement report; (3) the setting names reach the route and the failed-pane retention through `src/terminal-control/config.mjs`, so a value doctor accepts is the value a round uses; explicit values only are sent, the Rust core keeps its defaults.

- **2026-10-16 — The activation, install and observe locks join holder-lock.** `fgctl`'s activation lock, the machine install lock and the observe store lock become kernel locks at `<fgosDir>/locks/activation.lock`, `<stateRoot>/locks/install.lock` and `<fgosDir>/locks/observe.lock`; the observe lock waits 5 s with no TTL and writes the shard snapshot under the lock. Their legacy paths (`.fgos/installation/activation.lock`, `<stateRoot>/install.lock`, `.fgos/observe/.lock`) become tombstone directories. Windows `fgctl init|upgrade|repair` refused with `lock-driver-unavailable` until the Windows driver landed (2026-10-17, `docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md` §8.1). (The `lock-fences` check and fix that covered these rows were removed on 2026-10-22.) Details: RUL18 (startup reap only takes claims the runner itself made, never a human or session holder) above and `docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md` §15.

- **2026-10-16 — Holder-lock enters setup, doctor and the activation gate (RUL18 (`fgctl` activates a release only after the holder-lock semantics probe and the borrow vectors are green)).** The cold locks of the runner (gateway, runner, sessions, advance, reconcile, recovery, full-suite, provider account and state, dispatch cwd) move from pid/TTL files to kernel locks on open file descriptions (`docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md`). Owner decisions of 2026-10-16: a stop-everything cutover with fences instead of a two-protocol transition, so no marker and no protocol floor in the manifest; Windows reports `unsupported` for these locks rather than falling back to the old files; macOS runs the `flock` driver at once, gated at activation by the vectors and the probe. In this spec: six doctor checks (`lock-kernel-semantics`, `lock-borrow-vectors`, `lock-holders`, `lock-fences`, `lock-predecessor-kill-wait`, `state-root`; three remain since 2026-10-22) and the `lock-fences` fix replace `provider-capacity-lock-stale`, whose ledger is no longer a mutex; `fgos setup` creates `<lockRoot>` and `<fgosDir>/locks` and registered the config key `lock.predecessorKillWaitMs` (removed on 2026-10-22; the wait is fixed at 2000 ms). Plan: `plans/261016-1104-holder-lock-kernel-lock-foundation/plan.md`.


- **2026-10-12 — `fgctl init` downloads by default (RUL15 (fgctl init downloads a checksum-verified release when no source is given)).** Before this, a plain `fgctl init` in a project with no pin failed with "`--from <source>` is required", so a first install meant downloading the release tarball by hand. Owner decision: no source and no pin means the latest GitHub release; `FGCTL_VERSION` selects an exact tag; `FGCTL_FROM` and `--from` select a non-release build; checksum verification is mandatory; the transport is the system `curl` rather than a new HTTP crate (same behavior and override as `install.sh`, no TLS stack to carry in `fgctl`). Prior art: `fgctl init --from` (the release-asset door, kept unchanged and now equivalent to `FGCTL_FROM`), `install.sh`'s `FGCTL_VERSION`/`FGCTL_ASSET_BASE_URL`/`FGCTL_TARGET` (reused, not redefined). Same day, follow-up: the pin now records the tag, so a pinned workspace whose release is not staged on this machine downloads it instead of needing a source; only a digest-only legacy pin still needs `FGCTL_FROM`/`FGCTL_VERSION`/`--from`, because a digest names no download. Follow-up (2026-10-14): `fgctl upgrade` uses the same verified download pipeline (`--from` > `FGCTL_FROM` > `FGCTL_VERSION` > latest GitHub release) and records the downloaded tag in `.fgos/distribution.json`, so an upgraded project's pin keeps a downloadable `releaseVersion` for teammates instead of reverting to digest-only.
- **2026-10-13 — Windows is a native release target (RUL16 (Windows is a native release target: same assets, an installer and launchers that need no POSIX shell)).** Owner decision: the level is "native, complete" (PowerShell and `cmd.exe`, no Git Bash, no WSL), with `tar.gz` kept as the single archive format and macOS left out of scope. Prior art, reused: the Windows CI hardening track made the Rust workspace build and the release-tree staging work on Windows (the `fgos.exe` entry, colon-free release store directory names, drive-letter-safe archive validation), and an earlier change wrote `.cmd` launchers on Windows that ran the `sh` shims through a `sh` on `PATH`; that required Git for Windows, so it is replaced by launchers that read `activation.json` themselves. Missing before: a Windows release asset, `install.ps1`, a Windows consumer proof, and any check that the launchers exist. Also in this change: the Linux asset moves from `ubuntu-latest` (binaries then needed glibc 2.39 and printed a loader warning on Ubuntu 22.04, glibc 2.35) to `ubuntu-22.04`, with a CI gate on the glibc symbol versions.
- **2026-10-16 — fgOS has no npm runtime dependency; YAML is read through one vendored parser (RUL101 (fgOS has no npm runtime dependency; every YAML parse goes through one vendored js-yaml 5.4.3 behind src/util/yaml.mjs)).** **Superseded on 2026-10-23 by RUL108 (every YAML parse goes through the native door): the one-door rule stays, the parser behind the door is now the Rust crate, the vendored file, its hash test and the upgrade procedure below are gone; the text below is kept as history.** Before this, `yaml` was the one production dependency. An installed release carried it (the release builder stages declared production dependencies), but a checkout, linked worktree or unpacked copy without `npm install` did not, so every module importing it failed to load there, and the doctor and setup paths grew their own YAML readers and "not evaluated" branches to keep loading. Decision: `package.json#dependencies` stays empty; the only YAML parser is `src/util/third-party/js-yaml.mjs`, the ESM bundle from the js-yaml 5.4.3 tarball, unmodified except a header and the dropped source-map comment line, and every parse goes through `src/util/yaml.mjs` (`parseYaml(text, { filename })`: zero documents give `null`, more than one throws, `maxAliases` 100, js-yaml's default core schema). An architecture test fails on any other import of `yaml`, `js-yaml` or the third-party file. Rejected: keeping `yaml` and making doctor tolerate its absence (what the workarounds did, and the cause of the divergence); a hand-rolled parser (a second authority for what YAML means); `vendor/` or `dist/` as the location (the repository's scout-block hook refuses those path segments, so agents could not read or review the file); 5.4.2 (a block-indentation mis-parse fixed in 5.4.3) and 5.5.0 (one day old at the time). Readers that used to skip silently now report a parse failure as a named problem with file, line and column; pinned persona text that the strict parser rejects renders through a private legacy projection so older runs resume with the same text (its removal is tracked in the backlog). Evidence: commits `8ef1baf1c` (door and vendored file), `838b044e5` (call sites), `b75c01a3f` (release and dev-host staging), `6013ca389` (dependency dropped), `f96eece77`, `b7eeb4bb6` and `26b3338a7` (readers use the parser), `f705b9c8c` (doctor checks `compiled.json`); a parity run of the old parser against the door over every tracked YAML and frontmatter document found 828 documents, 0 differences, 13 rejected by both; a cold `fgos` start costs 2 to 3 ms more (97 to 99 ms for `version`, 109 to 110 ms for `dispatch decide`); the full suite ran 7850 tests with 0 failures with release binaries present; `test/util/yaml.test.mjs` pins the vendored bytes by hash. Kept on their own paths: `src/report/frontmatter.mjs` pairs `parseFrontmatter` with `renderFrontmatter` over a deliberately flat schema, so replacing only the parser would make the pair asymmetric; `distill.mjs` carries a minimal YAML reader because portable skills ship without `src/`; `domains/*/compiled.json` stays a generated projection because parsing domain YAML at import would put every verb, hook and `doctor` at the mercy of one YAML typo (doctor now checks its freshness instead). Upgrade procedure: in an empty scratch directory run `npm pack js-yaml@<version> --ignore-scripts`; compare the tarball's sha512 with `npm view js-yaml@<version> dist.integrity`; extract the `.mjs` bundle from the tarball without executing anything in it (build the path so the hook-refused segment does not appear in the command); confirm it has no import or require; diff it against the current bundle and read every changed line; re-run the parity comparison against the previous parser over the tracked YAML; replace the third-party file with the new bundle under a fresh header (source, version, integrity, license, hash); update the hash constant in `test/util/yaml.test.mjs`. js-yaml advisories are watched through the backlog, since `npm audit` no longer covers the file.
- **2026-10-17 — Instruction composition belongs to the Agent Context Engine; packaging-distribution delivers (RUL102 (one owner for composing agent instructions: the Agent Context Engine composes and selects rules, packaging-distribution only discovers, installs, renders per host and repairs)).** Before this, two documents gave the same authority to two components: `docs/platform/packaging-distribution/contracts/instruction-composition-and-projection.md` §2 named packaging-distribution owner of the composition engine and registry shape, while `docs/platform/proposals/documentation-system-unification.md` §4.7.2-4.7.3 put the Instruction Composer in the Agent Context Engine and said packaging-distribution "does not decide semantic composition". Left as is, a future Agent Context Engine would be built beside `src/setup/instruction-composition.mjs`, giving two composers and two orderings of the same rules. Owner decision: composing and selecting rules (kind order, override, conflict, per-task selection, per-host budget, progressive disclosure) has one owner, the Agent Context Engine; packaging-distribution keeps delivery (source discovery and install, per-host render adapters, projection ledger, doctor repair). Two delivery moments follow: static delivery, where packaging-distribution asks the engine for each host's effective set when sources change or at setup/install/upgrade and renders it to files; and per-task delivery, where the runner asks the engine for a context packet that goes into the worker brief, with no file written. The engine knows no host or file. Rejected: packaging-distribution keeping composition and also absorbing budgets and per-task selection (it would grow a content-deciding role inside an install/delivery component). Weight guard: no new component now; the existing code in `src/setup/instruction-registry.mjs` and `src/setup/instruction-composition.mjs` is the engine's seed and moves to its own module only when the first budget/tiering slice lands, in the same change, never kept in two places. Prior art, reused: the Windows CI hardening track made the Rust workspace build and the release-tree staging work on Windows (the `fgos.exe` entry, colon-free release store directory names, drive-letter-safe archive validation), and an earlier change wrote `.cmd` launchers on Windows that ran the `sh` shims through a `sh` on `PATH`; that required Git for Windows, so it is replaced by launchers that read `activation.json` themselves. Missing before: a Windows release asset, `install.ps1`, a Windows consumer proof, and any check that the launchers exist. Also in this change: the Linux asset moves from `ubuntu-latest` (binaries then needed glibc 2.39 and printed a loader warning on Ubuntu 22.04, glibc 2.35) to `ubuntu-22.04`, with a CI gate on the glibc symbol versions.
- **2026-10-16 — fgOS has no npm runtime dependency; YAML is read through one vendored parser (RUL101 (fgOS has no npm runtime dependency; every YAML parse goes through one vendored js-yaml 5.4.3 behind src/util/yaml.mjs)).** **Superseded on 2026-10-23 by RUL108 (every YAML parse goes through the native door): the one-door rule stays, the parser behind the door is now the Rust crate, the vendored file, its hash test and the upgrade procedure below are gone; the text below is kept as history.** Before this, `yaml` was the one production dependency. An installed release carried it (the release builder stages declared production dependencies), but a checkout, linked worktree or unpacked copy without `npm install` did not, so every module importing it failed to load there, and the doctor and setup paths grew their own YAML readers and "not evaluated" branches to keep loading. Decision: `package.json#dependencies` stays empty; the only YAML parser is `src/util/third-party/js-yaml.mjs`, the ESM bundle from the js-yaml 5.4.3 tarball, unmodified except a header and the dropped source-map comment line, and every parse goes through `src/util/yaml.mjs` (`parseYaml(text, { filename })`: zero documents give `null`, more than one throws, `maxAliases` 100, js-yaml's default core schema). An architecture test fails on any other import of `yaml`, `js-yaml` or the third-party file. Rejected: keeping `yaml` and making doctor tolerate its absence (what the workarounds did, and the cause of the divergence); a hand-rolled parser (a second authority for what YAML means); `vendor/` or `dist/` as the location (the repository's scout-block hook refuses those path segments, so agents could not read or review the file); 5.4.2 (a block-indentation mis-parse fixed in 5.4.3) and 5.5.0 (one day old at the time). Readers that used to skip silently now report a parse failure as a named problem with file, line and column; pinned persona text that the strict parser rejects renders through a private legacy projection so older runs resume with the same text (its removal is tracked in the backlog). Evidence: commits `8ef1baf1c` (door and vendored file), `838b044e5` (call sites), `b75c01a3f` (release and dev-host staging), `6013ca389` (dependency dropped), `f96eece77`, `b7eeb4bb6` and `26b3338a7` (readers use the parser), `f705b9c8c` (doctor checks `compiled.json`); a parity run of the old parser against the door over every tracked YAML and frontmatter document found 828 documents, 0 differences, 13 rejected by both; a cold `fgos` start costs 2 to 3 ms more (97 to 99 ms for `version`, 109 to 110 ms for `dispatch decide`); the full suite ran 7850 tests with 0 failures with release binaries present; `test/util/yaml.test.mjs` pins the vendored bytes by hash. Kept on their own paths: `src/report/frontmatter.mjs` pairs `parseFrontmatter` with `renderFrontmatter` over a deliberately flat schema, so replacing only the parser would make the pair asymmetric; `distill.mjs` carries a minimal YAML reader because portable skills ship without `src/`; `domains/*/compiled.json` stays a generated projection because parsing domain YAML at import would put every verb, hook and `doctor` at the mercy of one YAML typo (doctor now checks its freshness instead). Upgrade procedure: in an empty scratch directory run `npm pack js-yaml@<version> --ignore-scripts`; compare the tarball's sha512 with `npm view js-yaml@<version> dist.integrity`; extract the `.mjs` bundle from the tarball without executing anything in it (build the path so the hook-refused segment does not appear in the command); confirm it has no import or require; diff it against the current bundle and read every changed line; re-run the parity comparison against the previous parser over the tracked YAML; replace the third-party file with the new bundle under a fresh header (source, version, integrity, license, hash); update the hash constant in `test/util/yaml.test.mjs`. js-yaml advisories are watched through the backlog, since `npm audit` no longer covers the file.
- **2026-10-17 — Instruction composition belongs to the Agent Context Engine; packaging-distribution delivers (RUL102 (one owner for composing agent instructions: the Agent Context Engine composes and selects rules, packaging-distribution only discovers, installs, renders per host and repairs)).** Before this, two documents gave the same authority to two components: `docs/platform/packaging-distribution/contracts/instruction-composition-and-projection.md` §2 named packaging-distribution owner of the composition engine and registry shape, while `docs/platform/proposals/documentation-system-unification.md` §4.7.2-4.7.3 put the Instruction Composer in the Agent Context Engine and said packaging-distribution "does not decide semantic composition". Left as is, a future Agent Context Engine would be built beside `src/setup/instruction-composition.mjs`, giving two composers and two orderings of the same rules. Owner decision: composing and selecting rules (kind order, override, conflict, per-task selection, per-host budget, progressive disclosure) has one owner, the Agent Context Engine; packaging-distribution keeps delivery (source discovery and install, per-host render adapters, projection ledger, doctor repair). Two delivery moments follow: static delivery, where packaging-distribution asks the engine for each host's effective set when sources change or at setup/install/upgrade and renders it to files; and per-task delivery, where the runner asks the engine for a context packet that goes into the worker brief, with no file written. The engine knows no host or file. Rejected: packaging-distribution keeping composition and also absorbing budgets and per-task selection (it would grow a content-deciding role inside an install/delivery component). Weight guard: no new component now; the existing code in `src/setup/instruction-registry.mjs` and `src/setup/instruction-composition.mjs` is the engine's seed and moves to its own module only when the first budget/tiering slice lands, in the same change, never kept in two places. - A package marked as not intended for public registry publication can still
  be installed directly from its GitHub repository — that restriction only
  blocks publishing to a public registry, not this installation path.
- Both CLI entry points (`fgos` and `fgos-runner`) are installed identically,
  executable immediately after install — a fresh install does not require
  the installer to separately locate or make executable the autonomous-loop
  runner command.
- Calling `fgos`/`fgos-runner` (via the dev checkout shell helper) from
  inside a linked git worktree of this repository always runs the MAIN
  checkout's entry point, never that worktree's own local copy — accepted
  as-is for this mechanism, not treated as a defect.
- A package manager whose own policy blocks lifecycle scripts for
  git-hosted dependencies (e.g. pnpm 10+'s `allowBuilds`) never blocks
  installing this package, because this package's install never declares a
  lifecycle script in the first place (per str88-fgos-pnpm-lifecycle) —
  there is nothing for that policy to approve or refuse.
- `fgos setup` run a second time with nothing new to do reports that
  plainly rather than silently repeating (or silently no-oping without
  saying so).
- `fgos doctor`'s `config-not-stale` check on a machine where `fgos setup`
  was never run reports "not configured yet", not an error and not a
  silently-created file.
- A release tree staged for `fgctl` (`scripts/build-rust-distribution.mjs`)
  carries the legacy-node payload TOGETHER WITH its production dependencies
  (the package's `dependencies` and theirs), copied next to the sources, so
  every verb runs from the installed release alone. Before this, the staged
  tree held no dependencies and any verb that loads one (`fgos workflow`,
  found when dogfooding a project that had run `fgctl init`) failed with a
  missing-package error while `fgos version` and `fgos doctor` still passed.
  A dependency that is not installed when the tree is built fails the build
  instead of thinning the payload; two installed copies of one name are
  refused. The external-consumer CI step runs a dependency-loading verb for
  this reason, because `version` never imports one.
- An agent in a project with no `bin/` (only the installed `fgos`) finds how
  to run anything from `fgos --help --json` and `fgos <verb> [<sub>] --help
  --json`. The host's route table carries two option selectors, `--help` and
  `-h`, generated from `HELP_SELECTORS` in `src/cli/command-registry.mjs`
  like every verb route and sent to the legacy-node payload, which owns the
  verb manifest; every other leading option still has no route and exits 4.

  sent to the payload too, so it prints its manifest entry instead of
  running. `fgos version` lists verbs only, never the two help selectors."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-105","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-105","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-105","title":"Unheaded block 105","startLine":762,"endLine":803,"textDigest":"b712c1644b8475d3e1625be217fc446174718933cddf4092f1da35b3125f59e7","sample":"- A package marked as not intended for public registry publication can still

Settled Node Fallback Policy","sectionText":"## 6. Settled Node Fallback Policy

Public/default release posture means the officially supported release stance
for users outside the source checkout: which release channel is published or
recommended, which installed `fgos` entrypoint is documented as the default,
and what compatibility/rollback promise the release owner makes for that
channel. It is broader than local proof that a workspace-installed path can
enter the Rust host.

The compatibility posture is now settled as:

- The public release posture is preview.
- External installs default `fgos` through the Rust host.
- Public docs may state that Rust host is the default installed runtime.
- Rust host is the default runtime path for activated workspace installs.
- Legacy Node fallback is deprecated immediately as a public/default runtime
  posture.
- Legacy Node fallback may remain only as an explicit escape hatch during a
  short compatibility window. It must require an intentional selector such as
  an environment variable, flag, or equivalent supported mechanism; it must not
  silently catch Rust-host failures.
- Any escape-hatch invocation must emit a warning, log entry, or proof marker
  that distinguishes deliberate legacy fallback use from default Rust-host use. **Status note (2026-10-14):** This marker remains an open requirement, not implemented for direct npm/Node compatibility invocation (`bin/fgos.mjs`, as checked in `review-4-packaging-truth-f6.md`, truth-sample-28). The invocation record is opt-in and emitted only through Rust-host legacy-cli routes (`apps/fgos/src/legacy_exec.rs:176-191`); it does not satisfy this obligation for direct Node entry.
- The escape hatch remains supported for 30 calendar days after the preview
  release publication date. The public preview tag `v0.1.0` was published on
  2026-09-18, so the earliest removal date for this preview release is
  2026-10-18 unless a later release decision replaces that support promise.

This policy does not mean every component has moved to Rust. It means the
user-facing default entrypoint is Rust-host-owned; the Rust host may still
execute the legacy Node payload through the release manifest while that payload
remains a component behind the host boundary.

If the Rust host fails, support/rollback guidance follows the explicit
deprecated Node fallback escape-hatch policy above. Silent fallback is not part
of the support promise."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-15","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-15","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-15","title":"Unheaded block 15","startLine":128,"endLine":133,"textDigest":"efc2d20524d1a1ea23cfbac8e8996cb51b880a0a86d29b98921dd863498b551a","sample":"Public/default release posture means the officially supported release stance

Removed `lock-fences` and `lock-predecessor-kill-wait` checks/fixes/config defaults are not current: predecessor wait is fixed at 2000 ms. The removed `capability-rigor-ceiling` and separate `state-root` diagnostics are not presented as current checks either (state-root resolution is now described by the kernel-semantics check). The current lock checks are `lock-kernel-semantics`, `lock-borrow-vectors` and `lock-holders`; terminal behavior has its independent registered checks below.

- implementing instruction composition or projection renderers;
- changing skill distribution layout;
- changing `fgctl`, release-store, activation, setup, doctor, or legacy setup behavior.

Mission Boundary","sectionText":"## 4. Mission Boundary

Packaging-distribution is not an installer side quest. It is a platform capability:

- it lets fgOS serve other projects;
- it reduces environment friction;
- it prevents invisible runtime drift;
- it gives maintainers a repair path;
- it lets reviewers verify install/runtime claims.

It should optimize for the project using fgOS, not only for convenience while developing fgOS itself."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-7","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-7","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-7","title":"Unheaded block 7","startLine":60,"endLine":60,"textDigest":"f0ee1c56bc29234b360a942c6f86794deb05ea4b0edabec0164aadaf52df5681","sample":"Packaging-distribution is not an installer side quest. ```txt
fgctl
  installs / stages / verifies / activates / upgrades / repairs runtime identity

workspace-local fgos
  runs workflow semantics under the selected runtime

doctor / doctor --fix
  reports or repairs readiness under the active runtime through shared registries

canonical instructions
  compose by authority/specificity before rendering to AGENTS.md or adapters

canonical skills
  live under component/domain authority and render into host adapters
```

**Luật.** Mọi mẩu dữ liệu bền của forgent phải được khai, ngay lúc thiết kế,
là một trong hai:

- **Log** — append-only, tổ chức theo *feature/phiên*, trả lời "làm sao tới
  đây"; không bao giờ overwrite. (vd: `plans/reports/`, decisions.jsonl,
  changeset)
- **State** — overwrite theo reality, tổ chức theo *area*, trả lời "đang ở
  đâu"; luôn phản ánh hiện tại. (vd: `docs/distillery/sources/*.md`, state.json)

Một artifact không khai được nó thuộc vật lý nào là lỗi thiết kế, không phải
chi tiết để sau.

**Nguồn.** `beegog:state-vs-log-two-physics` ("đa số hệ chỉ có log");
harness ngầm cùng mô hình (changesets=log, db=state). forgent đã theo pattern
này một cách ngầm (distillery=state, reports=log) — luật này chỉ phát biểu
thành văn. D-ID `ca7de3cf`.

**Hệ quả.** Review mọi thiết kế state layer bắt đầu bằng câu hỏi "log hay
state?"; file lai (vừa append vừa sửa) phải tách đôi.

**Ngưỡng xem lại.** Không có — đây là luật phân loại, không phải trade-off."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-15","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-15","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-15","title":"Unheaded block 15","startLine":115,"endLine":116,"textDigest":"168dd2e09c1b7d5d85e9ab1c366ad3e2765e68bf3d3991db2335d781272862d7","sample":"**Luật.** Mọi mẩu dữ liệu bền của forgent phải được khai, ngay lúc thiết kế,
