- **RUL101 (the per-worktree dispatch lock is a kernel lock held through holder-lock; a dead holder releases at once, 2026-10-16).** The lock a dispatch takes on its working directory (`dispatch-cwd`, rank 30, kind `lease`, scope still `fgosDir`) is a kernel lock on an open file description, acquired through the holder-lock facade (`src/holder-lock/`, authority `docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md`), with the cwd keyed by `dev:ino` after `realpath`. The lock file is `<fgosDir>/locks/dispatch-cwd--<dev>-<ino>.lock`, so one directory reached through a symlink is one lock; a cwd that does not exist fails as `worker-spawn-fail` before any lock. There is no holder record, no `ttlMs`, no heartbeat renewal and no reclaim by a contender: the kernel releases the lock when every process holding the description has died, so a holder killed without releasing, with or without a reused pid, blocks nobody; a live holder that is wedged keeps it until it exits. `sharedCwd` and `forceSharedCwd` still take no lock. A second dispatch on a held cwd fails `dispatch-in-flight` naming the holder pid. The resume guard of `fgos run --resume` and the reconcile planner read the kernel's holder list (`lockHolders`, which takes no lock) and fall back to `probe(dispatch-cwd)` (one non-blocking shared try) only where holders cannot be listed, since a shared try could make a concurrent one-try acquire see `held`; they refuse on a holder, neither judges a holder alive or dead, and a lock that cannot be read is never read as free. The legacy `.fgos/dispatch--<cwd>.lock` path is fenced by a tombstone at cutover for every worktree and claim, in both the `path.resolve` and the `realpath` form; `fgos dispatch reconcile clear-cwd-lock` only reports held or free and never clears a cwd lock. The reconcile planner's own local lock (`reconcile`, rank 80) is a kernel mutex at `<fgosDir>/locks/reconcile.lock` under the same port. Order inside one `LockScope` is enforced at acquire: a lock taken at a rank not above every rank the scope already holds throws `lock-order-violation` at once, with no trace-then-warn release.
- **RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool; one family has one executor; llmAccounts is read for checking only, 2026-10-17).** A cell of `runner.modelPolicies.<family>.<tier>` is a model, a model served by a named pool (`model@pool`), or a non-empty ordered list of those. The pool is the service provider that bills the call. A cell entry is split at its last `@`, so a model id that itself contains `@` names its pool explicitly (`claude-opus-4@20250514@vertex`); an entry without `@` is served by the pool named after the family. There is no default-pool key. A run uses the first entry served by the family's own pool (`resolveTierModel`); `resolveTierCandidates` returns every entry for `fgos dispatch explain` and doctor. An entry served by another pool is accepted and never run until the lease routes pools; a cell with no entry for the family's pool counts as a missing tier, which still falls back to the executor's own `model` or the CLI default. *(Superseded by RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool): every entry is a candidate of the walk, run when its pool can serve the invocation, and a family with no cell at the tier refuses `tier-cell-missing`; the `executor.model` and CLI-default fallthrough is deleted.)* The project config accepts every form. The global `~/.fgos/config.json` is read by every fgOS release on the machine, and an older release fails on a list and passes `model@pool` to the CLI as a model id, so a list or `@` cell there is dropped with a warning naming the cell (once per process), and doctor `global-model-policies-portable` fails on it.
  Each agent family (`providerModel`) is served by exactly one executor; its transports (headless cli, herdr pane, sandboxed or not) are invocations of that executor, and `bind()` picks the pane invocation inside herdr and a cli one outside, so a capability gets the same family and model in both places. Doctor `executor-family-unique` fails on a family with two agent executors.
  `runner.llmAccounts.<pool>.<account>` is the machine's account inventory, global-only: `credentialStore: { <cli>: <login directory> }` (`~`, `${HOME}` and `$HOME` expand), plus optional `label` and `disabled`. A pool name is the family name for the family's own vendor and the provider's name otherwise (`openrouter`); it may not contain `@` nor be another spelling of a configured family (`codex`, `openai-codex`, `glm`, `agy`). `readLlmAccounts` reports problems instead of throwing; `compareWithLegacyInventory` sets it against `runner.providers.<provider>.accounts` by the state key the lease uses (`openai` is `openai-codex` there). The lease, account pins and credential provisioning read a pool from `runner.llmAccounts` when it declares the pool, and from `runner.providers` for a pool it does not declare (the transition read, RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool)). Doctor: `llm-accounts-shape` fails on any reader problem, `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` warns on accounts or login directories that differ once `llmAccounts` is declared (the comparison stays needed while both inventories are read), `model-policy-pools` warns on a cell naming a pool `llmAccounts` does not declare (the walk skips such an entry), `tier-fallback` warns on a family `runner.tierFallback` lists that has no cell at that tier or no agent executor.
  `fgos dispatch explain --for <capability> [--rigor <r>]` binds the capability through `bind()` and reports the family and the `prefer` entry that chose it, the tier, its source (rigor, override) and its ceiling (RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling)), the candidates in walk order (each with the reason it is out: `tier-cell-missing`, `pool-unusable`), the walk a seat takes when each binding fails, the entries of the primary's cell (`used`, `fallback`, `unusable` with the reason), and the accounts of every pool on the walk in the order the lease takes them with whether the CLI can run on each. It leases, spawns and writes nothing.

- **RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling, 2026-10-17).** `runner.maxTier`, when set, is the highest tier a seat runs at, whatever asked for the tier: the unit's rigor, the capability's rigor floor, or an override (`--override '{"tier":...}'`). A capability that declares its own `rigor` in `runner.capabilities` raises the ceiling for its own seats to `rigorToTier[rigor]` when that tier is higher. The ceiling of a seat is therefore the higher of `runner.maxTier` and the tier of its capability's declared rigor (`resolveTierCeiling` in `bind.mjs`); a unit's rigor and an override stay under it, so only the config decides which capabilities may run above the cap, and a frontier override on a capability declaring `high` stops at `flagship`. Without `runner.maxTier` there is no ceiling. A capability cannot be held below the global cap this way. The binding records the ceiling on `provenance.tier.ceiling` as `{ value, source }`, `source` being `global` or `capability-rigor(<capability>, <rigor>)`; a clamped tier's source reads `clamped:maxTier(<tier>, <ceiling source>)`. `fgos dispatch explain` shows the ceiling, and doctor `capability-rigor-ceiling` lists the capabilities lifted above `runner.maxTier` with the tier and model they run at; it never fails. The assignment policy (`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`) raises the tier `bind()` hands it and applies no ceiling, so when `bind()` clamped, the policy's recorded tier can read higher than the tier that ran; the model is always the one `bind()` chose.

- **RUL104 (`fgos run --resume` after a controller death takes the settled attempt through adopt and never runs the agent twice; Ctrl-C cancels; 2026-10-18; owner decision 2026-10-16).** A unit whose controller died never continues on its own: it reads `unitState: awaiting-resume` (last attempt `closed`, no `unit-summary.json`, no live controller; shown by `dispatch inspect`, `dispatch show-run` and `fgos run --json`) and only an explicit `--resume` goes on. Resume asks adopt about the last attempt of every seat and round before anything else: `closed` with a result is the attempt's result and the unit carries on from it (commit `writes`, reviewer, next attempt, `unit-summary.json`), so the agent runs once; a `cancelled`, `abandoned-not-started` or `abandoned-before-brief` receipt is superseded, a new attempt runs the unit again and names the old one in `supersedesRunId` (set only on a new launch; the old attempt reads `superseded`); a `gate-lost` receipt (binding present, gate dead, no `gate-exit`) is not relaunched, a named limit: adopt cannot prove the agent never ran, so it fails closed (r6 §9.7) rather than risk running it twice, and the person starts a new `fgos run`; `running` and `being-adopted` are refused `attempt-still-running` (resume does not wait); `legacy-run` is refused `attempt-legacy-run` (doctor `legacy-attempts-stuck` settles it as `abandoned-legacy`, which is closed for the unit); a second concurrent `--resume` of the unit finds the controller seat (`unit-control` ledger) held by a live controller and is refused `resume-in-progress`. Resume never starts a second supervisor for an attempt that already has a binding or a receipt. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM publishes `cancel-requested.json` for every attempt the controller handed over, waits for their receipts for at most `dispatch.cancelWaitMs` (default `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs` + 5000, minimum 1000) and exits 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) after printing the resume command; a second signal exits at once. `fgos dispatch recover` over a supervised attempt recommends `adopt`; `outbox/result-N.json` is evidence for it, never a reason to park. Mechanism and tables: [run-supervisor spec, section 9.1](../../../run-supervisor/spec.md#91-controller-death).
- **RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads; the driver hands over exactly that store's files, 2026-10-19).** A confined `cli` invocation may declare `credentialStore: { use, homeEnv, files? }` in the config: `use` is the store key (`codex`, `pi`, `omp`, a lowercase key; it replaces the basename of `command` as the key into an account's `credentialSources`), `homeEnv` is the environment variable its CLI reads its login home from, and `files` (optional, non-empty, relative, no `..`, no repeats) lists what to hand over. The config door refuses a malformed store and a store on an invocation with no confinement backend (an unconfined invocation reads its store in place through `env`; that path is not redesigned). One function, `credentialStoreOf` (`provider-capacity.mjs`), reads it for every consumer; an invocation that declares none but binds `private-home` to an env variable (the machine-global config and other projects still carry that older form) gets `{ use: <basename of command>, homeEnv: <that variable> }`, and that inference is the only remaining reader of `resourceBindings`; it goes when those configs have moved. The confinement request carries `invocation.credentialStore` in place of the generic `resourceBindings` (the contract keeps its name `confinement-request.v1`; nothing outside the repo reads the field). The bwrap driver points `env[homeEnv]` at the private home (over a value the invocation's own `env` carries, which names the real store) and copies the files of the store: the invocation's `files`, else the leased account's list (`home-files`), else `auth.json` (`codex-home`). **The copy rule replaces "a missing file refuses the launch":** files that are present are copied, an absent one is left out, and a store with none present refuses the launch with `credential-provisioning` (`credential-store-empty`, naming the account, the store key and the home); a dangling link, a link out of the home, a non-regular file or a path with `..` still refuses, as before. **An invocation that declares no store gets no login and no home variable, whatever account was leased** (the lesson of `569f72d3b`, which copied a Codex login into every executor's home), and `assessBwrap` refuses a policy that grants no `private-home` to an invocation that reads a store. Trust seeding, write-back and refresh-ahead keep reading the leased account's store, now chosen by the store key. `dispatch explain` names the store of the bound invocation and whether it is declared or inferred; `fgos doctor` `confined-pane-accounts` (same id) covers every confined invocation that reads a store, notes absent files and fails only when none is present. In this repo's committed config the invocations of one CLI under one executor collapse into one (`pi-cli-bwrap`; the account is leased at launch), invocation ids no longer carry an account name (`codex-herdr`, `omp-herdr`, `omp-cli-bwrap`), and the OpenRouter key variable left the pi `env` because pi reads the key from the store's `auth.json` (measured 2026-10-19: with the key variables unset and only the three store files, pi answered). Not changed: leasing, quarantine, `llmAccounts`, the account inventory shape; the leased account is still chosen before the invocation is known, so an account that has no file of the store fails late (B1 filters accounts by store key before the lease), and the older fields stay in the committed config until the release that reads `credentialStore` is active.

A seat that leases an account (an out-of-process agent that is not a tool) needs the cell; an in-process, inline or tool seat needs none and binds with `pool: null`. **Primary.** The first binding follows `prefer` order exactly as before, with the soft family spread of the panel seats unchanged, so council seats keep leading with different families. **After a failure** the walk takes, in order: the failed family's remaining cell entries, then the families `runner.tierFallback.<tier>` lists, limited to the families `prefer` names (a list narrows and never widens); with no list for the tier, the rest of the `prefer` order after the failed candidate. A walk never leaves its tier. The soft spread stays active in a walk and ranks the passing candidates, ties falling to walk order; without a spread request the walk takes the first untried candidate. **`runner.tierFallback`** is `{ <tier>: [family, ...] }` with the tiers of `modelPolicies`, each a non-empty list of distinct family names (the `modelPolicies` key, so GLM is `z-ai`); `validateTierFallbackShape` refuses anything else at load naming the key path, `tierFallbackOf` reads it, and doctor `tier-fallback` warns on a listed family with no cell at that tier or no agent executor. The code enforces the tier boundary and the narrowing only; the owner's groups are configuration: doer tiers (nano, standard, advanced) fall back across gemini, deepseek, z-ai, then claude, openai; flagship and frontier across claude, openai, gemini and xai. An older release ignores the unknown runner key, so the lists go in the project config. **Walk state** is the seat's earlier bindings (`tried`, identity = executor, invocation, pool and model), rebuilt from the attempts in `unit.json` by `triedBindingsOf`; `excludePools` replaces `excludeFamilies`: a dead login excludes that pool, not the family's other pools (RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool) supersedes the walk of 0058 items 2 to 3 and 6, and the `candidateIndex` chain of 0051 item 1). A retry on another account of the same candidate is not a step of the walk. `walkStateOf` is the one door that turns a recorded attempt into those two `bind()` options; the write gate and doctor `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot` both recompute through it, so a fallback attempt (`<round>-fb<n>`) is checked against the walk it was bound in. The write gate compares executor, pool, tier and posture. A unit record written before bindings carried a pool has no walk state this code reads: its bindings are left out and the walk restarts at the primary. **A pool is usable** when the lease can serve it: a pool with accounts needs an enabled account holding a login store for the CLI the chosen invocation declares (`credentialStore.use`, RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)); a pool with no account in either inventory is usable only as the family-named pool (the executor's own login). An unusable entry is out of the candidates with `pool-unusable`, and `fgos dispatch explain` says why. **Missing cell.** An out-of-process agent seat whose family has no cell at the tier it runs at refuses `tier-cell-missing`: `no model for tier "<t>" under family "<f>" (runner.modelPolicies.<f>.<t>)`, one text built by `tierCellMissingDetail` for `bind()` and for the assignment policy (which raises `tier-cell-missing: <text>`). The older fallthrough to `executor.model` or the CLI default is deleted. When several `prefer` families exist, or in a walk, a family with no cell is skipped and recorded in `provenance.skipped`, and the refusal names the last skipped cell when nothing is left; a lone candidate refuses at once. **Lease, state and quarantine are per pool.** A seat bound to a pool leases from it: the state key is `legacyStateKey(pool)`, so the family-named pool keeps the key it always had (`openai` is `openai-codex`) and existing state, sticky records and quarantines still apply; a quarantine or fault on one pool does not touch another pool of the same family. The accounts of a pool come from `runner.llmAccounts.<pool>` when it declares the pool, else from `runner.providers.<provider>.accounts`: **the transition read** (`providerAccountInventory`), which goes, together with the `runner.providers` key, once every fgOS release on the machine reads `runner.llmAccounts` (the later step that deletes `runner.providers` from the global config). `compareWithLegacyInventory` and doctor `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` go with it. **Account order is the declared order.** `rankProviderAccounts` takes the account the assignment already holds while it is usable, else the pool's accounts in the key order of the config, skipping quarantined and `disabled` ones; load does not reorder, so the first account takes every lease until it cannot (least-lease and least-recently-used are deleted from the ranking; `lastSelectedAt` is still written for `inspect`). The lease receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store (the pinned invocation, else the executor's first `cli` invocation), and `inspectAccountRotation` counts the enabled accounts of the pool for rotation. **Pin.** `--account` and the `account` key of `--override` take `pool/account` (`parseAccountPin`); a bare id is refused with the form to write. - `fgos-runner --once` → chạy đúng một vòng: gặt-lại → tìm việc → giao việc theo MẺ (nhiều việc cùng lúc, giới hạn hai tầng) → chấm từng việc → ghi, rồi nạp lại mẻ kế tiếp — lặp tới khi không còn việc đang chạy VÀ không còn việc sẵn-sàng (xem "Giao việc theo mẻ, song song có giới hạn" dưới)
- `fgos-runner --dry-run` → in kế hoạch (việc nào sẽ chạy, model nào) mà không làm gì
- `fgos-runner --watch [--poll-ms <n>]` → chạy BỀN, không tự thoát khi frontier rỗng; lặp lại vòng đời `--once` mỗi lượt, phản ứng gần-tức-thời khi lượt vừa xong có ghi gì đó, nghỉ `--poll-ms` (mặc định 5000) khi lượt đó không ghi gì; dừng CHỈ qua SIGINT/SIGTERM tường minh — xem "Vòng cầm-giao bền (--watch)" dưới
- Khởi động MỌI vòng đều bắt đầu bằng bước **gặt-lại** (reap): giải quyết các claim runtime (hoặc item mang trạng thái bền `doing` di sản) từ lần chạy trước bị crash trước khi tìm việc mới — xem "Gặt-lại lúc khởi động" dưới
- Ngay sau gặt-lại, TRƯỚC khi tìm việc thi công: **quét nghiên-cứu** — giao worker thật cho mọi item ở stage `discovery`; xem "Quét nghiên-cứu trước dispatch" dưới
- Ngay sau quét nghiên-cứu, CÙNG TRƯỚC khi tìm việc thi công: **quét chia-việc** — mọi item ở stage `planning`, cộng tên stage di sản `decompose`; xem "Quét chia-việc trước dispatch" dưới
- `fgos take`/`fgos return` (cửa pull, ngoài vòng runner — xem spec Work-State "Cửa pull giao–nhận việc") claim/trả việc qua bản ghi runtime claim (mọi claim mới KHÔNG BAO GIỜ ghi bền giá trị `doing` — *new claims do not durably write into doing*) + CAS + goal-check runner tự dùng; gặt-lại lúc khởi động BỎ QUA claim đến từ cửa pull — xem "Gặt-lại lúc khởi động" dưới
- `fgos review <id>` / `fgos approve <id> [--timeout <ms>] [--acknowledge-iron-law]` / `fgos reject <id> --reason "..."` (ngoài vòng runner, gọi bởi người vận hành) — cổng duyệt PR nội bộ cho một đề xuất `awaiting-approval` đã sẵn, MỘT cổng cho cả nguồn runner lẫn pull-door; `approve` nguồn runner còn chạy phán Iron Law trước khi merge, nhưng CHỈ khi lần merge đó land lên trunk (self-improve loop STR13 Slice 3, ranh giới trunk per `0032`) — xem "Cổng duyệt PR nội bộ" dưới
- `fgos review <id> --github [--pr <n>]` / `fgos approve <id> --github --pr <n>` (ngoài vòng runner, gọi bởi người vận hành, tuỳ chọn — github-adapter) — vận chuyển thay thế của CÙNG cổng duyệt trên, đưa việc duyệt sang GitHub thay vì diff/merge cục bộ, chỉ áp dụng cho đề xuất nguồn runner; `review --github` kèm `--pr` là phép hỏi thăm trạng thái sống của một PR đã mở, không mở PR mới (github-adapter, phát hiện đóng-không-merge) — xem "Cổng duyệt qua GitHub" dưới
- `fgos catchup <id>` (ngoài vòng runner, gọi bởi người vận hành) — đồng bộ lại một việc đang đỗ (`blocked`) vì gãy nhập (xung đột, verify đỏ sau nhập, hoặc trôi tích hợp): kéo trạng thái mới nhất của đích vào nhánh riêng của việc rồi thử lại — xem "Đồng bộ lại một việc đỗ (catch-up)" dưới
- `fgos evolve`, `fgos evolve --pick` và `fgos evolve --submit` không còn là entry point hiện hành; module ranking cũ đã bị xoá.
- `fgos session start [--item <id>]` / `fgos session end <session-id> [--force]` / `fgos session list` / `fgos session gc` (ngoài vòng runner, gọi bởi người vận hành/một tác nhân) — vòng đời phiên checkout đa-phiên tùy chọn: một worktree detached-HEAD mỗi phiên cho cây nguồn, dùng chung MỘT kho `.fgos/` qua symlink; `end` từ chối một phiên đã rời commit khởi tạo trừ khi `--force`; `gc` dọn các mục sổ mồ côi (worktree đã mất khỏi git, hoặc pid của lệnh `start` một-lần đã chết), tha các phiên còn commit lửng hoặc còn thay đổi chưa commit — xem "Phiên checkout đa-phiên" dưới"},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-3","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-3","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-3","title":"Unheaded block 3","startLine":27,"endLine":38,"textDigest":"c3f6001d31e2991b5f3e4ded817bcd1dfc864294e6d80de5af051bba2b3ba53a","sample":"- `fgos-runner --once` → chạy đúng một vòng: gặt-lại → tìm việc → giao việc theo MẺ (nhiều việc cùng lúc, giới hạn hai tầng) → chấm từng việc → ghi, rồi nạp lại mẻ kế tiếp — lặp tớ","identityFingerprint":"57661178d511ed3eb51f5a120ab56109dd5630c2931e7d46985e05a524523ef1","ancestry":["Added in candidate: Runner Entry Points & Triggers","Entry Points & Triggers"],"text":"- `fgos-runner --once` → chạy đúng một vòng: gặt-lại → tìm việc → giao việc theo MẺ (nhiều việc cùng lúc, giới hạn hai tầng) → chấm từng việc → ghi, rồi nạp lại mẻ kế tiếp — lặp tới khi không còn việc đang chạy VÀ không còn việc sẵn-sàng (xem "Giao việc theo mẻ, song song có giới hạn" dưới)

- `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` — CLI (--once/--dry-run/--watch/--poll-ms — str7-str8-priority-intent; `--config` bỏ ở RUL93 (the runner loop's worker and the fan-out batch run as one Unit run each)), exit theo phạm trù; nhánh `--watch` đăng ký `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` lên một `AbortController` chung TRƯỚC khi gọi `runWatch`, tín hiệu thứ hai buộc `process.exit(130)`; hàm `printResult` (dùng chung giữa `--once` và `onCycle` của `--watch`) nay bọc `result` (trừ `exitCode`) qua `wrapEnvelope` (`src/state/envelope.mjs`, cùng hàm `bin/fgos.mjs` dùng) và in JSON một dòng — không `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` như `fgos.mjs` — vì `--watch` phát nhiều phong bì nối tiếp theo thời gian (per str46-io-contract, xem RUL61 (kết-cục cuối của `fgos-runner` nay bọc cùng phong bì máy-đọc `fgos.v1` như mọi verb)); exit-code prose ở đầu file trỏ về `src/state/store.mjs`'s `EXIT_CODES` + `src/runner/loop.mjs`'s `EXIT_BUSY` thay vì tự liệt lại bảng
- `src/runner/loop.mjs` — vòng + startup reap (SKIP claim `human`/`session` — xem "Gặt-lại lúc khởi động") + khoá liên-tiến-trình `.fgos/runner.lock` (busy exit 6); NGAY SAU reap, TRƯỚC vòng dispatch: (1) quét mọi item `stage==='discovery' && status==='todo'` (không đọc `item.mode`), dựng worktree tạm + `spawnWorker` với `stage: 'discovery'` cho từng item, đọc khối phán quyết trong output của worker rồi gọi `resolveDiscovery` (`src/intake/discovery.mjs`) với chính verdict đó, truyền `'runner'` — nhánh không có commit nào, hoặc không đọc được verdict, thì item được để nguyên tại chỗ cho lượt sau; (2) đọc lại view tươi rồi quét mọi item ở `stageForStep(domain,'Divide')` (`planning`) CỘNG tên di sản `decompose`, với `status==='todo'`, và gọi `resolvePlan` (`src/intake/plan.mjs`) cho từng item, cùng truyền `'runner'` — không kèm verdict, nên nó chỉ cho đi thẳng khi `plan.md` của item khai mode `tiny`/`small`, còn lại no-op an toàn; cùng lượt chạy có thể chaining cả hai sweep trên một item vừa rời `discovery`; ghi bản outcome dự đoán tại claim + thực tế ở cả hai lối ra cuối (thành đề xuất, hoặc đỗ/dừng) qua `addOutcome` của store; mọi `moveWork` runner tự gọi (claim/propose/park) truyền `role:'runner'`; gọi `runGoalCheck` (từ `goal-check.mjs`, không còn tự triển khai) cho cả proof lúc dispatch lẫn proof lúc gặt-lại; ngay trước khi spawn worker, đọc lại view TƯƠI qua `listWork(dir)` rồi truyền `feedback: {answer: view.gates?.[item.id]?.answer, reason: view.work?.[item.id]?.reason}` vào `spawnWorker` (per worker-execution STR33 / 396d9d9e, xem RUL23 (phản hồi người threading vào prompt worker)); `dispatch.mjs` — prompt/config/spawn (argv-only, spawnSync timeout; caveat grandchild SIGTERM ghi trong doc comment) + `resolveExecutorCommand`/`resolveTierModel` (dùng chung cho mọi lượt spawn worker, kể cả lượt dispatch nghiên-cứu — không còn call site nào cho một lời gọi model phán lồng bên trong engine); `buildPrompt(work, feedback?)` dựng 5 section cố định (Goal, Description, Worktree boundary, Expected proof, Constraints — hợp đồng test pin presence) cộng mục `# Human feedback` TÙY CHỌN khi `feedback.answer`/`feedback.reason` có mặt (nguyên văn, xem RUL23 (phản hồi người threading vào prompt worker)); `description` là `work.description` nguyên văn, degrade "(không có)" khi vắng (per discovery-context STR30); `spawnWorker(work, cfg, cwd, opts)` nhận `opts.feedback` truyền xuống `buildPrompt`; `worktree.mjs` — lifecycle + reclaimOrphanedCheckout + `detectTrunk(repoRoot)`/`isMainWorktree(repoRoot)` (dời từ `merge.mjs` sang đây per tsk-49i — cả hai là danh tính worktree/nhánh, không mang ngữ nghĩa nội dung merge; dời đi cũng cắt luôn import vòng `merge.mjs` ↔ `worktree.mjs`) + `createBranchRef(repoRoot, id, opts)` (tạo `fgw/<id>` chỉ-là-ref, không worktree, idempotent) + `createWorktree`'s `opts.baseRef` (fork worktree mới từ một ref chỉ định thay vì HEAD hiện tại — dùng cho con fork từ tip nhánh gốc); `recovery.mjs` — 8 lớp; `anti-loop.mjs` — `visitCount` (lifetime, dùng cho outcome/metric) + `visitsSinceLastHumanEvent(events, id)` (ngân sách CỔNG, per-item, reset trên `role==='human'` mang `answer` hoặc `reason`, xem RUL29 (cổng chống-lặp reset theo can thiệp người cuối cùng của chính việc)) + breaker; `loop.mjs`'s gate (cả nhánh dry-run đơn lẻ lẫn nhánh lọc `overLimit` của batch dispatch dưới) gọi `visitsSinceLastHumanEvent`, không còn `visitCount`, để quyết park; `createMissBreaker` nay PER-ITEM (Map theo id, `consecutiveMissesFor(itemId)`; `consecutiveMisses` getter cũ giữ nguyên qua một khóa sentinel tương thích ngược, per fan-out-parallel-5). `runOnce`'s vòng dispatch nay là pool-loop batch (cell fan-out-parallel-8): đọc TOÀN BỘ `readyWork(dir)`, lọc qua `root-affinity.mjs`'s `steerFrontier`, nhóm theo gốc và cắt còn tối đa `parallel.maxRoots × parallel.maxLeavesPerRoot` (đọc từ `.fgos/config.json`'s `runner` section, mặc định 4×4 khi vắng khối `parallel`), claim từng việc bên trong callback của `write-queue.mjs`'s `enqueue` (bắt buộc — giải-và-ghi phải cùng một giao dịch hàng đợi để giữ đúng chứng minh chống-tranh-giành), rồi dispatch cả mẻ đồng thời qua `Promise.allSettled`; mỗi việc claim xong xác định LEAF hay ROOT qua `state/frontier.mjs`'s `resolveRoot(view, id)` — leaf: `createBranchRef(repoRoot, rootId, {baseRef:'main'})` rồi `createWorktree(repoRoot, item.id, {worktreeDir, baseRef: branchNameFor(rootId)})`; root: `createWorktree` không đổi, tự nhiên tái dùng nhánh đã có nếu tồn tại. Mẻ xong → đọc lại `readyWork` tươi, lặp tới khi không còn việc đang chạy VÀ không còn việc sẵn-sàng; `runOnce` trả `{outcome, dispatched, parked, reap, exitCode}` thay vì kết quả một item
- `src/runner/loop.mjs`'s `parseDiscoveredBlocks(output)` + `captureDiscoveredWork(...)` — kênh báo việc-phát-hiện (xem "Báo việc-phát-hiện từ trợ lý" trên, RUL45 (báo việc-phát-hiện của trợ lý: đúng một lần mỗi lượt, fail-safe, có trần + chống trùng)): tách mọi khối lồng `fgos-discovered` (JSON, chỉ cần `title` khác rỗng) khỏi output đã thu của trợ lý, fail-safe (thân JSON hỏng/thiếu `title`/không phải object đều bị bỏ qua, không throw); gọi đúng MỘT LẦN trong `finally` bọc vòng thử lại của `dispatchClaimedItem`, tại kết cục cuối (không gọi lại giữa các lần thử nội bộ); mỗi khối hợp lệ đi qua `write-queue.mjs`'s `enqueue` (cùng cửa ghi tuần tự) — bên trong đó: cắt còn tối đa `DISCOVERY_CAP` (=20) khối trước khi lặp (phần dư log rồi bỏ), rồi với mỗi khối: quét view hiện hành tìm item có `discoveredFrom` khớp item đang thi công VÀ tên khớp sau khi chuẩn hoá (trim + hạ chữ) — khớp thì log rồi bỏ qua (không tạo); không khớp mới gọi `generateId`/`classify`/`addWork` (đóng dấu `discoveredFrom: item.id`, và stage vào-vòng của domain — `discovery` cho `coding`); `dispatch.mjs`'s văn bản prompt worker mô tả kênh khối lồng này cho trợ lý (nguyên tắc "chỉ báo, không tự ghi" — trợ lý vẫn không bao giờ được gọi `fgos`/đụng `.fgos/`); `sanitizeTitleForLog(title)` (S11, review-fix P3) — gộp khoảng trắng/xuống dòng + cắt 120 ký tự (kèm dấu `…` khi cắt), gọi tại đúng hai điểm `log` có nội suy `block.title` bên trong `captureDiscoveredWork`; KHÔNG áp dụng lên trường `title` truyền vào `addWork`
- `src/runner/goal-check.mjs` — hàm goal-check dùng chung DUY NHẤT (`runGoalCheck(item, cwd, timeoutMs)`): chạy `item.verify` qua shell tại `cwd`, phán chỉ bằng exit status — trích xuất từ `loop.mjs` (stage-decompose S2-pull) để cả vòng tự hành LẪN cửa pull `fgos return` (spec Work-State) gọi đúng một bản logic, không bao giờ hai bản song song
- `src/runner/frozen-judge.mjs` (STR63, domain layer thuần — không fs/git) — `FROZEN_JUDGE_PATTERNS` (bê nguyên từ frozen-judge của bee, bỏ mục `.bee/config.json` không áp dụng) + `frozenJudgeHits(changedFiles, footprint)`: chấm file đã đổi khớp nhóm nhạy cảm (test/CI/lockfile/manifest) NGOÀI `footprint` đã khai — khớp exact-path, không prefix/glob. `bin/fgos.mjs`'s `changedFilesSince(cwd, from, to)` (`git diff --name-only`, cạnh `commitsSince`) cấp input; gọi trong `return` khi `check.passed`, xem RUL60 (`return` mang thêm khuyến nghị frozen-judge — advisory, không bao giờ chặn)
- `src/intake/discovery.mjs` — xem Pointers spec Work-State (module dùng chung giữa runner và verb `discover`); verb `discover` (phiên sống) truyền `'session'`; verdict đủ rõ `moveStage` tới `planning` (bỏ qua `exploring`), verdict chưa đủ rõ `moveStage` tới `exploring` RỒI đậu `awaiting-human` mang câu hỏi (hai cửa ghi rời nhau — `stage` và `status` không giẫm nhau); một đề xuất `verify` còn phải qua một vòng kiểm cú pháp độc lập trước khi được ghi, bất đồng thì cũng đậu chờ người. `judgeDiscovery` (lời gọi phán lồng cũ) đã NGHỈ HƯU: engine luôn cần một verdict do người gọi đưa vào — worker của quét nghiên-cứu, hay phiên sống gọi `fgos discover --verdict` — thiếu verdict thì role `runner` no-op an toàn, role khác báo lỗi rõ ràng
- `src/intake/plan.mjs` (đổi tên từ `decompose.mjs`) — xem Pointers spec Work-State (module dùng chung giữa runner và verb `plan` khi item ở stage `planning`, hoặc còn ở tên di sản `decompose`); verb `plan` (phiên sống) truyền `'session'`; `resolvePlan` cũng là chỗ nhả claim `doing→todo` khi gốc sang `executing` (claim-lock §3b)
- `src/runner/prompt-templates/worker-prompt-discovery.txt` — mẫu prompt riêng của lượt dispatch nghiên-cứu, chọn bởi luật `{domain:'coding', stage:'discovery'}` trong `selectTemplate` (`src/runner/prompt-templates.mjs`); mọi lời gọi không truyền `stage` giữ nguyên hành vi cũ, không bị luật này chen trước. chưa chứa đích (exit 1) → `git merge --no-commit --no-ff <đích>` → xung đột thật → `git merge --abort` + giữ nguyên `blocked`; sạch → `runGoalCheck` trên cây đã stage TRƯỚC khi commit → đỏ → `git merge --abort` + giữ nguyên `blocked`; Writer tự acquire của checkpoint (`acquiringMainCheckoutWriter`) dùng `allowSelfRecognition: false` để không tái nhập hold của một operation khác cùng pid. Checkpoint `.fgos` (`runOpportunisticMainCheckoutChecks`) chạy trọn add → commit → reset-khi-lỗi trong mutex này: mutex thuộc tầng runner nên checkpoint (tầng kernel) nhận `mainCheckoutWriter` từ caller: caller đã giữ (claim, merge không slot) truyền `heldMainCheckoutWriter(pid)`, caller chỉ giữ merge slot truyền `acquiringMainCheckoutWriter(dir)` (acquire rồi nhả ngay, bị giữ thì bỏ lượt); không có writer thì checkpoint không commit. | Từ | Nghĩa |

| **role** | một trong năm: `producer`, `synthesizer`, `reviewer`, `red-team`, `judge`. `panelist` bị bỏ; panel = N ghế `producer` cộng một `synthesizer` |

**Seat Binding là authority duy nhất trả lời "ghế agent này chạy bằng executor, invocation, model, effort, tier và account nào, và nếu hỏng thì đi đâu", kèm lý do cho từng phần.** Không component nào khác tính tier, model, thứ tự executor, thứ tự account hay bước fallback cho ghế agent. Hàng Execution Core của [component-boundary.md](../component-boundary.md) (trước đợt: `bind.mjs` là authority đó) đã chuyển sang Seat Binding cùng đợt.

| Seat Binding sở hữu | Seat Binding không sở hữu |
|---|---|
| Tier, trần, thứ tự executor, cell và pool, thứ tự account, quyết định rotate-hay-next (walk), kiểm ghim và override, độc lập lúc chọn, lời giải thích | Danh sách ghế của Unit: pattern và `seats:` của workflow sinh ra; Seat Binding nhận qua một seat resolver (mục 7.1) |
| Trạng thái account như một port: lease, release, quarantine, lazy probe (adapter = `provider-capacity`) | Chạy agent, transport, confinement, copy login-store (Dispatch Transport and Confinement) |
| `explain` và `dry-bind` = cùng một hàm, chạy không giữ lease | Case admission, frame, trần seat-launch (Workflow; Seat Binding báo số launch đã dùng) |
| Từ vựng tier và định nghĩa ladder (một hằng, nguồn của `$comment`) | Nạp persona và các lớp của nó (`agent-definitions`; tên và đường dẫn do Convention) |
| | Capability do tool executor phục vụ |

- **Hai stage thuần trong crate Rust.** Stage 1 *policy*: (seat ask, config) → tier, trần, tập cell, executor theo thứ tự, effective rigor, ràng buộc; cache theo seat + digest config. Stage 2 *ranking*: (policy, peers, walk state, accountView) → một danh sách candidate xếp hạng gọi tên executor, invocation, model, effort, pool, account; chạy lại ở mỗi bước walk và mỗi `lease-conflict`.
- **Facade Node mỏng** gọi crate qua route nội bộ của Rust host, cùng kiểu Convention và Session Identity. Thiếu route thì fail closed; không có JS policy fallback.
- **Không exec host dưới provider lock.** Facade thu `accountView` ngoài `withProviderStateLock`, gọi crate, rồi mới acquire dưới lock. Trước Seat Binding ranking và `ranked[0]` chạy trong lock (`provider-capacity.mjs:623-636`).
- **Quyết định, acquire và replay là một authority.**
  - Mỗi attempt lưu một `bindingInput` có version (seat, role, posture, effective rigor, peers `independentOf`/`preferIndependentOf` lúc quyết, walk state, digest config, nguồn tier và trần, digest accountView) và một `leaseReceipt`.
  - Adapter acquire đúng account crate đã gọi tên, dưới lock hiện có, hoặc trả `lease-conflict`; runner rồi bind lại với view mới, cùng policy.
  - Cổng ghi replay giai đoạn 1 từ config đã commit ở digest của run (từ chối khi lệch) và chạy giai đoạn 2 không có trạng thái lease; receipt của lease được đối chiếu với record provider lúc settle, trước khi một lượt pass được commit; không đọc lại đồng hồ quarantine hôm nay. Câu trả lời sức khoẻ hiện tại của `explain` và doctor chỉ là tạm.
  - Giữ nguyên: ghim cứng; không retry đè lên ghi dở của ghế ghi (RUL92 (a writing seat is not rerun over its own partial writes)); quarantine và lazy probe; trần launch; ghim chạy-cả-run bỏ qua ghế nó không áp được.
- **Ngân sách exec.** Plan phải nêu và đo số host exec cho mỗi seat × round × bước walk, trên facade có sẵn (Session Identity hoặc Convention), với panel ba ghế một bước walk. |---|---|

| `{ "model": "...", "pool": "...", "effort": "..." }` | `pool` và `effort` tuỳ chọn |

- Một cell là model cộng effort tuỳ chọn. Collapse khai báo giữa hai tier liền kề được phép.
- `parseTierCell` (`tier-cell.mjs:25-40`, trước đợt từ chối mọi giá trị không phải chuỗi) nhận dạng object; cell chuỗi vẫn hợp lệ nên cell cũ migrate nguyên.
- Effort là một phần lời hứa của tier: vào `bindingIdentity`, snapshot binding và so sánh ở cổng ghi. Override không được hạ effort của cell (từ chối `effort-below-cell`); override bằng hoặc cao hơn thì nhận như hôm nay.
- Cell không effort chạy ở mức riêng của template invocation (template pi/omp ghi cứng `--thinking medium`); mức đó được ghi lại nhưng không phải lời hứa.
- Effort mà CLI thật của candidate không render được thì bỏ candidate; với ghim cứng thì từ chối `effort-unsupported`, kèm các mức CLI render được.
- Từ vựng effort đợt này là `REASONING_EFFORT_VALUES` = `low, medium, high, max` (`config.mjs:519`). Mở rộng (`xhigh`, `minimal`, `off`) và đổi tên model có effort trong tên (gemini `-low`/`-medium`/`-high`) đi cùng diff làm mới model riêng.
- Lối thoát inline-lead bị bỏ bất cứ khi nào candidate đã cấu hình bị chính sách hoặc nguồn cung loại: trước đợt `bind.mjs:500-514` giao ghế `producer` cho lead phiên với `model: 'default'`, `source: 'session-lead-inline'`, vượt mọi luật tier, cell và trần. Cho một ghế agent, theo thứ tự:

1. **Tier đã giải** = giá trị đầu tiên được khai theo danh sách (bảng đầy đủ ở mục 6.3):
   1. khoá seat của project: `cap.seats.<seat>`, rồi `prefix.seats.<seat>`;
   2. khoá persona của project: `cap.personas.<p>`, rồi `prefix.personas.<p>`;
   3. khoá role của project: `cap.roles.<role>`, rồi `prefix.roles.<role>`;
   4. `tier` của ghế trong workflow (khuyến nghị);
   5. mặc định capability của project: `cap.tier`, rồi `prefix.tier`;
   6. tier trong domain package (đợt sau; vắng đợt này);
   7. `defaults.tier`.
2. **Override.** Tier override cao hơn tier đã giải bị từ chối `tier-escalation-unauthorized` trong đợt đầu (mục 5.5). Override bằng hoặc thấp hơn thì nhận, ghi `tierSource: override`.
3. **Nguồn hiển thị.** Binding record, run evidence và `explain` mang `tierSource` (đường config chính xác, `workflow:<id>/<unit>/<seat>` hoặc `override`). Khi giá trị chọn khác khuyến nghị của workflow, chúng mang cả khuyến nghị, ví dụ `workflow recommends frontier, project config sets flagship (capabilities."architecture:shape".seats.system.tier)`.

- Mỗi ask và result mang `seat` (id duy nhất trong unit), `role` (một trong năm) và **posture** của pattern (`readOnly`, `forceOutOfProcess`, stance của thành viên panel).
- Binding, thư mục assignment, seat ledger, resume của panel và debate, ref handoff đều khoá theo `unitRun + seat + round + attempt`. Trước đợt khoá theo role (`role-ledger.mjs:20-34`), nên ba ghế `producer` sập thành một ô.
- Một seat resolver sinh danh sách ghế cho thực thi, mô phỏng, doctor và đếm launch của admission. Nó kiểm id ghế duy nhất và bội số role của pattern.
- Thành phần:
  - `solo`: một ghế `producer` trừ khi khai khác.
  - `reviewed`: ghế `producer` cộng một **ghế checker** mỗi tên từ `checkersByRigor[effectiveRigor]` ∪ `minCheckers` (và `red-team` cho capability `code:*`), id ghế = tên ghế checker trừ khi khai. Ghế checker là `reviewer`, `red-team` hoặc `tester`; `tester` mang role `reviewer` (chỉ để tra khẩu vị) nhưng posture không phải verdict: kết quả của nó không đòi assessment và không đỡ verdict receipt. Một unit khai ghế phải khớp đúng tập ghế checker cần, thiếu hay thừa bị từ chối `seat-multiplicity`. Rigor chỉ quyết tập này, không quyết tier. (Erratum E1.)
  - `panel` và `debate`: bắt buộc `seats:`. `params.members`, `params.role`, `params.synthesizeRole` và khoá `panelist-N` của `roleTasks` bị xoá; `roleTasks` và `workflow start --seats` khoá theo ghế.
  - `debate`: `thesis` và `antithesis` thành ghế role `producer`; `judge` là ghế role `judge` (trước đợt `patterns/debate.mjs:35-43` khoá chúng theo role).
- `CHECKER_ROLES` (`bind.mjs:19-24`, ép out-of-process theo tên role và tiền tố `panelist-`) được thay bằng posture.

Chuyển đổi (đã xong, mã chuyển đổi đã gỡ)","sectionText":"## 9. Chuyển đổi (đã xong, mã chuyển đổi đã gỡ)

Đợt chuyển từ "rigor chọn tier" sang "config khai tier" đã chạy xong trên mọi workspace; mã chuyển đổi, doctor `seat-binding-drain` và test hàng rào đã gỡ ngày 2026-10-23 (mục 15). Những gì còn sống:

1. **Config.** Config project mang tier khai trực tiếp; `runner.rigorToTier` không còn trong schema. Một config project còn khoá đó bị validation thường từ chối, tên khoá trong thông báo, và người dùng xoá khoá rồi khai `tier` (`validateRunnerConfigShape`, `test/runner/dispatch.test.mjs`). `fgos setup` không chuyển config cũ nữa. Marker `runner.patterns.seatBinding.schema` vẫn do config project mới ghi và validator vẫn đọc giá trị của nó; thiếu marker không bị từ chối.
2. **File global.** File global không nhận khoá seat binding. Chủ máy còn `runner.rigorToTier` trong `~/.fgos/config.json`: loader bỏ khoá đó trong bộ nhớ, in một dòng ghi chú mỗi tiến trình, không ghi lại file (`dropRetiredGlobalKeys`). Giữ đến khi chủ máy tự xoá khoá khỏi file global.
3. **Hash.** `snapshotRunnerConfig` (`run.mjs`) phủ `defaults`, `maxTier`, `tierFallback` và không có `rigorToTier`.
4. **Bản ghi cũ.** `unit.json` trước hàng rào (không có `seatSchema`) không resume được: bị từ chối `record-predates-seat-binding`; lịch sử của nó và ref theo role vẫn đọc qua `legacy-seat-read.mjs`, giữ vĩnh viễn theo quyết định của owner.
5. **Doctor.** `seat-binding-dry-bind` bind mọi ghế của mọi workflow đã đăng ký (cả workflow đóng gói) bằng cùng hàm, trong phiên headless cố định, không lease, không khởi động gì. Từ chối chính sách là fail; không có pool, trạng thái account, `max-tier-cap` và family dùng chung là thông tin. `seat-binding-route` (host trả lời route). `seat-binding-config` chỉ so `$comment` của config project với ladder (lệch được báo, không fail). `fgos setup` làm mới `$comment` lệch, không backup.
6. **Bản ghi quyết định.** D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) supersede phần chọn ghế của sáu rule ở mục 15 (không sửa tại chỗ); spec runner và workflow trỏ về đây."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-37","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-37","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-37","title":"Unheaded block 37","startLine":260,"endLine":260,"textDigest":"c234b855bc57979edce78d9643dc85b5d6d58271380b4e556233061909140914","sample":"Đợt chuyển từ "rigor chọn tier" sang "config khai tier" đã chạy xong trên mọi workspace; mã chuyển đổi, doctor `seat-binding-drain` và test hàng rào đã gỡ ngày 2026-10-23 (mục 15).","identityFingerprint":"acedce8a02ce5ec876cacd6add8c2f61c42dee7f47a0d42560cb1e882f08b50b","ancestry":["Spec: Seat Binding (một authority cho câu hỏi "ghế này chạy bằng gì")","9. Ví dụ minh hoạ"],"text":"### 10.2 `architecture-advisory` từ đầu đến cuối","sectionText":"### 10.2 `architecture-advisory` từ đầu đến cuối

Workflow (`shape-proposals` đã chuyển):

```yaml
- id: shape-proposals
  template:
    capability: architecture:shape
    pattern: panel
    blind: true
    seats:
      - { seat: system,      role: producer,    persona: system-lens, tier: frontier }
      - { seat: alternative, role: producer,    persona: alternative-lens }
      - { seat: constraint,  role: producer,    persona: constraint-lens }
      - { seat: synthesis,   role: synthesizer }
```

| Unit / ghế | Tier (nguồn) | maxTier | Executor → model | Độc lập |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| frame-context / producer | flagship (`architecture:*`.tier) | flagship (toàn cục) | claude → `opus` | — |
| shape / system | frontier (khuyến nghị workflow thắng `architecture:*`.tier) | frontier (cap) | claude → `fable` | panel mềm |
| shape / alternative | flagship (`architecture:*`.tier) | frontier | spread: openai → `gpt-6.1-sol` | mềm |
| shape / constraint | flagship | frontier | spread: gemini → `gemini-4-argon-high` | mềm |
| shape / synthesis | flagship | frontier | xai → `grok-4.6` (spread mềm: family ít peer nhất thắng; erratum E2) | mềm |
| critique / producer | frontier (khoá seat của cap) | frontier (cap) | claude → `fable` | — |
| critique / reviewer | flagship (prefix) | frontier | cứng ≠ claude: openai → `gpt-6.1-sol` | cứng so với producer |
| critique / red-team | flagship | frontier | `prefix.roles.red-team.prefer` → xai `grok-4.6` | cứng; đôi một ở high |
| synthesize / producer | frontier (khoá seat của cap) | frontier | claude → `fable` | — |
| synthesize / reviewer, red-team, tester | flagship (prefix); rigor critical → ba checker | frontier | openai; xai; tester → gemini | cứng, đôi một |
| explain / producer | flagship (prefix) | flagship | claude → `opus` | — |

**Biến thể A (ngân sách bằng mặc định capability).** Project đặt `"architecture:*": { "tier": "standard" }`. Ghế không có khuyến nghị workflow chạy standard; `system` giữ frontier, vì khuyến nghị workflow thắng `tier` của capability và prefix, miễn `architecture:shape.maxTier` cho phép.

**Biến thể B (ngân sách bằng trần).** Project không khai entry `architecture:shape` và giữ `maxTier: flagship` toàn cục. `system` giải ra frontier từ workflow rồi bị hạ: `tier flagship (max-tier-cap: maxTier = flagship, global), lowered from frontier (workflow:architecture-advisory/shape-proposals/system)`. Muốn giữ frontier cho ghế đó, đặt `capabilities."architecture:shape".maxTier = "frontier"`. Muốn ghim thấp hơn ở mọi nơi, đặt `capabilities."architecture:shape".seats.system.tier`.

**Biến thể C (từ chối).** Project đặt `"architecture:shape": { "seats": { "system": { "prefer": ["deepseek"] } } }` dưới biến thể B. Tier bị cap xuống flagship; deepseek không có cell flagship; `prefer` thay danh sách nên không còn candidate khác. Kết quả: `tier-cell-missing: shape-proposals/system flagship — no allowed executor has a cell; change capabilities."architecture:shape".seats.system.prefer or set capabilities."architecture:shape".seats.system.tier`.

Một dòng `explain` cho một ghế:

```
architecture-advisory / critique-proposals / red-team  (role red-team, capability architecture:critique)
  → xai grok-4.6 @ flagship, effort: invocation default (medium), account xai/<id>
    tier: capabilities."architecture:*".tier = flagship; maxTier: capabilities."architecture:critique".maxTier = frontier (not applied)
    prefer: capabilities."architecture:*".roles.red-team = [xai]; independence: ≠ producer(claude) ok, ≠ reviewer(openai) ok
    on failure: rotate xai accounts → tierFallback.flagship ∩ [xai] → none left: refuse
```"},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-41","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-41","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-41","title":"Unheaded block 41","startLine":296,"endLine":296,"textDigest":"76b945e9a0389feba40242167a7f6710849d38ad7f09551cc423858cfa939e01","sample":"Workflow (`shape-proposals` đã chuyển):","identityFingerprint":"2f6a8f3939d25292787e7b95ffec9f5df9a0018e2f655374f143a8a0c3549277","ancestry":["Spec: Seat Binding (một authority cho câu hỏi "ghế này chạy bằng gì")","10. - **Effort theo CLI** (`REASONING_EFFORT_CONTROLS`, `provider-adapter.mjs:255-261`): claude `--effort` (low…max, xhigh); codex không có flag, qua `-c model_reasoning_effort=<v>` và adapter ánh xạ `max` → `xhigh`; pi `--thinking` và omp `--thinking=` (off…max); mọi CLI đã cấu hình render đủ `low, medium, high, max`. agy cài sẵn nhưng chưa cấu hình; grok chưa có ánh xạ; gemini chưa cài.
- **Không có đầu vào chứng thực con người** cho `fgos run` trực tiếp: `bin/fgos.mjs:2851`, `:2862`, `:2878`, `:2889`, `unit-handoff.mjs:198` tự gán `human-cli`, `bind.mjs:385` tin nó; Session Identity chỉ cho biết phiên nào ghi (`docs/platform/identity/spec.md:52`). Cửa mạnh nhất hiện có là consent gate của workflow (`case-verbs.mjs:167-184, 222-233`, `case-runtime.mjs:176-209`, `case-admission.mjs:153-160`); bản ghi của nó không mang identity người trả lời (`case-runtime.mjs:193`) nên tin theo quy ước.
- **Herdr và `confinement: required`:** thoả lúc bind (`confinement/policies.mjs:682-701, 717-744`; `codex-herdr` và `claude-herdr-bwrap` khai `backend: bwrap`); confinement authority vẫn ghi `herdr-partial-maturity` và IPC host nằm ngoài phạm vi (`confinement/authority.mjs:424-468`).
- **Một executor mỗi family:** doctor `executor-family-unique` có thật (`src/setup/registrations.mjs:1473`).
- **Đã đo khi triển khai (2026-10-21):** exec cost của facade Shape S trên host release, config 22 KB, một ghế: p50 3.71 ms, p95 4.23 ms; ngân sách (hai lần p95 của `identity`, 5.02 ms) đạt. Seat Binding không exec dưới provider lock (test exec-budget). Số đo ở báo cáo phase 04 và 08.

- **Quyết định:**
  1. Một authority, Seat Binding, trả lời toàn bộ câu hỏi ghế agent (mục 3); crate Rust, route nội bộ, facade Node mỏng; chuyển đổi một đợt (mục 4, 9).
  2. Rigor chỉ quyết số checker và độc lập; `rigorToTier` bị xoá; tier khai trực tiếp trên sáu bậc định nghĩa theo bản chất việc; cell = model cộng effort tuỳ chọn (mục 5).
  3. Năm role; panel = N `producer` cộng `synthesizer`; workflow khai ghế tường minh và không khai `prefer` (mục 6.1, 7).
  4. Khẩu vị role sống trong config capability; `prefer` là khoá duy nhất; không có `families`, không có `domains`; chỉ ghế agent (mục 6.2).
  5. Chỉ con người nâng tier; đợt đầu không nâng bằng override (mục 5.5).
  6. Ghim `family#invocation` là cứng (mục 8); `--provider` giữ khoá theo executor.
  7. Project thắng, `maxTier` hạ hiển thị, từ chối chỉ khi thiếu cell (mục 5.4).

One-Screen Summary","sectionText":"## 1. One-Screen Summary

The earlier proposal was too hard to read because it mixed five things:
history, theory, schema shape, runtime primitive, and future implementation
fixture. This rewrite separates them.

The corrected framing:

```txt
The current system is too narrow for general group-cognitive work.

It can express:
  static declared graphs,
  one-shot or fixed-round handoffs,
  isolated fan-out/fan-in,
  mediated consult,
  synthesis.

It cannot yet express many common patterns:
  Delphi-style repeated feedback,
  Nominal Group Technique phase changes,
  RFC review with optional follow-up,
  adversarial triad with judge-driven rounds,
  master-coordinator style adaptive review/fix/red-team loops,
  dynamic specialist pull-in.
```

So the proposal should not be "just build a review loop." The proposal should
separate:

1. **Capability expansion** — which coordination dimensions must become
   expressible at all.
2. **Safety boundary** — what remains kernel-hard and non-negotiable.
3. **First slice** — the smallest useful fixture to prove the expanded model.

The product move is:

```txt
Keep isolation-heavy fixtures hard.
Add declared ways to express more group-thinking shapes.
Start with a bounded review loop only as the first safe proof slice.
```"},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-12","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-12","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-12","title":"Unheaded block 12","startLine":79,"endLine":81,"textDigest":"629f11e1404c5e9e1bf7008d441a2aacffb60e131461004b1c00ed4c2b8bf9a3","sample":"The earlier proposal was too hard to read because it mixed five things:

Why This Exists","sectionText":"## 2. Why This Exists

Step 08 produced an asymmetry:

- Phase 05 hardened `group-cognition-framework.yaml`, an isolation-heavy
  topology. It proves that peer chat, recursive graph growth, vote-as-truth,
  and hidden sibling influence cannot be expressed in that fixture.
- Phases 06-07 were implemented with the manual `master-coordinator` playbook,
  which is communication-heavy: Doer, Reviewer, Fixer, Red-Team, and a
  persistent coordinator deciding whether another round is needed. That process
  found real bugs, including critical security bugs.

So the real question is not only:

```txt
Isolation or communication?
```

Nor is it only:

```txt
What is the smallest review-loop V1?
```

It is:

```txt
Which group-cognitive capabilities should fgOS make expressible, and how do
we add them without weakening fixtures whose value comes from strict isolation?
```"},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-18","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-18","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-18","title":"Unheaded block 18","startLine":122,"endLine":122,"textDigest":"56f067ebd17b3b158b4a3b16f9abd6b5aa5469cfe86379ddd30708259e5e32db","sample":"Step 08 produced an asymmetry:","identityFingerprint":"50006a43e4ca4b9f62d52f4b6b5db763eb109fbef4325ddb299eb9a171dc9e62","ancestry":["Architecture Intent","2. The Simple Model","sectionText":"## 4. The Simple Model

There are three layers:

```txt
Tier 1: Kernel safety
  Always enforced. No fixture opts out.

Tier 2: Fixture posture
  Each fixture declares whether it allows runtime communication deviation.
  Isolation fixture: no deviation envelope.
  Communication fixture: bounded deviation envelope.

Tier 3: Runtime rounds
  The external session driver may request extra review/recheck/consult rounds,
  but only through governed, budgeted, immutable events.
```

The important architectural rule:

```txt
The graph is the default route.
The external session driver is the leader.
The leader is not a graph node.
```

Reason: a leader inside the graph would be another dispatched worker claiming
"I verified this." That is self-report, not independent stop-gate authority.
The master-coordinator worked because the persistent driver re-read evidence
and decided whether the process could stop."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-26","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-26","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-26","title":"Unheaded block 26","startLine":167,"endLine":167,"textDigest":"fa32e44fe051372f495c106e1d4cc9d931d315fd75a14a1600cd8bdf120b4557","sample":"There are three layers:","identityFingerprint":"c6df48ef4894f9047546b752408f9e7cf377eb2a25cfec9e0be33f976fbc7899","ancestry":["Architecture Intent","4. Capability Axes As The Map","sectionText":"## 5. Capability Axes As The Map

The original seven axes are not decorative. They are the capability map. The
second sol-agent pass surfaced two more axes, deliberation memory and speech
acts, that explain why merely adding more graph edges would still leave common
review/problem-solving methods under-specified.

| Axis | What it asks | What fgOS supports today | What broader group cognition needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Topology shape | Who can see/send to whom? | Static edges only; no runtime-added edges; isolation fixture intentionally has no peer edges. | Static, star, pipeline, fan-out/fan-in, RFC-style many reviewers, optional specialist pull-in, possibly later dynamic edges. |
| Timing | Real-time or round-based? | Round-based async only. | Mostly round-based for V1; synchronous pair/mob remains separate because mutation exclusivity makes it expensive. |
| Role symmetry | Peers or asymmetric roles? | Mostly asymmetric roles. | Both asymmetric roles and symmetric reviewer sets, depending on fixture. |
| Information visibility | Raw peer output, aggregate, mediated artifact, or anonymous feedback? | Mediated, isolated-until-fan-in, or broadcast as static fixture posture. | Delphi/NGT need aggregate/anonymized feedback phases; RFC review may expose sibling comments after first pass; adversarial work needs controlled visibility windows. |
| Control regime / meta-authority | Fixed graph, driver-selected, data-triggered, or graph self-changing? | Fixed graph; external driver can imperatively call existing verbs, but protocol schema does not declare optional driver-selected rounds cleanly. | Driver-authorized optional rounds, conditional transitions, maybe later dynamic edge creation. In-graph autonomous leader remains rejected. |
| Feedback loop | One-shot, fixed-N, adaptive, convergence-based? | Fixed declared handoffs, often `maxRounds: 1`; retry exists but is not recheck. | Bounded adaptive loops: repeat review, critique, feedback, or recheck until stop condition or budget. |
| Decision / aggregation rule | How does N output become group answer? | `completion.mode` is coarse: synthesize/all-required/explicit-partial. | Vote, rank, Delphi convergence, author synthesis, judge ruling, dissent-preserving synthesis, explicit no-consensus. |
| Deliberation memory | What state persists across rounds? | Assignment artifacts and evidence refs. | Proposal versions, objections, responses, dispositions, unresolved issues, and revision lineage. |
| Speech acts | What kind of contribution was made? | Generic assignment result. | Typed `propose`, `challenge`, `clarify`, `respond`, `rank`, `request-round`, and `disposition` events. |

The first brainstorm was right that the current shape is too strict for many
ordinary group-thinking methods. The correction is that we do not need to
soften everything globally. Each fixture should declare where it sits on these
axes."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-31","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-31","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-31","title":"Unheaded block 31","startLine":198,"endLine":201,"textDigest":"ec0f9fdc5da7b3d47927e80ff836b80fcd0aeaa3068806afb8d259dca1fb9cbd","sample":"The original seven axes are not decorative. What Is Strictly Not Supported Today","sectionText":"## 6. What Is Strictly Not Supported Today

These are strict gaps if the goal is broad group-cognitive capability:

| Pattern | Strict gap today | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Delphi | No first-class aggregate/anonymized feedback phase. | Participants cannot receive controlled group feedback between rounds without ad hoc driver prose. |
| Nominal Group Technique | No declared phase rule for "silent generation -> round-robin sharing -> discussion -> private vote." | The schema can approximate phases, but not the visibility/voting rules that define the method. |
| RFC review | No clean optional follow-up rounds or comment visibility windows. | Many reviewers can run, but "author responds, selected reviewers recheck" is not declared as a reusable protocol. |
| Adversarial triad | No judge/driver authorization event and no distinct ruling/disposition primitive. | Doer/Red-Team/Judge can be simulated manually, but the protocol cannot show who ruled what and why. |
| Master-coordinator loop | No declared adaptive review/fix/red-team loop. | Retry exists, but recheck is semantically different and must preserve prior verdicts. |
| Dynamic specialist pull-in | No runtime `addSessionEdge` or equivalent. | A driver cannot add a previously unknown expert edge while keeping the graph/event audit complete. |
| Conditional materialization | No schema field for "run this operation only if prior result has accepted finding." | Driver can decide imperatively, but fixture cannot declare the condition. |
| Rich aggregation | `completion.mode` is too coarse for vote/rank/convergence/no-consensus semantics. | Group answer rules are part of cognition, not output formatting. |
| Deliberation memory | No first-class proposal/objection/response/disposition state. | Assignment artifacts alone are not enough for RFC review, NGT clarification, or judge disposition. |

These gaps do not mean the current architecture is wrong. It means Step 08
built the first strict, safe subset. This proposal is about widening that
subset deliberately."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-34","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-34","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-34","title":"Unheaded block 34","startLine":222,"endLine":222,"textDigest":"2b0993fe5dc255c18326022db83f8e2239dc0a6762b74960e1e458600c11a92c","sample":"These are strict gaps if the goal is broad group-cognitive capability:","identityFingerprint":"893fce43b6b2c1c90d1a329ca77d38a5c71a17671905f3c8cb9aa4cd36e115c8","ancestry":["Architecture Intent","6. Expansion Order","sectionText":"## 7. Expansion Order

Capability expansion should happen in layers:

1. **Optional declared rounds** — let a fixture declare operations that may be
   materialized only after driver authorization. This unlocks bounded
   review/recheck loops, RFC follow-up, and adversarial rechecks without
   dynamic topology mutation.
2. **Visibility windows / context grants** — let the fixture say what an actor
   may see before and after named milestones. Windows are static legality;
   `grantedContextRefs` remain the concrete per-invocation grant. The first
   slice is fail-closed private-first-pass and post-independent-pass sharing,
   not anonymization or aggregate transformation.
3. **Request/disposition events** — let actors request another round, and let
   the driver accept/reject with evidence refs. This unlocks judge/triad and
   master-coordinator auditability.
4. **Evidence-preserving aggregation** — validate one honest synthesis method
   first, with explicit source coverage, dissent, unresolved objections,
   omissions, failures, and artifact revisions. Vote, rank tally, and
   convergence remain later candidates until typed inputs exist.
5. **Typed deliberation events** — add durable, artifact-backed contributions
   such as `proposal`, `objection`, `response`, `clarification`, `rank`, and
   `specialist-request`. This is not a live peer-chat mailbox; it is structured
   deliberation state the runtime can audit. Driver disposition remains the
   existing driver-owned event rather than a worker contribution type.
6. **Bounded specialist binding** — let the external driver bind a specialist
   identity into a predeclared, capped topology slot. Arbitrary
   `addSessionEdge` remains deferred until multiple real consumers prove that
   declared slots are insufficient."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-37","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-37","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-37","title":"Unheaded block 37","startLine":242,"endLine":242,"textDigest":"fd2b5ee305d467faddebf503e89dd29685dcff6f54f1bc9af00a0dc4d7f7ab3a","sample":"Capability expansion should happen in layers:","identityFingerprint":"201229c61bcdd78de9628701962555d4f341fb09981f4aa24ab174f0e3e2e727","ancestry":["Architecture Intent","7. First Safe Slice: `bounded-review-loop.yaml`","sectionText":"## 8. First Safe Slice: `bounded-review-loop.yaml`

The first slice can still be a read-only coordination fixture around an
existing artifact. It is not the whole answer; it is the first proof that the
expanded capability model works without weakening isolation fixtures.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Existing artifact or code diff] --> R[Reviewer]
  A --> T[Red-Team]
  R -->|finding| D[External session driver]
  T -->|finding| D
  D -->|asks owner outside protocol| F[New artifact revision]
  F -->|driver authorizes declared operation| R2[Reviewer recheck]
  F -->|driver authorizes declared operation| T2[Red-Team recheck]
  R --> S[Synthesis]
  T --> S
  R2 --> S
  T2 --> S
```

What it can do:

- run independent Reviewer and Red-Team passes;
- keep Reviewer and Red-Team isolated before first verdict;
- allow driver-authorized clarification, consult, or recheck rounds;
- preserve failed actors, dissent, unsupported claims, and evidence refs;
- prove all extra rounds are visible in the session ledger.

What it cannot do yet:

- mutate source code as a protocol-owned Doer;
- move Work status/stage;
- merge or approve Work;
- spawn unbounded rounds;
- make an in-graph actor the stop gate.

That means a real mutating `code-implementation-cell.yaml` is a later design,
after Work-attached mutation authority and worktree isolation are explicitly
designed.

This is not really "peer communication." It is artifact-mediated orchestration:
agents produce independent artifacts, the driver dispositions them, and later
agents receive explicit context grants."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-39","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-39","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-39","title":"Unheaded block 39","startLine":272,"endLine":274,"textDigest":"da45552a8c2663cc757b9e9bda1058cc63dc299d30f3491a0f96b95a0294f605","sample":"The first slice can still be a read-only coordination fixture around an

The Primitive Is Still Open","sectionText":"## 9. The Primitive Is Still Open

The earlier draft centered one topology-changing primitive:

```txt
addSessionEdge(coordinationId, { from, to, intent, reason, triggeredBy, maxRounds })
```

That should probably not be V1's first primitive.

Most master-coordinator behavior is:

```txt
Run another declared operation because evidence now says it is needed.
```

Examples:

- Reviewer reports a bug, so a fix/recheck round is needed.
- Red-Team reports an exploit, so a fix/adversarial-recheck round is needed.
- A recheck fails, so another bounded recheck round is needed if budget remains.

That suggests a smaller first primitive:

```txt
authorizeDeclaredOperation(...)
```

Shape:

```json
{
  "operationId": "reviewer-recheck",
  "triggerEvidenceRefs": ["run-result-or-assignment-id"],
  "requestedBy": "reviewer-actor",
  "authorizedBy": "external-session-driver",
  "roundKey": "reviewer-recheck:2",
  "reason": "Reviewer found a regression; owner supplied a new artifact revision."
}
```

Possible split:

| Primitive | Use |
|---|---|
| `requestRound` | Actor records that another round is needed. No dispatch authority. |
| `authorizeDeclaredOperation` | Driver authorizes one already-declared optional operation. |
| `addSessionEdge` | Later-only primitive for a genuinely unknown specialist consult edge. |

`artifact-source` is not modeled as a topology actor. Initial Reviewer and

```yaml
profile:
  kind: CoordinationProtocol
  completion:
    mode: synthesize
  topology:
    contextVisibility: mediated
    edges: []
  optionalRounds:
    authority: external-session-driver
    requestedByRoles: [reviewer, red-team]
    operations:
      - reviewer-recheck
      - red-team-recheck
      - specialist-consult
    maxRoundsPerOperation: 1
    mutatingOperationsAllowed: false
  independence:
    noCrossReadBefore:
      - actors: [reviewer-actor, red-team-actor]
        milestone: first-independent-verdicts-linked
```

This table separates the retired coordination design from current owners. The
coordination engine was retired in `2180b4e72701bb090288af8fe8021008d9d42079`;
see [the current-owner map](../../agent-coordination/spec.md#current-summary).
The proposed V1 remains discussion intent, not an accepted runtime contract.

| Area | Current system | Conflict / gap for V1 |
|---|---|---|
| `FlowDefinition` topology | In the retired coordination engine, edges connected SessionActors. | An artifact/diff is not a SessionActor, so initial review must be modeled as root operations with explicit context refs, not `artifact-source -> reviewer`. |
| Declared operation dispatch | Historical: the retired engine dispatched declared operations. Architecture Change Size"],"text":"### 12.1 Small V1: bounded review loop, no topology mutation","sectionText":"### 12.1 Small V1: bounded review loop, no topology mutation

This is the current recommendation.

Expected architecture change: **small to medium**, not a rewrite.

What already works:

- `CoordinationProtocol` fixtures already declare actors, operations, graph
  phases, topology, completion mode, and policy.
- `dispatchDeclaredOperation` can already materialize a declared operation.
- A declared operation with no incoming topology edge can already receive
  explicit `contextRefs`.
- Session-wide hard bounds are already forwarded into the locked
  `createSessionAssignment` path: `maxAssignments`, `maxConcurrency`, and
  `maxRounds`.
- Existing isolation fixtures are unaffected if the new fixture uses a separate
  schema field and leaves their topology unchanged.

What must be added:

- A way to declare optional rounds, such as `optionalRounds`.
- An event/verb pair like `requestRound` and `authorizeDeclaredOperation`, so
  the ledger shows who requested, who authorized, why, and which evidence refs
  triggered the extra round.
- A context grant shape for rechecks: which artifact/diff revision and which
  previous verdicts the recheck may see.
- Negative tests for no pre-verdict Reviewer/Red-Team leakage, no unauthorized
  actor dispatch, no unbounded rounds, no mutation, and no budget bypass.

This scope does **not** require changing Work lifecycle, adding dynamic graph
mutation, or changing `group-cognition-framework.yaml`."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-64","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-64","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-64","title":"Unheaded block 64","startLine":435,"endLine":435,"textDigest":"0f09401cdae967fd6a319d6fc8f4a7330f7f6f26eff1f661cc355251fac24685","sample":"This is the current recommendation.","identityFingerprint":"ff1f077c46721d7fa556f4f6f1ac08f9b47ecec113374bec1f43e9b7d0541175","ancestry":["Architecture Intent","12. Architecture Change Size"],"text":"### 12.4 What Is Strictly Impossible Today?","sectionText":"### 12.4 What Is Strictly Impossible Today?

Under current accepted contracts/runtime, these are strictly not expressible:

- Dynamic topology mutation inside a declared protocol: no runtime
  `addSessionEdge` exists, and undeclared edges are illegal.
- A topology edge from an artifact/diff to an actor: topology edges connect
  SessionActors, not files or artifacts.
- Protocol-owned code mutation: standalone CoordinationSession has read-only
  Work context only.
- In-graph leader with stop-gate authority: not a runtime primitive and
  rejected by this proposal's verification-laundering argument.
- Reviewer/Red-Team first-pass cross-read while preserving independence:
  if independence is claimed, their first verdicts need no shared context
  except the starting artifact.
- Recheck as retry: retry supersedes a run for the same Assignment; recheck
  must be a new judgment preserving the earlier verdict.

These are currently possible with modest additions:

- Run declared root review operations over explicit artifact refs.
- Add an authorization event before re-dispatching a declared optional recheck.

Problems In The Earlier Proposal","sectionText":"## 14. Problems In The Earlier Proposal

The earlier draft had the right instinct but unclear shape:

1. It used the phrase `code-implementation-cell` while mutation stayed out of
   scope.
2. It over-centered `addSessionEdge`, although the safest V1 needs another
   declared round, not topology mutation.
3. It treated `session-driver` too much like a graph actor, even though the
   driver is outside the graph.
4. It blurred "actor requests another round" and "driver authorizes another
   round."
5. It did not clearly state that `maxRounds` is currently enforced through
   Assignment-count-like machinery.
6. It used role-level `forbiddenPairs`, but the real rule is time-windowed:
   Reviewer and Red-Team must not see each other before first independent
   verdicts; after that, driver-mediated synthesis or recheck may be valid.

Default Path And Deferred Path","sectionText":"## 15. Default Path And Deferred Path

Default path for V1: do not add `addSessionEdge` at all.

Instead:

```txt
V1 only adds requestRound + authorizeDeclaredOperation.
```

That would mean:

- the fixture must declare all possible Reviewer/Red-Team/Fixer/Recheck paths
  upfront;
- runtime can choose whether to run a declared optional path;
- no new actor-to-actor edge can appear mid-session;
- specialist consult remains out of V1 unless declared upfront as an optional
  operation.

Benefit: smaller schema, easier negative tests, less risk of weakening
isolation guarantees by accident.

Cost: less flexible than the master-coordinator playbook. Some real "pull in a
specialist now" cases would still need manual driver behavior outside the
declared fixture.

This is the safest first slice if the goal is to prove bounded review-loop
coordination without immediately opening topology mutation."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-96","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-96","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-96","title":"Unheaded block 96","startLine":643,"endLine":643,"textDigest":"2f71acb9bef46280693a7ef1d200f1ded1848981fba440633456f038d8be7f42","sample":"Default path for V1: do not add `addSessionEdge` at all.","identityFingerprint":"8cfb341e93590ab8a3fe10481f791d7fe0b71bbcc5ebc72bd9d996296df2787b","ancestry":["Architecture Intent","15. These objections should stay visible until answered:

- Driver authority is now central. The design must define driver identity,
  authorization, audit trail, and bounds. Calling it "external driver" is not
  enough.
- Fixes happen outside the protocol, so each verdict must pin the artifact or
  diff revision it reviewed. Otherwise a later fix can make earlier evidence
  stale or ambiguous.
- Retry is not recheck. Retry supersedes an attempt for the same Assignment;
  recheck is a new judgment that must preserve both old and new verdicts.
- Assignment count is not full round semantics. It is a conservative hard cap,
  but future runtime should avoid treating it as the conceptual definition of
  a round.
- `first-independent-verdicts-linked` needs precise behavior when an actor
  fails, is late, is replaced, or the session closes partial.
- Synthesis must not hide dissent. The output contract must preserve findings,
  dispositions, evidence refs, failed/missing actors, and unresolved dissent as
  separate fields or sections.
- P05.2 proves the current infra can produce an honest null result under
  failure. It does not prove the bounded review loop improves quality. A later
  live proof must test that claim directly."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-102","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-102","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-102","title":"Unheaded block 102","startLine":672,"endLine":672,"textDigest":"905370b46292b288e2a9cb8fdf596f240de144605f5c86eeb24f2bc8285b647c","sample":"These objections should stay visible until answered:","identityFingerprint":"c93f72489eecf087d88566713d289223fddfcaf0f2ce2ed638cc2b63c207e73d","ancestry":["Architecture Intent","16. MVP Roadmap","sectionText":"## 17. MVP Roadmap

This is the plan shape, not a menu of questions. Each MVP keeps the original
intention alive while adding only the architecture needed for that layer. The
detailed proposal lives in
[Step 09 - Group Thinking Substrate](../../proposals/step-09-group-thinking-substrate.md).

Stable spine:

```txt
FlowDefinition = static legality envelope
CoordinationSession = event-sourced runtime ledger
External driver = adaptive authority outside the worker graph
Assignment / Run / RunResult = execution and evidence path
Context grant = visibility and memory access path
Skill / surface = thin launcher only
```

| MVP | Goal | Real shape | Architecture change | Proof |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Shape lock. | Record the stable spine and boundaries before runtime work. | Docs-only. | Link/check review; no runtime/schema edit. |
| 1 | Standalone Master Coordination fixture. | `plan.md` or `artifact.md` enters a declared worker graph: Doer, Reviewer, Red-Team, Fixer/Doer-followup, optional Synthesizer. Doer/Fixer produce session-local artifacts/revisions. | Fixture draft first; schema validation after acceptance. | Static skeleton expresses Master Coordination without Work fields or git authority. |
| 2 | Driver authorization primitive. | Optional operations require `operation-authorized` before dispatch, with `authorizationId`, `operationId`, `targetActorId`, `invocationKey`, `authorizedBy`, `reason`, `grantedContextRefs`, and `artifactRevision`. | Schema/runtime after acceptance. | Missing authorization, undeclared operation, over-cap invocation, terminal-session authorization, and context beyond grant are rejected. |
| 3 | Recheck and disposition. | Recheck is a new Assignment against a new artifact revision; disposition is a driver event, not worker self-report. | Schema/runtime after MVP 2. | Old verdict remains immutable; new verdict links to revision; synthesis preserves dissent and unresolved findings. |
| 4 | Surface launcher. | A skill/slash surface builds a request for a declared fixture and calls `fgos coordination run --file`, then reads `coordination show`/evidence. | Surface only; no group-thinking logic inside the skill. | Launcher cannot bypass FlowDefinition/session authorization. |
| 5 | Live standalone proof. | Run the Master Coordination loop with no Work: input plan, Doer artifact, Reviewer report, Red-Team report, driver-authorized fix, revision, recheck, final disposition. | CLI/headless run. | CLI/headless parity, crash/resume no duplicate, unauthorized optional operation rejected, hidden context rejected, bounds enforced. |
| 6 | Visibility windows. | Topology declares fail-closed private-first-pass and post-independent-pass windows; operation bindings select a window; authorization and Assignment provenance retain exact `grantedContextRefs`. | Deferred schema/runtime. | Opt-in fixtures share only eligible same-session artifact refs after the milestone; unchanged isolation fixtures still reject sibling leakage. |
| 7 | Evidence-preserving aggregation. | Keep completion eligibility separate from one `evidence-preserving-synthesis` method whose validated outcome is `consensus`, `qualified`, or `no-consensus`. | Deferred schema/runtime plus Team Cognition boundary. | Aggregate output cannot hide source coverage, dissent, unresolved objections, failed/missing actors, or artifact revisions, and cannot upgrade evidence confidence. |
| 8 | Deliberation memory. | Link immutable, artifact-backed `proposal`, `objection`, `response`, `clarification`, `rank`, and `specialist-request` contributions into the session ledger. | Deferred schema/runtime. | Replay preserves contribution lineage without recipient, inbox, unread, delivery, or arbitrary message-body semantics. |
| 9 | Bounded dynamic specialist pull-in. | The driver binds one specialist into a predeclared, capability- and assignment-capped specialist slot, then uses existing operation authorization. | Deferred schema/runtime. | Opt-in fixture accepts the bounded binding; undeclared slots, over-cap binding, foreign context, unauthorized writers, and unchanged isolation fixtures reject it. |
