6. **Machine backend registry:** `~/.fgos/confinement-backends.json` được định nghĩa theo schema đóng `confinement-backend-registry.v1`, không cho phép project config ghi đè, và tự động bootstrap qua `fgos doctor --fix` (P01).
7. **Bản đồ kiến trúc:** Component `src/runner/dispatch/confinement/`, slice `confinement-enforcement`, và contract CTR010 (`confinement-authority.v1`) đã được đăng ký chính thức tại `docs/architecture-map.md` (P07)."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-140","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-140","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-140","title":"Unheaded block 140","startLine":1396,"endLine":1396,"textDigest":"a7fc9ce0823faab5b809042244aae5280d335cab7d03343c7e3ba2fe7e1e20ea","sample":"Bảy rủi ro ban đầu đã được giải quyết qua các cell thi công P00-P06:","identityFingerprint":"b1c786cc1b5446ca0588e253b69428a929822a0c3f7007a24dd17cf671eb9c00","ancestry":["Spec: Agent Confinement Authority","13. **Công thức (đã chạy thật, Request-to-Run P6):** một invocation `herdr-spawn` có `confinement.backend: bwrap` giữ trạng thái của agent trong một private home thay vì thư mục account thật (đang read-only dưới posture):

1. `credentialStore: { use: <codex | pi | omp>, homeEnv: <CODEX_HOME | PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR>, files?: [...] }` trên invocation (cùng dạng `codex-cli-bwrap`; runner.md RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)). Config viết trước field này (config toàn máy, project khác) vẫn khai `resourceBindings: [{ resource: 'private-home', target: { kind: 'env', name: <biến> } }]`; một hàm (`credentialStoreOf`) suy `credentialStore` từ đó, và nhánh suy này bị xoá khi các config ấy đã chuyển.
2. Login của account đến từ inventory toàn máy `runner.providers.<provider>.accounts.<id>.credentialSource` trong `~/.fgos/config.json` (RUL65b của `docs/specs/runner.md`): kind `codex-home` (`auth.json`) hoặc `home-files` (danh sách file tường minh, copy owner-only, fail closed) — driver `drivers/bwrap.mjs` copy vào private home trước khi spawn, theo `credentialStore.files` của invocation nếu có, không thì theo danh sách của account. **Luật chép (2026-10-19, thay luật "thiếu một file thì từ chối"):** file có mặt thì chép, file vắng thì bỏ qua, không file nào có mặt thì từ chối `credential-provisioning` (`credential-store-empty`); symlink treo hay trỏ ra ngoài home, file không thường, đường dẫn có `..` vẫn bị từ chối. Invocation không khai store thì không được chép gì dù account nào được lease (bài học `569f72d3b`), và `assessBwrap` từ chối policy không cấp `private-home` cho invocation đọc store. Account có thể khai `credentialSources` (một store cho mỗi CLI, key là `credentialStore.use` của invocation); request của Authority (`buildConfinementRequest`) chọn store theo khoá đó, và khoá không có store thì bị từ chối trước khi worker chạy (runner.md RUL80 (account trước, CLI sau: một login store cho mỗi CLI)). Không mount thư mục account thật, không bypass flag thay sandbox.
3. Trust của workspace ghi vào store trong private home (`herdr-round.mjs` `trustStorePaths`), dẫn xuất từ store account thật — store của chính account được lease (credential source mà Authority chuyển cho adapter qua `trustAccountSource`), không phải account mà env tĩnh của invocation chỉ tới (runner.md RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store)); với codex, trust từng hook của `<cwd>/.codex/hooks.json` (`[hooks.state."<đường dẫn tuyệt đối>:<event>:<nhóm>:<handler>"] trusted_hash`, băm theo luật của codex, ghim bằng test) được gieo cùng lúc, chỉ vào config của private home (không bao giờ vào config thật của account; private home bị xoá sau dispatch nên không có bước gỡ) và chỉ khi gốc repo đã được người dùng tin; với claude, các MCP server do `<cwd>/.mcp.json` khai báo được duyệt riêng cho tiến trình worker bằng `--settings` (`enabledMcpjsonServers`, thêm vào args khi chuẩn bị worker invocation; không ghi file dùng chung), cũng chỉ khi gốc repo đã được tin; `fgos doctor` check `confined-pane-accounts` báo invocation confine nào đọc store mà account không có file nào của store đó (agent sẽ khởi động chưa đăng nhập), và ghi chú file vắng.

**Lịch sử (để khỏi suy ra lại):** `5a42bc376` (2026-09-11) `codex-bwrap` cli-spawn có private-home→`CODEX_HOME`; `569f72d3b`, `a1a966ff2`, `ec6a0745d` (09-16, rotator slice 1 thay `FGOS_CODEX_CREDENTIAL_HOMES`) chuyển credential sang inventory (khi đó chỉ `codex-home`). `c54c1888b`, `8c4b4aeeb`, `2cff7102a` (09-11..18) đưa launch confine của herdr-spawn qua Authority — chứng minh bằng worker giả và claude. `e37f8225d` (09-21, H8) từ chối `credential-provisioning-unsupported` cho adapter khác cli-spawn; lý do chỉ nằm trong comment code và `plans/reports/dispatch-execution-engine-architecture-review-260920.md`. `e7bd9b418`, `a9fc61324` (09-17) gộp/đổi tên executor id (`codex-bwrap` thành `openai`/`codex-cli-bwrap`), `5bbd066cd` xoá `claude-herdr`/`pi-herdr` "dormant" nên grep theo tên cũ không còn ra. `cfd670c43` (2026-10-01) áp posture lên mọi invocation herdr nhưng không kèm binding: codex/pi/agy chết ngay lúc khởi động (state dir read-only). 2026-10-19 (đợt model pool B2): binding chung `resourceBindings` được thay bằng `credentialStore` trên invocation, khoá chọn store là `use` thay vì tên lệnh, và id invocation bỏ tên account (`codex-herdr-fgovn` thành `codex-herdr`).

**Vì sao từng bị quên:** (a) cách làm nằm trong commit và trong spec dưới nhãn "Codex bwrap" nên đọc như chuyện riêng của cli-spawn; (b) ngoại lệ H8 loại herdr-spawn không có trong spec; (c) id executor bị đổi tên, tìm theo tên cũ không thấy; (d) phase "facts" của kế hoạch chỉ hỏi về code hiện tại, không hỏi "trước đây đã có gì và vì sao bị bỏ". Private home nhận một **bản chép** của login, bị xoá sau dispatch. Hai điều đi kèm (chi tiết và luật ở `docs/specs/runner.md`, RUL75 (login xoay vòng được gia hạn một lần tại nguồn, trong bản chép fgOS giữ, và login được gia hạn trong private home được ghi ngược)):

- **Kho SQLite chép dạng snapshot.** File `agent.db` (omp) trong danh sách `files` được chép bằng `VACUUM INTO` qua `node:sqlite` — snapshot nhất quán, gồm cả phần còn nằm trong write-ahead log — thay vì chép file thô thiếu WAL; không có `node:sqlite` thì chép file như trước. Danh sách file được phép chép không đổi, thư mục account thật vẫn không bao giờ được mount.
- **Bản mới hơn được ghi ngược lúc xoá home.** Khi dispatch được opt-in (caller truyền hàm gia hạn), ownership marker của private home ghi thêm `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, home nguồn, layout, runtime dir; chỉ tên và đường dẫn, không giá trị credential) sau khi chép xong. Mọi đường xoá home — cleanup của driver, `finalizeConfinementResources` và orphan reaper — đi qua một hàm xoá duy nhất (`removeConfinementDir`, `confinement/cleanup.mjs`): trước khi xoá, login trong home mới hơn login nguồn thì được dàn (staging) rồi áp lên nguồn dưới lock của account, một lần thử không chờ; lock bận thì để `pending/` cho lần refresh-ahead kế tiếp. Lỗi ghi ngược chỉ báo bằng mã cố định trên stderr và chỉ chặn việc xoá trong đúng một trường hợp: việc dàn thất bại (xem dưới). Bản dàn không bao giờ bị xoá khi nguồn không đọc được (đang ghi dở, `agent.db` không mở được, hoặc không xác định được entry) hay khi bản chép không đọc được vì lý do có thể qua (thiếu `node:sqlite`, `agent.db` không mở được): bản chép được giữ ở `pending/` (giới hạn 5 bản mỗi kho login (mỗi account với một kho, mỗi `stores/<cli>` với kho theo CLI), nhưng chỉ bản dư thừa mới bị bỏ: sau khi áp các bản pending dưới account lock, bản có login trùng hệt một bản pending khác thì bị bỏ khi account vượt giới hạn, bản mới nhất của mỗi nhóm trùng được giữ; bản không chứng minh được là dư thừa hay lỗi thời thì không bao giờ bị bỏ để nhường chỗ, nên account có thể vượt giới hạn và check doctor báo; bản do probe ghi dở được giữ ở `torn/` cho việc khôi phục thủ công, không bao giờ tự áp hay tự bỏ, và doctor báo ở mọi tuổi; `torn/` chỉ áp cho bản scratch của probe, còn scratch do runner đã chết để lại và pane home có store bị cắt vẫn bị xoá khi JSON không đọc được; bản không parse được thì so theo byte của file store và của write-ahead log hoặc rollback journal không rỗng (file không đọc được, trừ khi không tồn tại, không bao giờ bị coi là không có; index `-shm` không tính); home có file store trùng từng byte với nguồn và không bên nào có write-ahead log hay journal không rỗng thì không renew gì nên không được dàn) và báo `staged`/`apply-deferred`; chỉ xoá khi nguồn đọc được và chứng minh bản chép không mới hơn, hoặc bản chép được chứng minh hỏng (JSON hỏng, hay không có entry dùng được). Lỗi đọc file của hệ điều hành (quyền, I/O; mã `unreadable-file`) có thể qua nên bản chép được giữ; chỉ file kho không tồn tại (`missing-file`) mới được coi là rỗng và bị xoá. Nếu việc dàn thất bại, private home và marker được giữ lại (việc xoá báo lỗi, một dòng stderr mã cố định) để lần xoá sau, kể cả của reaper, thử lại; mỗi lần thất bại được đếm trong marker (`credentialKept`; hai lần cách nhau dưới 15 phút chỉ tính một, để lỗi tạm thời không dùng hết hạn mức), marker được ghi qua file tạm rồi rename và marker có mặt nhưng đọc không được thì việc xoá dừng lại. Sau 5 lần home bị giữ hẳn: không thử xoá nữa, không bao giờ bị xoá vì quá tuổi. Home bị giữ được kiểm lại dưới account lock khi account đó được gia hạn lần kế tiếp và bởi `fgos doctor --fix` (tập temp root tìm kiếm giống của doctor: root mặc định cộng `tempRoot` của từng backend đã đăng ký, lấy qua hook do phía dispatch truyền xuống; home nằm dưới `privateHomeRoot` riêng của backend không thuộc tập này nên không check, repair, reaper hay lần gia hạn nào thấy, và cũng không bao giờ bị xoá), và chỉ với home thuộc đúng runtime dir của lock đang giữ: chỉ xoá khi nguồn đọc được và chứng minh login trong home không mới hơn, hoặc login đó đã dàn được cạnh nguồn (và được áp); không thì vẫn giữ. Bản đã dàn và thư mục `pending/` được đồng bộ xuống đĩa trước khi home bị xoá. File marker không nhận ra được là marker nào cả (không phải JSON, không phải object, hay không có tên contract) thì mọi việc xoá home đó dừng lại. Finalizer so digest của marker không tính `credentialKept` (cleanup của driver thêm trường này sau khi digest được lấy) và không dừng ở home đó mà vẫn xoá các resource còn lại của dispatch (dispatch ghi là `retained`, kèm lý do của home). Check `credential-copies-retained` của `fgos doctor` báo theo provider/account: home bị giữ hẳn (fail, nêu thư mục home), home đang thử lại và các bản `pending/`/scratch quá một ngày (cảnh báo); chỉ có số đếm và tuổi, không bao giờ in giá trị, và check không xoá gì. Provisioning Codex đóng kín (fail closed): `auth.json` là symlink trỏ ra ngoài home, hoặc `home` tương đối, làm dispatch thất bại trước khi worker chạy (trước đây symlink được theo, home tương đối được hiểu theo cwd). Đường xoá home gọi module gia hạn credential (`provider-credential-renewal.mjs`) và qua đó phụ thuộc vào provider capacity, chỉ để lấy account lock. Bản dàn không bao giờ bị xoá khi nguồn không đọc được (đang ghi dở, `agent.db` không mở được, hoặc không xác định được entry) hay khi bản chép không đọc được vì lý do có thể qua (thiếu `node:sqlite`, `agent.db` không mở được): bản chép được giữ ở `pending/` (giới hạn 5 bản mỗi kho login (mỗi account với một kho, mỗi `stores/<cli>` với kho theo CLI), nhưng chỉ bản dư thừa mới bị bỏ: sau khi áp các bản pending dưới account lock, bản có login trùng hệt một bản pending khác thì bị bỏ khi account vượt giới hạn, bản mới nhất của mỗi nhóm trùng được giữ; bản không chứng minh được là dư thừa hay lỗi thời thì không bao giờ bị bỏ để nhường chỗ, nên account có thể vượt giới hạn và check doctor báo; bản do probe ghi dở được giữ ở `torn/` cho việc khôi phục thủ công, không bao giờ tự áp hay tự bỏ, và doctor báo ở mọi tuổi; `torn/` chỉ áp cho bản scratch của probe, còn scratch do runner đã chết để lại và pane home có store bị cắt vẫn bị xoá khi JSON không đọc được; bản không parse được thì so theo byte của file store và của write-ahead log hoặc rollback journal không rỗng (file không đọc được, trừ khi không tồn tại, không bao giờ bị coi là không có; index `-shm` không tính); home có file store trùng từng byte với nguồn và không bên nào có write-ahead log hay journal không rỗng thì không renew gì nên không được dàn) và báo `staged`/`apply-deferred`; chỉ xoá khi nguồn đọc được và chứng minh bản chép không mới hơn, hoặc bản chép được chứng minh hỏng (JSON hỏng, hay không có entry dùng được). Lỗi đọc file của hệ điều hành (quyền, I/O; mã `unreadable-file`) có thể qua nên bản chép được giữ; chỉ file kho không tồn tại (`missing-file`) mới được coi là rỗng và bị xoá. Nếu việc dàn thất bại, private home và marker được giữ lại (việc xoá báo lỗi, một dòng stderr mã cố định) để lần xoá sau, kể cả của reaper, thử lại; mỗi lần thất bại được đếm trong marker (`credentialKept`; hai lần cách nhau dưới 15 phút chỉ tính một, để lỗi tạm thời không dùng hết hạn mức), marker được ghi qua file tạm rồi rename và marker có mặt nhưng đọc không được thì việc xoá dừng lại. Sau 5 lần home bị giữ hẳn: không thử xoá nữa, không bao giờ bị xoá vì quá tuổi. Home bị giữ được kiểm lại dưới account lock khi account đó được gia hạn lần kế tiếp và bởi `fgos doctor --fix` (tập temp root tìm kiếm giống của doctor: root mặc định cộng `tempRoot` của từng backend đã đăng ký, lấy qua hook do phía dispatch truyền xuống; home nằm dưới `privateHomeRoot` riêng của backend không thuộc tập này nên không check, repair, reaper hay lần gia hạn nào thấy, và cũng không bao giờ bị xoá), và chỉ với home thuộc đúng runtime dir của lock đang giữ: chỉ xoá khi nguồn đọc được và chứng minh login trong home không mới hơn, hoặc login đó đã dàn được cạnh nguồn (và được áp); không thì vẫn giữ. Bản đã dàn và thư mục `pending/` được đồng bộ xuống đĩa trước khi home bị xoá. File marker không nhận ra được là marker nào cả (không phải JSON, không phải object, hay không có tên contract) thì mọi việc xoá home đó dừng lại. Finalizer so digest của marker không tính `credentialKept` (cleanup của driver thêm trường này sau khi digest được lấy) và không dừng ở home đó mà vẫn xoá các resource còn lại của dispatch (dispatch ghi là `retained`, kèm lý do của home). Check `credential-copies-retained` của `fgos doctor` báo theo provider/account: home bị giữ hẳn (fail, nêu thư mục home), home đang thử lại và các bản `pending/`/scratch quá một ngày (cảnh báo); chỉ có số đếm và tuổi, không bao giờ in giá trị, và check không xoá gì. Provisioning Codex đóng kín (fail closed): `auth.json` là symlink trỏ ra ngoài home, hoặc `home` tương đối, làm dispatch thất bại trước khi worker chạy (trước đây symlink được theo, home tương đối được hiểu theo cwd). Đường xoá home gọi module gia hạn credential (`provider-credential-renewal.mjs`) và qua đó phụ thuộc vào provider capacity, chỉ để lấy account lock. **Quyết định (2026-10-13):** invocation `codex-herdr-fgovn` (từ 2026-10-19 là `codex-herdr`) truyền thêm `--no-daemon` cạnh `-s danger-full-access -a never`. bwrap là confinement; sandbox riêng của Codex phải tắt trong suốt phiên, không chỉ ở lượt đầu.

**Vì sao:** mặc định TUI của Codex (từ 0.160) không tự chạy phiên mà giao cho một app-server daemon dùng chung (`codex app-server --listen unix:// --managed-daemon`), cài vào `<CODEX_HOME>/packages/app-server-daemon/releases/<version>/` lúc khởi động, kèm một daemon-updater tự thay bản mới hơn. Cờ `-s` của TUI chỉ áp cho thread nó mở; một thread mà daemon mở lại sau khi bị thay thì chạy theo mặc định của config, mà với workspace đã được gieo trust thì đó là sandbox `workspace-write` của chính Codex. Sandbox đó dựng bwrap riêng, coi cwd là writable root và mkdir các mount che (`.codex`, `.aws`, ...) bên trong cwd; dưới `--ro-bind / /` của fgOS lệnh mkdir thất bại nên mọi lệnh hỏng trước khi chạy: `bwrap: Can't mkdir <cwd>/.aws: Read-only file system`. Với `--no-daemon` phiên chạy trong chính tiến trình TUI, mang `-s danger-full-access` đến hết, không có daemon/updater nào chạy ra từ private home.

**Bằng chứng:** sự cố thật ở run `unit-run-1791874482416-acccbfe0/panelist-2/1` (pane chạy codex 0.160.1, lệnh đầu chạy được, sau một lần turn bị ngắt thì daemon 0.162.1 xuất hiện trong private home và mọi lệnh hỏng với lỗi trên). Tái hiện cơ chế: dưới đúng mount fgOS dựng (`--ro-bind / /`, `--tmpfs /tmp`, private home và outbox writable), `codex sandbox -c sandbox_mode="workspace-write" -- <ghi outbox>` với cwd là checkout chính báo đúng `bwrap: Can't mkdir /home/vantt/projects/forgentX/.aws: Read-only file system` (worktree không có `.codex` thì báo `.codex`), còn `danger-full-access` ghi được outbox; `read-only` hỏng vì cách khác (`execvp codex-linux-sandbox`). Dispatch pane thật có `--no-daemon`: private home không có `app-server-daemon/` hay `packages/`, run settle, outbox có `report-1.md` và `result-1.json`.

**Chưa chứng minh:** sự kiện nào khiến thread trong sự cố chạy lại dưới `workspace-write` (giả thuyết mạnh nhất: daemon-updater thay 0.160.1 bằng 0.162.1 giữa run, chính việc thay thế làm ngắt turn, và thread được mở lại không mang `-s`). Tắt daemon loại bỏ cả nhánh này; ghi `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` vào `config.toml` của private home là lớp phòng thủ thứ hai chưa làm (file đó do bước gieo trust ghi, và driver bwrap không được rẽ nhánh theo provider). - `npm install -g github:vantt/forgent` (run anywhere) → resolves and installs

  channel it refuses (`git-addon-unavailable: addon not shipped on this
  channel: onboard this project with fgctl init`) and changes nothing: this
  channel ships no native Git addon and Git has one door, so a project is
  onboarded with `fgctl init`, whose activated release carries the addon. The
  init/doctrine/marker-detection behavior itself (owned by the coexistence
  area, see `docs/coexistence.md`) runs from that activated release.

  shell profile → makes `fgos` and `fgos-runner` available directly from any
  location inside a checkout of the forgent source repository itself
  (including a linked git worktree of it), with no separate install step.

  wires the shell helper's source line into every shell profile the caller
  actually has, and brings the local config file up to date with the current
  defaults. New workspace onboarding should use `fgctl init` (which
  downloads the latest release when `.fgos/distribution.json` is absent, RUL15 (fgctl init downloads a checksum-verified release when no source is given))
  plus local `fgos doctor --fix` and `fgos doctor`; `doctor --fix` runs only registered fixes, so the
  config defaults, hook wiring and Claude Code hook still come from one `fgos
  setup` in the project. Shell/global integration remains legacy setup
  compatibility until the compatibility-window decision retires it.
- `fgos doctor` (run anywhere) → reports whether the environment is set up

|---|-------|---------|--------|----------|---------|
| 1 | Package name | The npm package identity used for the git-based install command | `forgent` | yes | — |
| 2 | Package version | A semantic version string tooling (e.g. packaging commands) needs to treat the package as valid | semver string | yes | `0.1.0` |
| 3 | Distribution file allowlist | The exact set of paths shipped to anyone installing the package — everything else in the source repo is excluded | `bin`, `src`, `scripts`, `core`, `domains`, `.agents`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`, the end-user documentation subset (`docs/how-to`, `docs/explanation`, and `docs/enduser-docs-index.json`), plus `packages/convention/contracts/convention.rules.v1.json`, which installed doctor needs to interpret per-rule cutoffs without duplicating native rule data, and `packages/seat-binding/contracts/seat-binding.tier-ladder.v1.json`, the tier names the runner config loader accepts, read from the same file the Seat Binding crate embeds | yes | — |
| 4 | CLI entry points | The commands exposed once installed | `fgos` → runs `bin/fgos.mjs`; `fgos-runner` → runs `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` (the autonomous-loop runner, see spec Runner) | yes | — |
| 4b | Claude Code plugin skill set | `plugins/fgOS/skills/` — the Claude Code plugin's own skill bundle, distributed via the Claude Code plugin marketplace mechanism (a separate distribution channel from the npm-installed `fgos`/`fgos-runner` CLI above). Ships two layers: hand-authored CLI-wrapper skills (`cook`, `discover`, `pick`, `submit`, ...) and mirrored `fgos-*` dev-skills plus `_shared/` for plugin-only consumers. Dev-skills are authored in `core/skills/` or `domains/*/skills/`; run `npm run build:skills` in the fgOS source repo to assemble `.agents/skills/`, generate `.claude/skills/` thin wrappers and references, and mirror dev-skills/shared fragments into the plugin. Plugin mirrors stay byte-identical to `.agents/skills/`, while Claude `SKILL.md` files are thin redirects with byte-identical frontmatter (`test/skills/fgos-mirror.test.mjs`). Assembled Markdown carries a generated-from source header. Do not hand-edit `.agents`, generated `.claude` files, or plugin mirrors; hand-authored CLI-wrapper skills remain sources. `plugin-dev-skills-packaged` (doctor check, row 7 below) detects missing or stale plugin mirrors | mirrored dev-skills + shared fragments + hand-authored CLI-wrapper skills | yes (the mirrors let plugin-only consumers dispatch dev-skills without a source checkout) | — |
| 5 | Dev checkout shell helper | An opt-in file, sourced from a contributor's own shell profile, exposing the same two CLI entry points from inside a checkout of the source repository — no install, no package fetch | one file, both commands | no (contributor's own choice) | not sourced automatically anywhere |
| 5b | Global config file | `~/.fgos/config.json` — same schema as the project-local shared config file, initialized/kept current by `fgos setup` (tsk-1ri) the same way it already handles the project-local file; project always wins any key present in both (`mergeWithGlobalConfig`, `src/config/global-config.mjs`) | one file, home-dir-relative | no (optional; a missing file is not an error, resolves to `{}`) | not created by anything except `fgos setup` |
| 5c | Machine backend registry file | `~/.fgos/confinement-backends.json` (overridable via `FGOS_CONFINEMENT_BACKEND_REGISTRY_PATH`) — machine-local backend registry declaring confinement backends (e.g. `bwrap`, container) available on the host (`confinement-backend-registry.v1`); managed by `fgos doctor --fix` (not project-over-global merge), trust store for security isolation drivers | one file, machine-local path | no (optional; bootstrap creates default bwrap backend on demand) | `~/.fgos/confinement-backends.json` |
| 5d | Provider-capacity runtime state | `~/.fgos/runtime/provider-capacity/state.json` — machine-local selected-account lease/quarantine state for provider-capacity rotation. Intentionally host-global only (never project-overridden) so multiple projects sharing provider accounts coordinate concurrency and rate limits safely without starvation. It is never packaged, never committed, and never repaired by `doctor`; `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` and the `provider-capacity-state` doctor check report it, while manual clear goes through `fgos dispatch reconcile provider-capacity clear-quarantine ...`. An account locked for a dead login is also unlocked by one real call when a dispatch would otherwise find no usable account (the lazy-probe unlock rule, now in `docs/specs/runner.md`). Its locks are holder-lock kernel locks under the machine lock root (row 5g): `provider-state` guards this file, and `provider-account/<provider>/<account>` guards one account while a renewal or unlock probe runs through it, held until that call and every process it started have exited. The same directory holds `account-locks/<provider>/<account>/`: copies of a login renewed elsewhere and waiting to be applied, a scratch home while a renewal runs, and the renewal failure cooldown; it is created only when a renewal or write-back runs and holds no credential outside those copies. | one runtime directory, home-dir-relative | no (created only when a provider account lease/quarantine/write occurs) | absent/inactive |
| 5e | Confinement attestation store state | `~/.local/state/fgos/attestations/` (or `$XDG_STATE_HOME/fgos/attestations`, overridable via `FGOS_CONFINEMENT_ATTESTATION_STORE_PATH`) — host-global security attestation records. Intentionally host-global only (outside all agent write grants) so confined agents can never tamper with their own audit trails, preserving immutable attestation integrity across projects. | one directory, machine-local path | no (created on first confined dispatch attestation) | absent/inactive |
| 5f | Workspace customization folder | `fgos/` at the project root: tracked in the project's own git, written once as a skeleton at onboarding and never edited by fgOS afterwards. Holds the customer's own agent definitions (`fgos/agents/<name>.yaml`), which win over a definition of the same name in the installed set (RUL13 (customer customization lives in one tracked workspace folder)). Read by `--seats @name` (runner decision 0057); the `fgctl init` skeleton is not built yet | directory | no | absent — the installed set alone applies |
| 5g | Lock directories | `<lockRoot>` = `<stateRoot>/locks` (machine-scope lock files: `full-suite`, `provider-account/<provider>/<account>`, `provider-state`, `install`) and `<fgosDir>/locks` (repo-scope lock files: `gateway`, `runner`, `sessions`, `reconcile`, `main-checkout`, `worktree-admin`, `merge-slot--<encodeURIComponent(ref)>` per target ref, `state.hot` and `state.reclaim.lock`, `porting-events.hot` and `porting-events.reclaim.lock` (the state store's hot mutex: the `.hot` record is not a kernel lock file, only the `.reclaim.lock` file is), `activation`, `observe`, and `dispatch-cwd--<dev>-<ino>` keyed by the dispatch directory's identity after realpath; the run locks live in their run: `<workflowRunDir>/locks/advance.lock`, `<runDir>/locks/recovery.lock`), both created by `fgos setup` (the machine root with mode 0700); `stateRoot` is the single resolution of `docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md` §11 (`FGOS_STATE_ROOT` pinned by the host, else `FGOS_STATE_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME/fgos`, `HOME/.local/state/fgos`). There is no lock config key: the wait for the processes of a dead previous holder to exit after they are terminated is fixed at 2000 ms. Lock files are never packaged, committed or repaired; `lock-kernel-semantics`, `lock-borrow-vectors` and `lock-holders` report them (row 7) | two directories | no (created by setup) | none |
| 5h | Terminal-control directory and the `terminal` config key | `<stateRoot>/terminal` (one subdirectory per driver; allocation records and their markers, a cache of what the port opened: deleting it never closes a pane because nobody closes a pane that has no record), created with mode 0700, together with every directory under it, by the allocation store on first use (there is no setup fix for it). One config key, `terminal` (`registerConfigDefault({id: 'terminal', key: 'terminal', shape: {allocationGraceMs: 60000, retainFailedPaneMs: null, layout: {policy: 'measured-split', minCols: 80, minRows: 20, maxPanesPerTab: 8}}})`); `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md` §9 gives each number's source. Project over global over default; the merge adds a missing key only. No new environment variable (`FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` stays, as the input of `attach`). Checked 2026-10-18: the release active in the forgentX, mdview and mcp-skill-hub workspaces (one digest) accepts a `terminal` section in the global and in the project config, so the key is written like `lock`; had it refused unknown keys, setup would have written it to the project config only until all three workspaces ran the new release. | `<stateRoot>/terminal` present / absent; config key present / absent | yes (computed, not stored) | — |
| 6 | Config staleness | Whether a config file (project-local or global — same computation, tsk-1ri) already has every setting the current default schema defines | up to date / missing one or more default settings | yes (computed, not stored) | — |
| 7 | Doctor check | One named diagnostic `fgos doctor` reports on | not a fixed list — an extensible registry (`src/setup/registrations.mjs`'s `registerCheck`); a check registration and a config-default registration are independent, never a forced pairing — a module may register only a check, only a config-default, or both. Today's registered checks: `convention-conformance`, `identity-project-id` (this repository carries one project id in the tracked file `.fgos/project.json`, asked through `fgos identity project --json`; absent only warns and there is no fix, because a fix on every machine would mint one id per clone: `fgos identity project --init` runs once on one machine, the file is committed and the others pull it; an unreadable or invalid file fails), `node-version-and-git`, `cli-version-visible` (tsk-2ej), `shell-integration-sourced`, `project-fgos-launcher` (a release install has one fgos launcher on PATH that runs each project's own activated fgos, see RUL17 (one fgos on PATH runs each project's own activated fgos)), `config-not-stale`, `main-checkout-hook-wired`, `tool-registry-configured`, `work-classification-vocabulary`, `work-step-vocabulary` (tsk-64h), `domain-workflow-operations-coverage`, `root-drift`, `delivered-not-on-trunk` (tsk-1l9), `config-awareness`, `provider-capacity-state` (reports account lease/quarantine state and never auto-clears), `credential-copies-retained` (login copies still pending for a renewal after a day, and private homes held after repeated staging failures, counted by provider/account and age; read-only, a held home fails, copies waiting for a renewal only warn, and, when the machine-global provider inventory was read, copies of any age in a store directory the account's login store layout no longer reads fail, naming the directory for hand recovery (when the global config cannot be read or is refused by the validator the check fails, says the layout was not checked with the reason, lists copies at any age and promises nothing about a dispatch); interrupted stagings (pending/.tmp-*) are reported too once their writer is gone and they have sat for ten minutes, and the over-limit line names the store; kept homes under a registered backend's temp and private-home roots are scanned, which the orphan reaper check does not do, and one there counts as held at once because nothing retries it; the check itself never deletes and never prints a value), `lock-kernel-semantics` (for the workspace lock directory and the machine lock root: the holder-lock driver's guarantee through the in-process door, then a two-process probe on that same mount, a description locked here and handed to a child must read held while the child lives and free once it died; prints driver, exclusion, borrow and holders levels, then the state root with its source and the fixed 2000 ms kill wait; kernel with a green probe passes, a missing directory warns until setup creates it, a guarantee of unsupported (a platform with no driver), a network filesystem none, an unresolved state root and an unreachable door fail by name; - **Blocked when:** the installer's machine cannot reach GitHub over the
  network, or does not have Node.js 18+ available.
- **What changes:** the installer's package manager (npm, pnpm, or yarn)
  resolves the forgent GitHub repository, packages it according to the
  distribution file allowlist, and installs both CLI entry points — `fgos`
  and `fgos-runner` — into the caller's chosen install location (global or
  project-local, per the installer's own install flags), both immediately
  executable. The install resolves against whatever ref the installer's own
  command names: a tagged release commit when the command names a tag
  (`README.md`'s recommended path,
  `docs/knowledge/how-to-cut-a-fgos-release-tag/cut-a-fgos-release-tag.md`),
  or the source repository's default branch when it doesn't (the
  bleeding-edge path README also documents) — preparing release metadata is
  scripted by `npm run release:prepare -- <tag>`, but tag-cutting itself stays
  a manual, repo-owner-judgment act (per tsk-jtb). Pushing a `v*` tag then
  triggers the release workflow that builds assets, verifies the external
  consumer path, and publishes the GitHub Release. The
  install runs
  no lifecycle script of its own — there is nothing for a package manager's
  build-script policy (e.g. pnpm's `allowBuilds`) to approve or block, so the
  install succeeds the same way regardless of which of the three package
  managers runs it (per str88-fgos-pnpm-lifecycle).
- **Side effects:** none beyond the local install; no registry account is
  created or touched, and nothing is published to the public npm registry.
- **Afterwards:** the installer has a working `fgos` command. The content
  they received is limited to the distribution file allowlist — the source
  repository's own internal data (its live event log, its own dogfood
  runner configuration, its test suite) is never part of what they receive.
  The installer also receives the end-user documentation subset (how-to
  guides, design-rationale docs, and the read-by-tag index) — every link the
  README's Documentation section points to resolves to a file that is
  actually present in what they installed; contributor/maintainer-only docs
  (decision records, area specs, the product backlog, platform foundations)
  are not part of the install and are not linked from that section — a
  reader who wants those clones the source repository instead."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-6","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-6","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-6","title":"Unheaded block 6","startLine":93,"endLine":127,"textDigest":"ddee3916eeb71a2e1df124e5b3b2737128f48fa21494c2720fd4284db23a9941","sample":"- **Blocked when:** the installer's machine cannot reach GitHub over the

- **Blocked when:** the current location is not inside any git repository —
  sourcing the helper file still succeeds (it only defines functions), but
  calling `fgos` or `fgos-runner` then fails immediately with a clear error
  and a non-zero exit, before anything is invoked.
- **What changes:** once sourced, `fgos` and `fgos-runner` become available
  as ordinary shell commands. Each resolves the checkout's own root the
  moment it is called — using the current location, not where the file was
  sourced from — then runs that checkout's `fgos`/`fgos-runner` entry point
  with whatever arguments were passed.
- **Side effects:** none — nothing is installed, no file outside the current
  shell session is touched, and no other install mechanism (npm or
  otherwise) is affected.
- **Afterwards:** a contributor working anywhere inside a checkout of this
  repository — the main checkout or a linked git worktree of it — has both
  commands available without a separate install, and without needing to

- **RUL1 (distributed package never includes the source repo's own runtime data).** The distributed package never includes the source repository's own
  runtime data directory or its own dogfood runner configuration — install
  content is always limited to the distribution file allowlist.
- **RUL2 (distribution is a GitHub install, not an npm registry publish).** Distribution happens by installing directly from the GitHub
  repository, not by publishing to the public npm registry — no package
  rename and no registry publish credentials are involved.
- **RUL3 (install never changes init/doctrine/marker-detection behavior).** Installing fgos does not change init/doctrine/marker-detection
  behavior in any way — that behavior belongs entirely to the coexistence
  area and is unchanged by installation.
- **RUL4 (every README Documentation link resolves to a shipped file).** Every link in the README's Documentation section resolves to a
  file that is actually present in the distribution file allowlist — a link
  to content that isn't shipped is a defect, not an acceptable pointer to
  "clone the repo for more" (per str77-79-doc-gap-fixes / ea8b9a8d).
  Contributor/maintainer-only documentation (decision records, area specs,
  the product backlog, platform foundations) is intentionally excluded from
  both the allowlist and that section — it is out of scope for an installed
  end user, not an oversight.
- **RUL5 (dev checkout shell helper is never sourced automatically).** The dev checkout shell helper file is never sourced automatically
  by any install step or other mechanism in this repository — a contributor
  adding it to their own shell profile is always their own explicit,
  separate action.
- **RUL6 (install never runs a lifecycle script).** Installing (from any of npm, pnpm, or yarn) never runs a lifecycle
  script of its own — the contributor hooks setup is always a separate,
  manually-invoked command, never an automatic `prepare`/`postinstall` step
  (per str88-fgos-pnpm-lifecycle). This is what lets every package
  manager's own build-script approval policy stay out of the way entirely,
  rather than needing to be satisfied.
- **RUL7 (setup/doctor cover both bash and zsh).** `fgos setup` and `fgos doctor` both cover bash and zsh — neither
  shell is treated as a lesser case.
- **RUL8 (setup's config update never overwrites a customized setting).** `fgos setup`'s config update never overwrites a setting the
  caller already customized, at any nesting depth; array-valued settings
  are never partially merged, only added wholesale when entirely missing.
- **RUL9 (doctor's default path never writes anything).** `fgos doctor`'s default (no `--fix`) path never writes
  anything, under any circumstance, including when a check would
  otherwise need to create a file to check it — a missing config file is
  reported as missing, never created as a side effect of checking.
  `--fix` is the deliberate exception: it runs every registered fix
  (Data Dictionary #7b) before re-reporting checks — reversed from the
  original no-exceptions wording per `tsk-2qz`, which reverses this
  rule and RUL11 (doctor --fix exists and is real, runs every registered fix) together (`docs/history/doctor-fix-gate-bypass/
  CONTEXT.md`).
- **RUL10 (setup never asks for confirmation, acts then reports).** `fgos setup` never asks for confirmation before writing to a
  shell profile or the config file — it acts and then reports exactly what
  it changed. Every other verb, and both of these two without
  `--pretty`, still produce the same enveloped-JSON result shape as before
  this feature — `--pretty` only changes how that same result is displayed,
  never what it contains.
- **RUL11 (doctor --fix exists and is real, runs every registered fix).** `fgos doctor --fix` exists and is real: it runs every fix
  registered via `registerFix` (Data Dictionary #7b) against the current
  cwd before re-reporting checks, then returns the same checks shape as
  the no-flag path plus a `fixed` array. The fix list is a registry, not
  a fixed set — a module can register a new one the same way a check or
  config-default is registered, independent of either (per tsk-2cs). This
  supersedes the original v1 "does not exist yet, Deferred Idea" wording
  — `tsk-2qz` reverses that decision deliberately, per
  `docs/distribution-vision.md` §3's trụ cột 3.
- **RUL12 (setup also runs every registered fix, unconditionally).** Legacy `fgos setup` also runs every registered fix (the same
  `runFixes()` `doctor --fix` calls per RUL11 (doctor --fix exists and is real, runs every registered fix)), unconditionally and with no
  confirmation — consistent with RUL10 (setup never asks for confirmation, acts then reports)'s own act-then-report contract for
  this deprecated compatibility verb, not an exception to it. `setup`'s result gains a `fixed` array,
  the same per-entry `{id, changed, message}` shape RUL11 (doctor --fix exists and is real, runs every registered fix) already describes
  for `doctor --fix`'s own (per `tsk-5hi`,
  `docs/history/setup-runs-registered-fixes/CONTEXT.md`).

- **RUL13 (customer customization lives in one tracked workspace folder; fgOS reads it first and never writes it; specified 2026-10-07; the lookup, the same-tier rule and the doctor check are built (runner decision 0057), the `fgctl init` skeleton and README are not).** A customer project that wants its own agent definitions (persona, role, decision boundary) puts them in `fgos/agents/<name>.yaml` at its project root. It is not `.fgos/`: that folder is runner state, ignored by git (`/.fgos/*`), every merge that stages a change under it is refused (`fgos-write-rejected`), and a fresh worktree has it stripped (ADR0020 (the runner strips .fgos/ from every fresh worktree)). It is not `.agents/` either: that is generated skill output which `fgos setup` and `npm run build:skills` rewrite. The first scope is `agents/` only; `workflows/`, `task-specs/` and `skills/` follow the same layout when a customer needs them, not before.
  - Lookup, by name, first match wins: the workspace folder, then a domain or extension (`domains/<name>/agents/`), then the installed `core/agents`. A higher tier replaces the whole file of a lower one; fields are never merged. Two definitions of one name in the same tier are an error that `fgos doctor` reports, never a silent pick. This replaces the earlier rule that a name is unique across `core/agents` and every domain: a name is unique within a tier and a higher tier shadows a lower one.
  - fgOS creates the folder and a README once, at onboarding (`fgctl init`), and never edits it afterwards; an fgOS upgrade never touches it. The installed tier is located through the release manifest, never through the working directory or PATH.
  - Built: `src/runner/agent-definitions.mjs` is the one lookup (workspace, then `domains/*/agents/`, then `core/agents/`; a project without its own `domains/` or `core/agents/` folder reads the running package's). `fgos workflow start --seats "@name|..."` uses it and pins the text at start. The doctor check `agent-type-names-unique` now means unique within each tier, covers `fgos/agents`, and reports which definition each customization replaces. The unit-level and capability-level `persona:` names still read `core/agents` of the working project at dispatch.
  - A doctor check registers with the feature and reports each customization, which installed definition it shadows, whether it has the shape the loader needs, and a shadowed core name or an override that no longer fits the installed set after an upgrade.
  - Not customizable here: executor, model and provider policy (`config.json`) and the platform laws. An extension is treated as a domain until an extension loader exists.
  - No component-boundary change: it extends the three-tier discovery convention coordination protocols already use (project, `domains/<name>/`, packaged `core/`) to agent definitions.

- **RUL14 (the lazy-probe unlock rule: moved).** The rule that unlocks an account locked for a dead login with one real call now lives with the provider-capacity rules in `docs/specs/runner.md` (RUL74 (lazy-probe unlock: an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call that succeeds)), together with the refresh-ahead and write-back rules for a rotating login (RUL75 (a rotating provider login is renewed once at the source, in a copy fgOS holds, and a login renewed inside a private home is written back)). This document keeps only where the state lives (row 5d).
- **RUL15 (`fgctl init` needs no hand-downloaded tarball: it picks its release by a fixed precedence and downloads it checksum-verified; 2026-10-12).** The release `fgctl init` installs comes from the first of these that is set:
  1. `--from <path | URL>` on the command line;
  2. the `FGCTL_FROM=<path | URL>` environment variable (same meaning as the flag, for a non-release build: a `.tar.gz`, a release directory, or a URL);
  3. `FGCTL_VERSION=<tag>`, which downloads exactly that tag's asset (needed for a pre-release, which "latest" never selects);
  4. the release pinned by the project's committed `.fgos/distribution.json` (no network when that release is staged on the machine; otherwise see "The pin records the tag" below);
  5. otherwise the latest GitHub release, found by following `<repo>/releases/latest` to its tag.
  - An explicit source (1-3) beats a pin; the pin then only validates what was fetched (a different digest is refused as a pin mismatch, as for `--from` today). The inputs are read per invocation; nothing is remembered.

  - **Workspace launchers.** `fgctl init` and `fgctl repair` write four launchers into `.fgos/installation/bin/`: the `sh` pair `fgos`, `fgos-runner` (Linux, macOS, Git Bash) and the batch pair `fgos.cmd`, `fgos-runner.cmd` (PowerShell, `cmd.exe`; no `sh` involved). Each reads `activation.json`, refuses with exit 3 unless `status` is `ready`, and runs the active release's entry. A directory on `PATH` holding them makes `fgos` resolve in PowerShell through `PATHEXT`. The post-activation tail (`init`, `doctor --fix`, `doctor`) runs the `.cmd` form on a Windows host. `fgctl verify` checks that the launchers its host needs (the `sh` pair everywhere, the batch pair too on Windows) exist and equal what this `fgctl` writes; a missing or edited one is reported with `run fgctl repair` and never quarantines the (intact) release.
  - **Proof.** Pushing a release tag builds both targets and runs a consumer proof on each, and only when both pass does the publish job run; publishing exists only in `release.yml`. The Windows proof (`scripts/ci-external-consumer.ps1`, under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7) installs `fgctl` with `install.ps1`, runs `fgctl init` against a local release server, runs the activated `fgos` from PowerShell and from `cmd.exe`, and checks that a tampered download is refused by both the installer and `fgctl init`.

  - The fix writes one small launcher named `fgos` (`fgos.cmd` on Windows) into the directory `fgctl` was found in on `PATH`. The launcher walks up from the working directory to the nearest `.fgos/installation/bin/fgos` and runs it with the same arguments, so each project runs the release it activated, from any subdirectory, in any shell, interactive or not; it edits no rc file. Outside a project it exits 127 and says to run `fgctl init`.
  - The launcher carries a marker line. The check reports `ready`, an out-of-date copy (rewritten by the fix), a foreign `fgos` found first on `PATH` (never overwritten; the check names it), no `fgos` with `fgctl` on `PATH` (the fix writes it), or neither on `PATH` (the check says to add the directory `fgctl` was installed into).
  - A source checkout keeps the sourced shell-integration script and needs no launcher; the check passes there.
  - Proof: `test/setup/project-launcher.test.mjs` (two projects and a nested one each run their own fgos; the `cmd` launcher runs on Windows in the focused Windows job)."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-15","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-15","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-15","title":"Unheaded block 15","startLine":340,"endLine":343,"textDigest":"b9673a0dca105175779073677428da87748a2eb1ad3ff63119b2c0ff506c6976","sample":"- **RUL18 (`fgctl` activates a release only after the holder-lock semantics probe and the borrow vectors are green; 2026-10-16).** Right before `fgctl` publishes the activation fil","identityFingerprint":"ca80e52d8cdd977f3bfe2bc4adbcf4e4a810ccc2052e5dde6df5b1685cf21b1e","ancestry":["Spec: Distribution","Business Rules"],"text":"- **RUL18 (`fgctl` activates a release only after the holder-lock semantics probe and the borrow vectors are green; 2026-10-16).** Right before `fgctl` publishes the activation file, on every path that activates (`init`, `upgrade`, `repair`), it runs through the `fgos-holder-lock` crate it links itself, never anything under the candidate directory: the driver guarantee plus a two-process semantics probe (a child holds the lock exclusively, the parent must see it held; the child dies, the parent must see it free) for `<workspace>/.fgos/locks` and `<lockRoot>`, and the four borrow vectors with the sibling check. - **2026-10-23 — Terminal setup loses a row and a fix.** The doctor row `terminal-config` is part of `terminal-control`, and the `terminal-dir` fix is gone: the allocation store creates `<stateRoot>/terminal` and everything under it with mode 0700 itself, so a repair that only recreated what the owner of the directory already creates was a second door. Source: `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md` §15 and the T2 arbitration `plans/reports/council-261023-0402-harden-t2-arbitration.md`.
- **2026-10-23 — Every YAML parse goes through the native door (RUL108 (every YAML parse goes through the native door: one Rust parser behind src/util/yaml.mjs); supersedes RUL101 (fgOS has no npm runtime dependency; every YAML parse goes through one vendored js-yaml 5.4.3 behind src/util/yaml.mjs)).** Before this, a vendored, hash-pinned js-yaml 5.4.3 bundle was the Node parser because a bare checkout had no `npm install`, while the Rust side already read YAML through `fgos-yaml-doc`: two authorities for what YAML means. Decision: the one-door rule of RUL101 (every YAML parse goes through one vendored js-yaml) stays and the implementation behind the door becomes Rust, as the YAML Document spec (section 10) signed on 2026-10-22 says. `src/util/third-party/js-yaml.mjs` and its hash test are deleted in the same change; the upgrade-procedure paragraph of RUL101 (every YAML parse goes through one vendored js-yaml) no longer applies (the parser's own record is `packages/yaml-doc/upgrade-record.md`, RUL107 (a third-party crate under a component contract is pinned exactly with an upgrade record and acceptance tests)). Consequence, stated plainly: a process that cannot load the addon (a bare checkout without a staged addon, a channel that does not ship it) fails every YAML read with the door's named error; scripts that read YAML from a checkout stage the addon first (`ensureAddonForScript`), and a focused `node --test` needs the staged environment `npm test` builds. Evidence: the 136 golden cases of `packages/yaml-doc/contracts/fixtures/parse.v1.json` (every case of the old Node test lives there); a parity run of the old door against the new over 1414 tracked YAML and frontmatter documents found 1396 equal, 18 rejected by both, 0 different; `test/util/yaml.test.mjs` is the one Node wiring proof. Rejected: keeping js-yaml beside the crate (two authorities), a JSON projection plus a spawned process (owner 2026-10-22: 3 to 40 ms per call against 12 microseconds). Reversal condition: if the addon cannot be loaded on a channel the product must support, the fix is to ship the addon there, never a JavaScript parser.

- **2026-10-23 — Third-party crates under a component contract are pinned exactly, with an upgrade record and acceptance tests (RUL107 (a third-party crate that a component's contract rests on is pinned exactly and has an upgrade record and acceptance tests)).** Before this, the YAML parser had a record and the validator crate was about to be the second case; the convention was in neither spec. Decision: the rule above. Evidence: `jsonschema` =0.60.0 reproduced three defects under the product's serde_json feature set that the default-feature evaluation did not show (an `unreachable!` on an out-of-range number, quadratic `pattern` compile time, wrong object comparison under `preserve_order`), each now guarded and covered by a test that fails when upstream fixes it (`packages/config/upgrade-record.md`, `packages/config/rust/tests/validator_acceptance.rs`). Rejected: an unwritten convention (the next crate's author would not know the bar).

- **2026-10-21 — The npm channel's `fgos init` points to `fgctl init`.** Before this, a project onboarded with `npm install -g github:vantt/forgent` plus `fgos init`; that route needs Git through the native addon, which only an activated release ships ("until M10" in the old message). Git keeps one door, so the npm channel gets no addon-less Git read path: in a project no `fgctl init` has activated, `fgos init` refuses with `git-addon-unavailable: addon not shipped on this channel: onboard this project with fgctl init` and writes nothing. `test/setup/doctor-fresh-run.test.mjs` and `test/install-packaging.test.mjs` prove that refusal; the doctor state of an onboarded project is proven by the `fgctl init` tests (real runtime tail).

- **2026-10-18 — Terminal-control enters setup and doctor.** `fgos setup` adds the `terminal` config section and creates `<stateRoot>/terminal` (0700); `fgos doctor` replaces `herdr-available` with `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations`. Reasons: the herdr check now asks the port what the driver can do instead of running `herdr --version` on its own (one door); the new settings must be visible to doctor with their source or they are guesses (L5). Prior art read: the `herdr-available` check and `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` diagnosis are kept inside `terminal-control`; `lock` is the precedent for a top-level section registered by a component. Decisions: (1) a missing herdr is a warning, not a failure, because direct mode does not use a terminal; (2) the doctor floor of 40x8 for `minCols`/`minRows` is the measured one from the measurement report; (3) the setting names reach the route and the failed-pane retention through `src/terminal-control/config.mjs`, so a value doctor accepts is the value a round uses; explicit values only are sent, the Rust core keeps its defaults.

- **2026-10-16 — The activation, install and observe locks join holder-lock.** `fgctl`'s activation lock, the machine install lock and the observe store lock become kernel locks at `<fgosDir>/locks/activation.lock`, `<stateRoot>/locks/install.lock` and `<fgosDir>/locks/observe.lock`; the observe lock waits 5 s with no TTL and writes the shard snapshot under the lock. Their legacy paths (`.fgos/installation/activation.lock`, `<stateRoot>/install.lock`, `.fgos/observe/.lock`) become tombstone directories. Windows `fgctl init|upgrade|repair` refused with `lock-driver-unavailable` until the Windows driver landed (2026-10-17, `docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md` §8.1). (The `lock-fences` check and fix that covered these rows were removed on 2026-10-22.) Details: RUL18 (startup reap only takes claims the runner itself made, never a human or session holder) above and `docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md` §15.

- **2026-10-16 — Holder-lock enters setup, doctor and the activation gate (RUL18 (`fgctl` activates a release only after the holder-lock semantics probe and the borrow vectors are green)).** The cold locks of the runner (gateway, runner, sessions, advance, reconcile, recovery, full-suite, provider account and state, dispatch cwd) move from pid/TTL files to kernel locks on open file descriptions (`docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md`). Owner decisions of 2026-10-16: a stop-everything cutover with fences instead of a two-protocol transition, so no marker and no protocol floor in the manifest; Windows reports `unsupported` for these locks rather than falling back to the old files; macOS runs the `flock` driver at once, gated at activation by the vectors and the probe. In this spec: six doctor checks (`lock-kernel-semantics`, `lock-borrow-vectors`, `lock-holders`, `lock-fences`, `lock-predecessor-kill-wait`, `state-root`; three remain since 2026-10-22) and the `lock-fences` fix replace `provider-capacity-lock-stale`, whose ledger is no longer a mutex; `fgos setup` creates `<lockRoot>` and `<fgosDir>/locks` and registered the config key `lock.predecessorKillWaitMs` (removed on 2026-10-22; the wait is fixed at 2000 ms). Plan: `plans/261016-1104-holder-lock-kernel-lock-foundation/plan.md`.

- **2026-10-12 — `fgctl init` downloads by default (RUL15 (fgctl init downloads a checksum-verified release when no source is given)).** Before this, a plain `fgctl init` in a project with no pin failed with "`--from <source>` is required", so a first install meant downloading the release tarball by hand. Owner decision: no source and no pin means the latest GitHub release; `FGCTL_VERSION` selects an exact tag; `FGCTL_FROM` and `--from` select a non-release build; checksum verification is mandatory; the transport is the system `curl` rather than a new HTTP crate (same behavior and override as `install.sh`, no TLS stack to carry in `fgctl`). Prior art: `fgctl init --from` (the release-asset door, kept unchanged and now equivalent to `FGCTL_FROM`), `install.sh`'s `FGCTL_VERSION`/`FGCTL_ASSET_BASE_URL`/`FGCTL_TARGET` (reused, not redefined). Same day, follow-up: the pin now records the tag, so a pinned workspace whose release is not staged on this machine downloads it instead of needing a source; only a digest-only legacy pin still needs `FGCTL_FROM`/`FGCTL_VERSION`/`--from`, because a digest names no download. Follow-up (2026-10-14): `fgctl upgrade` uses the same verified download pipeline (`--from` > `FGCTL_FROM` > `FGCTL_VERSION` > latest GitHub release) and records the downloaded tag in `.fgos/distribution.json`, so an upgraded project's pin keeps a downloadable `releaseVersion` for teammates instead of reverting to digest-only.
- **2026-10-13 — Windows is a native release target (RUL16 (Windows is a native release target: same assets, an installer and launchers that need no POSIX shell)).** Owner decision: the level is "native, complete" (PowerShell and `cmd.exe`, no Git Bash, no WSL), with `tar.gz` kept as the single archive format and macOS left out of scope. Prior art, reused: the Windows CI hardening track made the Rust workspace build and the release-tree staging work on Windows (the `fgos.exe` entry, colon-free release store directory names, drive-letter-safe archive validation), and an earlier change wrote `.cmd` launchers on Windows that ran the `sh` shims through a `sh` on `PATH`; that required Git for Windows, so it is replaced by launchers that read `activation.json` themselves. Missing before: a Windows release asset, `install.ps1`, a Windows consumer proof, and any check that the launchers exist. Also in this change: the Linux asset moves from `ubuntu-latest` (binaries then needed glibc 2.39 and printed a loader warning on Ubuntu 22.04, glibc 2.35) to `ubuntu-22.04`, with a CI gate on the glibc symbol versions.
- **2026-10-16 — fgOS has no npm runtime dependency; YAML is read through one vendored parser (RUL101 (fgOS has no npm runtime dependency; every YAML parse goes through one vendored js-yaml 5.4.3 behind src/util/yaml.mjs)).** **Superseded on 2026-10-23 by RUL108 (every YAML parse goes through the native door): the one-door rule stays, the parser behind the door is now the Rust crate, the vendored file, its hash test and the upgrade procedure below are gone; the text below is kept as history.** Before this, `yaml` was the one production dependency. An installed release carried it (the release builder stages declared production dependencies), but a checkout, linked worktree or unpacked copy without `npm install` did not, so every module importing it failed to load there, and the doctor and setup paths grew their own YAML readers and "not evaluated" branches to keep loading. Decision: `package.json#dependencies` stays empty; the only YAML parser is `src/util/third-party/js-yaml.mjs`, the ESM bundle from the js-yaml 5.4.3 tarball, unmodified except a header and the dropped source-map comment line, and every parse goes through `src/util/yaml.mjs` (`parseYaml(text, { filename })`: zero documents give `null`, more than one throws, `maxAliases` 100, js-yaml's default core schema). An architecture test fails on any other import of `yaml`, `js-yaml` or the third-party file. Rejected: keeping `yaml` and making doctor tolerate its absence (what the workarounds did, and the cause of the divergence); a hand-rolled parser (a second authority for what YAML means); `vendor/` or `dist/` as the location (the repository's scout-block hook refuses those path segments, so agents could not read or review the file); 5.4.2 (a block-indentation mis-parse fixed in 5.4.3) and 5.5.0 (one day old at the time). Readers that used to skip silently now report a parse failure as a named problem with file, line and column; pinned persona text that the strict parser rejects renders through a private legacy projection so older runs resume with the same text (its removal is tracked in the backlog). Evidence: commits `8ef1baf1c` (door and vendored file), `838b044e5` (call sites), `b75c01a3f` (release and dev-host staging), `6013ca389` (dependency dropped), `f96eece77`, `b7eeb4bb6` and `26b3338a7` (readers use the parser), `f705b9c8c` (doctor checks `compiled.json`); a parity run of the old parser against the door over every tracked YAML and frontmatter document found 828 documents, 0 differences, 13 rejected by both; a cold `fgos` start costs 2 to 3 ms more (97 to 99 ms for `version`, 109 to 110 ms for `dispatch decide`); the full suite ran 7850 tests with 0 failures with release binaries present; `test/util/yaml.test.mjs` pins the vendored bytes by hash. Kept on their own paths: `src/report/frontmatter.mjs` pairs `parseFrontmatter` with `renderFrontmatter` over a deliberately flat schema, so replacing only the parser would make the pair asymmetric; `distill.mjs` carries a minimal YAML reader because portable skills ship without `src/`; `domains/*/compiled.json` stays a generated projection because parsing domain YAML at import would put every verb, hook and `doctor` at the mercy of one YAML typo (doctor now checks its freshness instead). Upgrade procedure: in an empty scratch directory run `npm pack js-yaml@<version> --ignore-scripts`; compare the tarball's sha512 with `npm view js-yaml@<version> dist.integrity`; extract the `.mjs` bundle from the tarball without executing anything in it (build the path so the hook-refused segment does not appear in the command); confirm it has no import or require; diff it against the current bundle and read every changed line; re-run the parity comparison against the previous parser over the tracked YAML; replace the third-party file with the new bundle under a fresh header (source, version, integrity, license, hash); update the hash constant in `test/util/yaml.test.mjs`. js-yaml advisories are watched through the backlog, since `npm audit` no longer covers the file.
- **2026-10-17 — Instruction composition belongs to the Agent Context Engine; packaging-distribution delivers (RUL102 (one owner for composing agent instructions: the Agent Context Engine composes and selects rules, packaging-distribution only discovers, installs, renders per host and repairs)).** Before this, two documents gave the same authority to two components: `docs/platform/packaging-distribution/contracts/instruction-composition-and-projection.md` §2 named packaging-distribution owner of the composition engine and registry shape, while `docs/platform/proposals/documentation-system-unification.md` §4.7.2-4.7.3 put the Instruction Composer in the Agent Context Engine and said packaging-distribution "does not decide semantic composition". Left as is, a future Agent Context Engine would be built beside `src/setup/instruction-composition.mjs`, giving two composers and two orderings of the same rules. Owner decision: composing and selecting rules (kind order, override, conflict, per-task selection, per-host budget, progressive disclosure) has one owner, the Agent Context Engine; packaging-distribution keeps delivery (source discovery and install, per-host render adapters, projection ledger, doctor repair). Two delivery moments follow: static delivery, where packaging-distribution asks the engine for each host's effective set when sources change or at setup/install/upgrade and renders it to files; and per-task delivery, where the runner asks the engine for a context packet that goes into the worker brief, with no file written. The engine knows no host or file. Rejected: packaging-distribution keeping composition and also absorbing budgets and per-task selection (it would grow a content-deciding role inside an install/delivery component). Weight guard: no new component now; the existing code in `src/setup/instruction-registry.mjs` and `src/setup/instruction-composition.mjs` is the engine's seed and moves to its own module only when the first budget/tiering slice lands, in the same change, never kept in two places. - **2026-10-16 — fgOS has no npm runtime dependency; YAML is read through one vendored parser (RUL101 (fgOS has no npm runtime dependency; every YAML parse goes through one vendored js-yaml 5.4.3 behind src/util/yaml.mjs)).** **Superseded on 2026-10-23 by RUL108 (every YAML parse goes through the native door): the one-door rule stays, the parser behind the door is now the Rust crate, the vendored file, its hash test and the upgrade procedure below are gone; the text below is kept as history.** Before this, `yaml` was the one production dependency. An installed release carried it (the release builder stages declared production dependencies), but a checkout, linked worktree or unpacked copy without `npm install` did not, so every module importing it failed to load there, and the doctor and setup paths grew their own YAML readers and "not evaluated" branches to keep loading. Decision: `package.json#dependencies` stays empty; the only YAML parser is `src/util/third-party/js-yaml.mjs`, the ESM bundle from the js-yaml 5.4.3 tarball, unmodified except a header and the dropped source-map comment line, and every parse goes through `src/util/yaml.mjs` (`parseYaml(text, { filename })`: zero documents give `null`, more than one throws, `maxAliases` 100, js-yaml's default core schema). An architecture test fails on any other import of `yaml`, `js-yaml` or the third-party file. Rejected: keeping `yaml` and making doctor tolerate its absence (what the workarounds did, and the cause of the divergence); a hand-rolled parser (a second authority for what YAML means); `vendor/` or `dist/` as the location (the repository's scout-block hook refuses those path segments, so agents could not read or review the file); 5.4.2 (a block-indentation mis-parse fixed in 5.4.3) and 5.5.0 (one day old at the time). Readers that used to skip silently now report a parse failure as a named problem with file, line and column; pinned persona text that the strict parser rejects renders through a private legacy projection so older runs resume with the same text (its removal is tracked in the backlog). Evidence: commits `8ef1baf1c` (door and vendored file), `838b044e5` (call sites), `b75c01a3f` (release and dev-host staging), `6013ca389` (dependency dropped), `f96eece77`, `b7eeb4bb6` and `26b3338a7` (readers use the parser), `f705b9c8c` (doctor checks `compiled.json`); a parity run of the old parser against the door over every tracked YAML and frontmatter document found 828 documents, 0 differences, 13 rejected by both; a cold `fgos` start costs 2 to 3 ms more (97 to 99 ms for `version`, 109 to 110 ms for `dispatch decide`); the full suite ran 7850 tests with 0 failures with release binaries present; `test/util/yaml.test.mjs` pins the vendored bytes by hash. Kept on their own paths: `src/report/frontmatter.mjs` pairs `parseFrontmatter` with `renderFrontmatter` over a deliberately flat schema, so replacing only the parser would make the pair asymmetric; `distill.mjs` carries a minimal YAML reader because portable skills ship without `src/`; `domains/*/compiled.json` stays a generated projection because parsing domain YAML at import would put every verb, hook and `doctor` at the mercy of one YAML typo (doctor now checks its freshness instead). Upgrade procedure: in an empty scratch directory run `npm pack js-yaml@<version> --ignore-scripts`; compare the tarball's sha512 with `npm view js-yaml@<version> dist.integrity`; extract the `.mjs` bundle from the tarball without executing anything in it (build the path so the hook-refused segment does not appear in the command); confirm it has no import or require; diff it against the current bundle and read every changed line; re-run the parity comparison against the previous parser over the tracked YAML; replace the third-party file with the new bundle under a fresh header (source, version, integrity, license, hash); update the hash constant in `test/util/yaml.test.mjs`. js-yaml advisories are watched through the backlog, since `npm audit` no longer covers the file.
- **2026-10-17 — Instruction composition belongs to the Agent Context Engine; packaging-distribution delivers (RUL102 (one owner for composing agent instructions: the Agent Context Engine composes and selects rules, packaging-distribution only discovers, installs, renders per host and repairs)).** Before this, two documents gave the same authority to two components: `docs/platform/packaging-distribution/contracts/instruction-composition-and-projection.md` §2 named packaging-distribution owner of the composition engine and registry shape, while `docs/platform/proposals/documentation-system-unification.md` §4.7.2-4.7.3 put the Instruction Composer in the Agent Context Engine and said packaging-distribution "does not decide semantic composition". Left as is, a future Agent Context Engine would be built beside `src/setup/instruction-composition.mjs`, giving two composers and two orderings of the same rules. Owner decision: composing and selecting rules (kind order, override, conflict, per-task selection, per-host budget, progressive disclosure) has one owner, the Agent Context Engine; packaging-distribution keeps delivery (source discovery and install, per-host render adapters, projection ledger, doctor repair). Two delivery moments follow: static delivery, where packaging-distribution asks the engine for each host's effective set when sources change or at setup/install/upgrade and renders it to files; and per-task delivery, where the runner asks the engine for a context packet that goes into the worker brief, with no file written. The engine knows no host or file. Rejected: packaging-distribution keeping composition and also absorbing budgets and per-task selection (it would grow a content-deciding role inside an install/delivery component). Weight guard: no new component now; the existing code in `src/setup/instruction-registry.mjs` and `src/setup/instruction-composition.mjs` is the engine's seed and moves to its own module only when the first budget/tiering slice lands, in the same change, never kept in two places. - A package marked as not intended for public registry publication can still
  be installed directly from its GitHub repository — that restriction only
  blocks publishing to a public registry, not this installation path.
- Both CLI entry points (`fgos` and `fgos-runner`) are installed identically,
  executable immediately after install — a fresh install does not require
  the installer to separately locate or make executable the autonomous-loop
  runner command.
- Calling `fgos`/`fgos-runner` (via the dev checkout shell helper) from
  inside a linked git worktree of this repository always runs the MAIN
  checkout's entry point, never that worktree's own local copy — accepted
  as-is for this mechanism, not treated as a defect.
- A package manager whose own policy blocks lifecycle scripts for
  git-hosted dependencies (e.g. pnpm 10+'s `allowBuilds`) never blocks
  installing this package, because this package's install never declares a
  lifecycle script in the first place (per str88-fgos-pnpm-lifecycle) —
  there is nothing for that policy to approve or refuse.
- `fgos setup` run a second time with nothing new to do reports that
  plainly rather than silently repeating (or silently no-oping without
  saying so).
- `fgos doctor`'s `config-not-stale` check on a machine where `fgos setup`
  was never run reports "not configured yet", not an error and not a
  silently-created file.
- A release tree staged for `fgctl` (`scripts/build-rust-distribution.mjs`)
  carries the legacy-node payload TOGETHER WITH its production dependencies
  (the package's `dependencies` and theirs), copied next to the sources, so
  every verb runs from the installed release alone. Before this, the staged
  tree held no dependencies and any verb that loads one (`fgos workflow`,
  found when dogfooding a project that had run `fgctl init`) failed with a
  missing-package error while `fgos version` and `fgos doctor` still passed.
  A dependency that is not installed when the tree is built fails the build
  instead of thinning the payload; two installed copies of one name are
  refused. The external-consumer CI step runs a dependency-loading verb for
  this reason, because `version` never imports one.
- An agent in a project with no `bin/` (only the installed `fgos`) finds how
  to run anything from `fgos --help --json` and `fgos <verb> [<sub>] --help
  --json`. The host's route table carries two option selectors, `--help` and
  `-h`, generated from `HELP_SELECTORS` in `src/cli/command-registry.mjs`
  like every verb route and sent to the legacy-node payload, which owns the
  verb manifest; every other leading option still has no route and exits 4.

  sent to the payload too, so it prints its manifest entry instead of

The web dashboard is a browser surface for watching fgOS work and answering
the questions it raises, from a device that is not the developer's machine.

The need it exists for is concrete, and it is the reason the design looks the
way it does: the product owner wants to **review and approve from a phone**,
and at exactly that moment there is usually no cockpit terminal open
(rationale: `docs/history/herdr-web-dashboard/CONTEXT.md`'s own rationale section for the child-process decision — the dashboard runs as a child process that outlives the cockpit pane, precisely so it does not vanish when the terminal closes). A surface that
only lives as long as a terminal pane is absent precisely when it is needed.

Three things bound this surface:

- It runs **alongside** the herdr TUI, never replacing it (boundary: the web dashboard belongs to the fgos gateway, `apps/fgos-gateway/`; it runs alongside, not instead of, the `herdr-dashboard` TUI plugin). A
  person at a terminal keeps the TUI; the dashboard serves the person who is
  not at one.
- It is an **independent client project**, not server code inside the gateway
  (per fgos-interface-daemon — gateway and TUI sit behind hexagonal ports; the web client is a separate adapter calling in from outside). Its source lives at `apps/fgos-gateway/web/`; the fgos gateway embeds the built bundle and serves it, which is hosting, not ownership of any API logic. It calls the gateway's REST/RPC API from the outside,
  which is what decision `0014` requires of any non-terminal UI. An earlier
  decision of this feature (tsk-ldb's own — web dashboard as a new subsystem inside the former single herdr crate) proposed embedding an HTTP server
  directly in the former combined gateway-and-TUI binary (since split into `fgos-gateway` and `herdr-dashboard`); that branch is closed — cite fgos-interface-daemon's hexagonal-ports decision, not
  tsk-ldb's original one, for where the web client lives.
- It never becomes a second write path. Every change it makes goes through
  an fgOS one-door-write verb executed by the gateway (R2 below).

**Out of scope for this spec.** Question authoring quality at the source
(`tsk-539`, deliberately decoupled — tsk-ldb and tsk-539 stay scope-separated). Multi-project port/identity
mechanics (`tsk-3b0` — multi-project port/identity handling is deferred to tsk-3b0). The concrete visual layout, colour and
typography (`tsk-3x6`, `docs/reference/herdr-web-dashboard-layout.md`) — this
spec states what an actor expects to be able to do, never how it is drawn."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-2","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-2","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-2","title":"Unheaded block 2","startLine":13,"endLine":14,"textDigest":"f5637b304adfb2017df338ea99078d779a43a721765c812868be7dce2b0b55d3","sample":"The web dashboard is a browser surface for watching fgOS work and answering

- **Open the dashboard.** A person opens the dashboard's address in a browser
  on any device that can reach the machine. The first interaction is always
  sign-in; there is no anonymous view (mandatory token auth from v1, not deferred to a later version).
- **Open the taskboard.** The default landing surface once signed in: every
  work item on the connected project, grouped so the person can see state at a
  glance.
- **Open one task's detail.** From the taskboard, or directly by address.
- **Open "questions needing answer".** The list of everything currently
  waiting on a person — covering **both** channels, `ask` questions and
  `gate-approve` questions (question-needing-answer covers both channels), not just the `ask` channel.
- **Availability trigger (not a person's action).** The dashboard is reachable
  whenever its own process is running. That process is started and stopped
  from the cockpit but **outlives the cockpit pane** — closing the cockpit does
  not stop the dashboard (it runs as a child process outliving the cockpit pane). It is enabled by default (its own config toggle defaults ON, unlike other auto-launch toggles), listens on the
  configured bind address (default reaches beyond loopback — binds 0.0.0.0 by default, bind address configurable, warns when non-loopback) and on port
  8788 (its config section carries a port field, defaulting to 8788).
- **No outbound trigger exists.** Nothing notifies the person that a question
  is waiting; they have to come and look. A push/attention channel is a
  different, unbuilt capability (`docs/io-contract.md` §Ranh giới — STR48)."},{"unitKind":"unheaded-block","anchor":"unheaded-block-7","githubAnchor":"unheaded-block-7","stableAnchor":"unheaded-block-7","title":"Unheaded block 7","startLine":44,"endLine":62,"textDigest":"6fe8b44476ba00c6aa3e5c46960ec7e060c6186fffd0f444669a3bc8950cb176","sample":"- **Open the dashboard.** A person opens the dashboard's address in a browser
